description: Date after which the germination rate certification is no longer valid and retesting is required per USDA Federal Seed Act regulations. Drives lot status transitions to 'expired' and triggers procurement or retesting workflows.

reference: USDA Federal Seed Act (7 U.S.C. 1551-1611); AOSA (Association of Official Seed Analysts) Rules for Testing Seeds; AOSCA Seed Certification Standards

reference: USDA Federal Seed Act (7 U.S.C. 1551-1611); AOSA Rules for Testing Seeds; AOSCA Seed Certification Standards

description: Identifier or description of the GMO (Genetically Modified Organism) trait stack present in this seed lot (e.g., 'RR2Y/YGCB', 'Roundup Ready 2 Yield + YieldGard Corn Borer'). NULL if non-GMO. Required for USDA APHIS biotech regulatory compliance, COOL labeling, and customer GMO disclosure requirements.
reference: USDA APHIS Biotechnology Regulatory Services (BRS); USDA National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard (NBFDS); EPA Biopesticide Registration

description: Indicates whether this seed lot contains genetically modified organisms (GMO). True = GMO seed; False = non-GMO seed. Required for USDA National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard compliance, customer labeling, and export documentation.
reference: USDA National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard (NBFDS); USDA APHIS Biotechnology Regulatory Services; Codex Alimentarius

description: Indicates whether this seed lot is certified under the USDA National Organic Program (NOP). True = NOP-certified organic seed; False = conventional seed. Required for organic crop production compliance and NOP audit trails.
reference: USDA National Organic Program (NOP) 7 CFR Part 205; IFOAM Organic Standards

description: Externally-known alphanumeric lot number (LOT) assigned by the seed supplier or internal seed processing facility. Used for seed traceability from procurement through planting to harvest, and for FSMA seed traceability compliance. reference: FSMA Traceability Rule (21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S); USDA AOSCA Seed Certification Standards; SAP S/4HANA MM Batch Management

description: Current lifecycle status of the seed lot. 'available' = in storage and ready for use; 'reserved' = allocated to a planting plan; 'planted' = fully consumed in field operations; 'depleted' = quantity exhausted; 'quarantined' = held pending quality or regulatory review; 'expired' = past germination validity date.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Batch Status Management; USDA AOSCA Seed Certification Standards

description: Moisture content of the seed lot expressed as a percentage at time of testing or receipt. Critical for safe storage, preventing mold and mycotoxin development, and maintaining germination viability. Monitored per USDA grain storage standards.
reference: USDA Federal Grain Inspection Service (FGIS); USDA AMS Grain Grading Standards; ISO 6540 (Maize moisture content determination)

description: Indicates whether this seed lot has been certified as free of noxious weed seeds as defined by USDA Federal Seed Act and applicable state seed laws. True = certified noxious weed free; False = noxious weed seeds detected or certification not obtained. Required for interstate commerce compliance.
reference: USDA Federal Seed Act (7 U.S.C. 1551-1611); USDA APHIS Noxious Weed Program; State Seed Laws

description: Percentage of pure seed (by weight) in this lot as determined by seed analysis, excluding inert matter, other crop seed, and weed seed. Expressed as a percentage (0.00–100.00). Required for USDA Federal Seed Act labeling compliance and AOSCA certification standards.
reference: USDA Federal Seed Act (7 U.S.C. 1551-1611); AOSA Rules for Testing Seeds; AOSCA Seed Certification Standards

description: Total quantity of seed in this lot expressed in the applicable unit of measure (seeds, bags, CWT, or BU as defined in unit_of_measure). Tracks available inventory for planting planning, procurement, and WMS (Warehouse Management System) inventory control in Manhattan Associates WMS.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Inventory Management; Manhattan Associates WMS; USDA AMS Seed Regulatory Program

description: Date on which this seed lot was physically received at the storage facility. Marks the start of the lot's custody chain for FSMA traceability, FIFO inventory management, and storage duration tracking.
reference: FSMA Traceability Rule (21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S); SAP S/4HANA MM Goods Receipt; USDA GAP Standards

description: Commercial name of the seed treatment product applied to this lot (e.g., 'Cruiser Maxx', 'Poncho/VOTiVO', 'Apron XL'). Required for EPA FIFRA compliance, SDS (Safety Data Sheet) reference, and agronomic record-keeping under GAP standards.
reference: EPA Federal Insecticide Fungicide and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA); EPA Pesticide Registration; USDA GAP (Good Agricultural Practices)

description: Type of chemical or biological coating applied to the seed lot prior to packaging. 'fungicide' = fungicide-only coating; 'insecticide' = insecticide-only coating; 'fungicide_insecticide' = combined coating; 'biological' = biological agent coating; 'untreated' = no treatment applied. Required for EPA pesticide registration compliance, REI (Restricted Entry Interval) tracking, and PHI (Pre-Harvest Interval) management.
reference: EPA Federal Insecticide Fungicide and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA); EPA Pesticide Registration; USDA AMS Seed Regulatory Program

reference: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) Grain Grading Standards; USDA Federal Grain Inspection Service (FGIS)

reference: ISTA (International Seed Testing Association) Rules for Seed Testing; AOSA Rules for Testing Seeds; ISO 520 (Cereals and pulses - determination of the mass of 1000 grains)

reference: EPA Federal Insecticide Fungicide and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA); Codex Alimentarius MRL Standards; USDA AMS Pesticide Data Program

description: Date on which the seed treatment was applied to this lot. Used to calculate treatment age, validate treatment efficacy windows, and support EPA FIFRA compliance and PHI/REI tracking.
reference: EPA Federal Insecticide Fungicide and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA); USDA GAP Standards; FSMA Traceability Rule

reference: FSMA Traceability Rule (21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S); SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) Audit Trail Requirements; ISO 8601

reference: Trimble Ag Software scheduling; EPA PHI/REI label requirements; USDA GAP; Climate FieldView

reference: FSMA traceability; GLOBALG.A.P. record-keeping; ISO 22000

description: Primary key for zone_map
Reference to the specific crop season or growing period for which this zone map is applicable. Links the map to temporal crop planning cycles.
Reference to the farm or agricultural operation that owns or manages the field associated with this zone map.
Reference to the agricultural field for which this zone map was created. Links the zone map to the specific field boundary and location.
Self-referencing FK on zone_map (parent_zone_map_id)
Date when the zone map was formally approved for use in field operations and variable rate application prescriptions.
Username or identifier of the supervisor, agronomist, or authorized personnel who reviewed and approved the zone map for operational use.
Specific agronomic or environmental attribute measured or represented in the zone map (e.g., soil pH, organic matter percentage, elevation above sea level, NDVI value, soil moisture content).

Algorithm or methodology used to classify and delineate management zones within the map (e.g., manual delineation, k-means clustering, supervised classification, unsupervised classification, threshold-based).
Date when the underlying data for the zone map was collected or captured. Important for understanding temporal relevance and data currency.
Spatial reference system or coordinate system used for the zone map (e.g., EPSG:4326 for WGS84, EPSG:32633 for UTM Zone 33N). Critical for accurate geospatial alignment.
Timestamp when this zone map record was first created in the system. Audit field for data lineage and compliance tracking.
Primary source of data used to generate the zone map, such as satellite imagery, drone-based remote sensing, in-field sensors, manual survey, yield monitor data, or soil sampling results.
Date from which this zone map becomes valid and applicable for field operations and variable rate application prescriptions.
Date until which this zone map remains valid. Nullable for maps with indefinite validity. Used for version control and temporal management.
Unique identifier or reference code for the zone map in the external source system. Enables cross-system traceability and data reconciliation.
Digital file format in which the zone map is stored or distributed (e.g., Shapefile, GeoTIFF, GeoJSON, KML, ISO 11783 XML). Critical for system interoperability.
Storage location or file path where the zone map digital file is stored within the data lake or file system. Used for retrieval and access management.
Size of the zone map file expressed in megabytes. Useful for storage management and data transfer planning.
Date when the zone map was generated or created from the source data. Distinct from collection date as processing may occur later.

Name of the external Farm Management Information System (FMIS) or precision agriculture platform from which the zone map was imported or to which it is exported (e.g., Climate FieldView, Trimble Ag Software, John Deere Operations Center).
Boolean flag indicating whether this zone map is actively used for variable rate application prescriptions in field operations (True) or is for reference only (False).
Unique alphanumeric business identifier or code for the zone map, used for external reference and system integration.
Human-readable name or title assigned to this zone map for identification and reference purposes.
Classification of the zone map based on the agronomic or environmental attribute it represents (e.g., soil type, yield potential, elevation, NDVI vegetation index, soil moisture, nutrient levels).
Maximum value of the measured attribute observed across all zones in the map. Defines the upper bound of the data range.
Average or mean value of the measured attribute across all zones in the map. Provides a central tendency measure for the field.
Minimum value of the measured attribute observed across all zones in the map. Defines the lower bound of the data range.
Timestamp when this zone map record was last modified or updated. Audit field for change tracking and data governance.
Free-text field for additional notes, observations, or contextual information about the zone map, such as data quality issues, field conditions during collection, or special considerations.

description: RTK-corrected WGS84 longitude coordinate of the equipment at the time of the reading, in decimal degrees. Supports fleet position tracking, field coverage monitoring, geofence evaluation, and theft detection.
reference: WGS84 Coordinate Reference System; RTK (Real-Time Kinematic) Positioning Standard; Esri ArcGIS

description: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index value captured by the onboard crop sensor at the time of the reading, ranging from -1.0 to 1.0. Supports variable rate application (VRA) decisions, crop health monitoring, and precision agriculture analytics.
reference: NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) Standard; John Deere Operations Center; Trimble Ag Software; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Current operational state of the equipment at the time of the reading. Drives OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) calculation by classifying time into productive, transport, idle, and parked categories. EVENT_PAYLOAD_OR_VALUE per EVENT_LOG role minimum.
reference: ISO 22400 OEE Standard; John Deere Operations Center; FMIS

description: Indicates whether the Power Take-Off (PTO) shaft was engaged at the time of the reading. PTO engagement signals active implement operation (e.g., mower, spreader, pump) and is used for productive-time classification in OEE calculations.
reference: John Deere Operations Center Telematics; ISO 22400 OEE; ASABE Standards

description: Power Take-Off shaft speed in revolutions per minute at the time of the reading when PTO is engaged. Used to verify correct implement operating speed and diagnose PTO-related faults.
reference: John Deere Operations Center Telematics; ASABE Standards

description: Data quality classification for this telemetry record assigned during Silver layer ingestion. 'Valid' records are used in analytics; 'suspect' records require review; 'invalid' records are excluded from reporting. Supports data governance and AI/ML feature engineering.
reference: Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Data Quality; GFSI Data Integrity Standards

description: The precise UTC timestamp when the telemetry event was recorded by the equipment's onboard controller. EVENT_TIMESTAMP per EVENT_LOG role minimum. Distinct from ingestion audit timestamps.
reference: John Deere Operations Center Telematics API; ISO 8601

description: Quality indicator for the GPS/RTK positional correction applied at the time of the reading. 'Fixed' indicates sub-inch accuracy; 'float' and 'dgps' indicate degraded precision. Critical for VRA prescription audit trails and auto-steer accuracy validation.
reference: RTK (Real-Time Kinematic) Positioning Standard; NMEA 0183; Trimble Ag Software

description: Cellular or satellite communication signal strength in decibel-milliwatts (dBm) at the time of the reading. Supports data quality assessment, connectivity gap analysis, and telematics infrastructure planning.
reference: John Deere Operations Center Telematics; IoT (Internet of Things) Connectivity Standards

description: Latency in milliseconds between the equipment recording the telemetry event and the data being received by the cloud platform. Supports data quality scoring and near-real-time fleet dashboard reliability assessment.
reference: John Deere Operations Center Telematics; IoT (Internet of Things) Data Quality Standards

description: Primary key for the lot_allocation association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

description: Foreign key linking this allocation record to the customer account receiving the committed commodity quantity.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: Foreign key linking this allocation record to the specific commodity lot from which quantity is being committed.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: The quantity of the commodity lot committed to this customer account under this allocation, expressed in bushels. This value belongs to the allocation relationship — not to the lot (which tracks total on-hand) nor to the account (which does not own inventory).
reference: USDA grain measurement standards; SAP SD delivery quantity

description: The date on which this allocation was created and committed, recording when the business decision to assign this lot quantity to this account was made. Used for FIFO/FEFO rotation audit trails and forward contract settlement timing.
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: Current lifecycle status of this lot-to-account allocation. Drives fulfillment workflow: PENDING (created, awaiting confirmation), CONFIRMED (customer accepted), SHIPPED (quantity dispatched), INVOICED (billing complete), CANCELLED (allocation voided), ON_HOLD (suspended pending quality or compliance review).
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: The forward contract number, sales order number, or purchase agreement identifier governing this allocation. Links the allocation to the originating commercial agreement. May reference a SAP SD sales order or an external grain trading platform contract ID.
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: The negotiated or contracted price per bushel for this specific lot-account allocation. Price varies by deal, contract terms, and market conditions — it belongs to the allocation, not to the lot (which has no single price) nor to the account (which has no per-lot price).
reference: CBOT/CME commodity pricing; forward contract settlement price

description: Primary key for the lot_fulfillment association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

description: Foreign key linking to the commodity lot being allocated or fulfilled against this delivery order
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: Foreign key linking to the delivery order that this commodity lot (or portion thereof) is fulfilling
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: Batch or lot tracking identifier assigned to the commodity in this delivery. Enables end-to-end traceability from farm origin through customer delivery for FSMA compliance and recall management. [Moved from delivery_order: The lot_number string on delivery_order is a denormalized reference that can only capture a single lot per delivery order. In the true M:N business reality, a delivery order is fulfilled by multiple lots. This field should be removed from delivery_order and replaced by the lot_fulfillment association, which properly links delivery_order to multiple commodity_lot records via commodity_lot_id (which carries lot_number as an attribute).]
reference: FDA FSMA — Traceability Rule (21 CFR Part 1); GLOBALG.A.P. Traceability Standard

description: The percentage of the total commodity lot quantity allocated to this specific delivery order. Supports FIFO/FEFO rotation tracking and lot consumption reporting when a single lot is split across multiple delivery orders.
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: The moisture content percentage of this commodity lot measured at the time of delivery for this specific delivery order. Used for shrinkage calculation, quality settlement, and FSMA traceability. Distinct from the lot's master moisture_content_pct which reflects the moisture at receipt.
reference: USDA moisture testing standards

description: The USDA or contractually specified quality grade confirmed for this specific lot at the time of delivery. May differ from the lot's master grade if re-grading occurred at load-out. Belongs to the lot-delivery pairing, not to either entity alone, and is used for quality settlement and contract compliance.
reference: USDA grain grading standards

description: The quantity of this commodity lot allocated to this specific delivery order, expressed in bushels. Represents the planned commitment of lot inventory to the delivery at the time of allocation. Cannot reside on commodity_lot (which tracks total on-hand) or delivery_order (which tracks total ordered quantity) alone.
reference: FSMA Section 204 lot traceability

description: The actual quantity of this commodity lot that was physically delivered against this delivery order, expressed in bushels. May differ from quantity_allocated_bu due to scale tickets, shrinkage, or load adjustments. Used for quality settlement and inventory depletion.
reference: FSMA Section 204 lot traceability

description: Primary key for the lot_pesticide_exposure association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

description: Foreign key linking to the commodity lot whose PHI compliance status is being determined by this pesticide application exposure record.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

business_glossary_term: Lot Pesticide Exposure - Pesticide Use Record Id
description: Foreign key linking to the pesticide use record (PUR) that generated this exposure event for the associated commodity lot.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: The active ingredient (AI) of the pesticide product as it applies to this lot's exposure record. Captured at the association level to support MRL (Maximum Residue Limit) checks and export compliance queries per lot without requiring a join to the PUR. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.
reference: EPA AI Registration; Codex Alimentarius MRL Tables

description: The date of the pesticide application as it pertains to this specific lot's PHI compliance calculation. Sourced from the detection phase relationship data. Denormalized here to support lot-level PHI window calculations without requiring a join back to the PUR.
reference: EPA PUR Reporting Requirements

description: The application rate of the pesticide product relevant to this lot's exposure. Captured at the association level to support residue estimation and MRL compliance checks per lot. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.
reference: EPA Label Application Rate; FIFRA

description: The portion of the total treated area that is attributable to this specific commodity lot. A single application may cover an entire field, but individual lots may represent sub-parcels or harvest windows within that field. Sourced from detection phase relationship data.
reference: USDA NASS Field Boundary Standards

description: The method by which this lot was determined to be exposed to this pesticide application — e.g., via GIS field boundary overlap, manual agronomist assignment, or system-derived parcel matching. Required for audit trail and regulatory defensibility.
reference: FSMA Section 204 Traceability Records

description: The earliest date on which this commodity lot may be harvested while remaining compliant with the PHI for this specific pesticide application. Calculated as application_date + phi_days from the associated PUR. This derived date belongs to the association because it is specific to the lot-application pairing.
reference: EPA PHI Label Requirements; FSMA Section 204

description: Indicates whether the commodity lot's actual or projected harvest date satisfies the Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) requirement for this specific pesticide application. This flag belongs to the association because the same PUR may be PHI-compliant for one lot (harvested later) and non-compliant for another (harvested earlier).
reference: EPA Label PHI Requirements; FIFRA Section 2(ee)

description: The Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) date — the earliest date on which the commodity could have been legally harvested after the last pesticide or chemical application, per EPA label requirements. Lots harvested before this date may have MRL (Maximum Residue Limit) violations. Critical for food safety compliance and FSMA traceability. [Moved from commodity_lot: The phi_date on commodity_lot is a single scalar that cannot represent the PHI clearance dates from MULTIPLE pesticide applications. The true PHI clearance date is the MAXIMUM phi_clearance_date across all associated PURs for that lot. The lot-level phi_date should be a derived/computed field (max of association phi_clearance_dates), not a stored attribute on the lot itself. The per-application PHI clearance date belongs to the lot_pesticide_exposure association.]
reference: EPA Federal Insecticide Fungicide and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA); FDA MRL regulations 40 CFR Part 180; GLOBALG.A.P. PHI compliance

description: Lifecycle status of this lot-application exposure record. PENDING = awaiting compliance review; CONFIRMED = PHI compliance determination finalized; DISPUTED = under review due to data discrepancy; SUPERSEDED = replaced by a corrected record.
reference: Internal Compliance Workflow

description: Date on which this lot-application exposure linkage was reviewed and confirmed by a compliance officer. Part of the regulatory audit trail for PHI compliance sign-off.
reference: FSMA Section 204; EPA PUR Reporting

description: Name or user ID of the compliance officer or agronomist who reviewed and confirmed this lot-application exposure linkage. Required for regulatory audit trail.
reference: EPA PUR Audit Requirements

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Externally-known document or instrument number assigned by the county recorder or title company at the time of recording. Used for title due diligence and cross-referencing recorded documents.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency Land Records; County Recorder Office Standards

description: Current lifecycle status of the easement. Active indicates the easement is in force; expired indicates the term has lapsed; terminated indicates early legal termination; pending indicates recorded but not yet effective; suspended indicates temporarily inactive due to legal dispute or review.
reference: Internal Land Asset Governance Policy; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: Classification of the easement by its legal purpose. Common types include right-of-way (road/rail corridor), utility (power/telecom lines), drainage (water flow), conservation (land preservation), access (ingress/egress), and pipeline (oil/gas/water). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: right_of_way|utility|drainage|conservation|access|pipeline|irrigation|flood_control|scenic|agricultural_preservation — promote to reference product]
reference: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) Easement Programs; GLOBALG.A.P. Land Use Standards

description: Date on which the easement rights become legally binding and enforceable. May differ from the recording date if the instrument specifies a future commencement date.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency Land Records; GLOBALG.A.P. Land Use Standards

description: Indicates whether an environmental impact review or assessment is required for activities within or adjacent to the easement area. True = environmental review required per EPA or state agency mandate; False = no review required.
reference: EPA National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA); ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: Date on which a term easement expires and the rights revert to the landowner. Null for perpetual easements. Critical for land use planning and lease renewal workflows.
reference: USDA NRCS Easement Program Guidelines; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: Reference identifier linking to the easement boundary geometry stored in Esri ArcGIS. Enables spatial analysis, field mapping, and RTK-accurate boundary visualization in the John Deere Operations Center and ArcGIS GIS platform.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Geospatial Data Standards; John Deere Operations Center Field Mapping

description: Name of the ArcGIS feature layer or map service layer containing the easement geometry. Used to locate and render the easement boundary in GIS-based land use planning and environmental monitoring workflows.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Geospatial Data Standards; ISO 19115 Geographic Information Metadata

description: Full legal name of the party receiving the easement right — typically a utility company, government agency, neighboring landowner, or conservation organization. Required for title due diligence and regulatory compliance.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency Land Records; FSMA Traceability Rule

description: Classification of the grantee entity receiving the easement right. Supports analytics on easement exposure by counterparty category and regulatory reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: utility_company|government_agency|neighbor|conservation_org|railroad|pipeline_company|irrigation_district|municipality — promote to reference product]
reference: USDA NRCS Easement Program Classifications

description: Full legal name of the party granting the easement right — typically the landowner or agricultural operator who owns the burdened parcel. Required for title due diligence and legal enforceability.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency Land Records; FSMA Traceability Rule

description: Indicates whether the easement is perpetual (no expiration date) or term-limited. True = perpetual easement with no expiration; False = term easement with a defined expiration date.
reference: USDA NRCS Easement Program Guidelines

description: Date of the most recent stewardship monitoring visit or compliance inspection conducted on the easement area. Required for conservation easement compliance reporting to USDA NRCS and GFSI certification bodies.
reference: USDA NRCS Conservation Easement Monitoring Requirements; GLOBALG.A.P. Environmental Compliance

description: Formal legal description of the easement area as recorded in the deed or instrument, using metes and bounds, lot/block, or Public Land Survey System (PLSS) section-township-range notation. Required for title due diligence and legal enforceability.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency Land Records; Public Land Survey System (PLSS) Standards

description: Total linear length of the easement corridor in feet. Used for linear easements such as utility lines, pipelines, and road rights-of-way. Combined with corridor_width_ft to determine total encumbered area.
reference: USDA Rural Utilities Service Right-of-Way Standards; Esri ArcGIS GIS Measurement

description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, legal commentary, or land management observations related to the easement. Used by land managers and legal counsel for context not captured in structured fields.
reference: Internal Land Asset Governance Policy

description: Narrative description of land uses explicitly permitted within the easement area by the grantor. May include grazing, crop production, or recreational access where not restricted by the easement terms. Supports land use planning and compliance audits.
reference: USDA NRCS Easement Program Guidelines; GLOBALG.A.P. Land Use Standards

description: Name of the county or jurisdiction where the easement instrument was officially recorded. Required for title due diligence and regulatory compliance reporting.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency Land Records; FSMA Traceability Rule

description: Date the easement instrument was officially recorded with the county recorder or relevant land registry authority. Establishes the legal priority and effective date of the encumbrance.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency Land Records; County Recorder Office Standards

description: Two-letter US state code (e.g., IA, IL, KS) where the easement instrument was recorded. Used for jurisdictional compliance and regulatory reporting to USDA, EPA, and state agricultural agencies.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency Land Records; ISO 3166-2 State/Province Codes

description: Narrative description of land use restrictions imposed by the easement on the grantor's parcel. Includes prohibited activities such as construction, tillage, chemical application, or tree removal within the easement corridor. Critical for crop planning, BMP compliance, and GLOBALG.A.P. certification.
reference: GLOBALG.A.P. Land Use Standards; USDA NRCS Conservation Easement Requirements; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: Scheduled date for the next periodic review or monitoring inspection of the easement, particularly for conservation easements requiring annual stewardship monitoring per USDA NRCS requirements.
reference: USDA NRCS Conservation Easement Monitoring Requirements; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

description: Operational system of record from which this easement record originated. Supports data lineage and integration traceability across Esri ArcGIS, Granular Farm Management, Oracle NetSuite, or manual entry workflows.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer Lineage Policy

description: Actual date on which the easement was legally terminated, released, or extinguished prior to or at its natural expiration. Distinct from expiration_date which is the scheduled end date. Null if the easement is still active.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency Land Records; Internal Land Asset Governance Policy

description: Reason for the termination or expiration of the easement. Applicable only when easement_status is terminated or expired. Values include expired (natural term end), released (voluntary release by grantee), condemned (eminent domain), merged (unity of ownership), or court_order (judicial termination).
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency Land Records; Internal Land Asset Governance Policy

description: Policy number of the title insurance policy that covers this easement encumbrance. Used for risk management, title due diligence, and insurance claims processing.
reference: ALTA (American Land Title Association) Title Insurance Standards; Internal Risk Management Policy

description: Timestamp when the easement record was most recently modified. Supports change data capture (CDC), audit trail, and data quality monitoring in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer.
reference: SOX Section 404 Internal Controls; GDPR Article 5 Data Integrity

description: Narrative description of any identified easement violation or encroachment, including the nature of the violation, date discovered, and current remediation status. Populated only when violation_flag is True.
reference: USDA NRCS Easement Violation Procedures; EPA Enforcement Policy

description: Indicates whether an active easement violation or encroachment has been identified on this easement. True = violation or encroachment currently under investigation or remediation; False = no known violation.
reference: USDA NRCS Easement Violation Procedures; EPA Enforcement Policy

business_glossary_term: Field Certification Scope - Field Certification Scope Id
description: Primary key for the field_certification_scope association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

description: Foreign key linking to the agricultural field or paddock covered under this certification scope record.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

business_glossary_term: Field Certification Scope - Sustainability Certification Id
description: Foreign key linking to the sustainability certification master record under which this field is scoped.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: The numeric audit score or percentage achieved for this specific field during the most recent certification audit. Per-field scores may differ across fields covered by the same certificate, particularly for farm-level certifications spanning multiple paddocks.
reference: Derived from detection phase relationship_data

description: Per-field certification status under this scope record. A field may be suspended or withdrawn from a certification while other fields under the same certificate remain active — this per-field status is distinct from the master certification_status on the sustainability_certification record.
reference: Derived from detection phase relationship_data

description: The portion of this specific field's area that is covered and certified under this certification scope record, in hectares. May be less than the field's total_area_ha if only part of the field is in scope. Distinct from the certification master's aggregate certified_area_ha.
reference: Derived from detection phase relationship_data

description: The date from which this field is operationally in scope for this certification. May differ from the master certificate's effective_date if the field was added to the certification scope after initial issuance.
reference: Derived from detection phase relationship_data

description: The date on which this field's coverage under this certification lapses. May differ from the master certificate's expiry_date if the field's scope was granted for a shorter period or is subject to a separate renewal cycle.
reference: Derived from detection phase relationship_data

description: Indicates whether the field holds active USDA National Organic Program (NOP) certification. Drives input restriction rules, segregation requirements, and organic premium pricing in sales and procurement workflows. [Moved from field: This boolean flag on field is a denormalised indicator that duplicates information now captured structurally in the field_certification_scope association (where USDA Organic certification coverage is a specific scope record). Once the association is in place, organic certification status for a field is derivable by querying field_certification_scope for scheme_name = 'USDA Organic' with certification_status = 'active'. Retaining the boolean creates a dual-maintenance risk and potential inconsistency.]
reference: USDA National Organic Program (NOP) 7 CFR Part 205; GLOBALG.A.P. Organic Certification

business_glossary_term: Field Input Restriction - Field Input Restriction Id
description: Primary key for the field_input_restriction association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

description: Foreign key linking to the agricultural field or paddock on which the input restriction applies
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

business_glossary_term: Field Input Restriction - Ag Input Id
description: Foreign key linking to the agricultural input product that is restricted on the associated field
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: The date from which this field-input restriction is considered active and operationally enforced. Typically aligned with the start of an organic certification period, conservation contract enrollment date, or regulatory advisory issuance date.
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: The date on which this restriction lapses or is no longer applicable. May be null for indefinite restrictions. Examples: expiry of organic certification, end of FSA conservation contract term, or lifting of a groundwater advisory.
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: Indicates whether this restriction is currently in force. Derived from effective_date and expiry_date but maintained as an explicit operational flag to support fast compliance queries during application planning and spray record generation.
reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: The regulatory or policy authority underpinning this restriction. Drives compliance reporting and audit trail. Aligned with USDA NOP, EPA FIFRA, and FSA program requirements.
reference: USDA NOP 7 CFR Part 205, EPA FIFRA, FSA conservation program regulations

description: Human-readable explanation of why this input product is restricted on this field. Examples: 'Organic certification prohibits synthetic inputs', 'Groundwater advisory — sandy soil over aquifer recharge zone', 'FSA conservation contract CRP enrollment', 'GMO-restricted field boundary'.
reference: USDA NOP, EPA groundwater advisory, FSA CRP contract

description: Classification of how the input product is restricted on this field. 'prohibited' means no application permitted; 'rate_limited' means application is allowed below a maximum rate; 'buffer_zone_only' means application is excluded within a defined distance of a waterway or boundary; 'timing_restricted' means application is only permitted outside certain windows (e.g., pre-planting only); 'conditional' means restriction applies only under specific conditions.
reference: USDA NOP, EPA FIFRA label requirements

description: Unique system-generated identifier for the agricultural land lease agreement record. Primary key for the lease data product.
reference: Granular Farm Management; SAP S/4HANA RE-FX (Real Estate) module

description: Reference to the landowner (lessor) party record. Identifies the individual or entity that owns the land and is granting the lease.
reference: Granular Farm Management; SAP S/4HANA Business Partner

description: Reference to the operational farm unit to which the leased land is assigned. Provides operational context for crop planning and field operations.
reference: Granular Farm Management; John Deere Operations Center

description: Reference to the land parcel(s) covered under this lease agreement. Links to the parcel master record in the land domain for legal and GIS boundary context.
reference: Esri ArcGIS; USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) parcel records

description: Foreign key linking to customer.account. Business justification: Leases are executed between legal entities (accounts). The tenant operator account is required for billing, FSA farm operator designation, crop insurance enrollment, and lease payment processing. Role
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Indicates whether the lease agreement contains an automatic renewal clause. When True, the lease renews for an additional term at expiry unless either party provides written notice of termination within the required notice period.
reference: Granular Farm Management; standard agricultural lease contract terms

description: Annual cash rent rate expressed in US dollars per acre. Applicable for cash_rent and flex_rent lease types. Represents the base rental obligation per acre per year. Sensitive commercial term.
reference: USDA ERS Cash Rent Survey; Granular Farm Management; IFRS 16 (lease liability measurement)

description: Indicates whether the lease agreement mandates adherence to specific conservation practices (e.g., cover cropping, no-till, buffer strips) as a condition of tenancy. Supports BMP and ISO 14001 environmental compliance tracking.
reference: USDA NRCS; ISO 14001; GLOBALG.A.P.; Granular Farm Management

business_glossary_term: County Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) Code
description: Five-digit FIPS code identifying the US county in which the leased land is located. Used for USDA program enrollment, regulatory reporting, and geographic analytics.
reference: USDA FSA; US Census Bureau FIPS codes; NRCS county records

description: Timestamp when the lease record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and Silver layer ingestion tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: ISO 8601; SOX audit trail requirements; Databricks Lakehouse Silver layer conventions

description: Free-text description of any crop-specific restrictions or requirements stipulated in the lease (e.g., no GMO crops, organic production required, specific rotation mandated). Impacts crop planning and seed selection decisions.
reference: Granular Farm Management; USDA National Organic Program (NOP); GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Percentage of crop proceeds or harvested commodity allocated to the landowner under a crop share lease arrangement. Typically ranges from 25% to 50%. Applicable only when lease_type is 'crop_share'.
reference: USDA ERS; Granular Farm Management; GLOBALG.A.P. land tenure

description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this lease record (e.g., USD, CAD, BRL). Supports international operations and multi-currency reporting.
reference: ISO 4217; IFRS 16; SAP S/4HANA FI

description: Reference identifier or URL to the executed lease agreement document stored in the document management system. Enables retrieval of the original signed contract for legal and audit purposes.
reference: Granular Farm Management; SAP S/4HANA Document Management

description: The date on which the lease agreement expires or is scheduled to terminate. Nullable for open-ended or evergreen leases. Used for renewal planning and land tenure reporting.
reference: USDA FSA; Granular Farm Management

description: The date on which the lease agreement was formally signed and executed by both parties. May differ from the start date for leases signed in advance of the crop year.
reference: Granular Farm Management; SAP S/4HANA RE-FX

description: The commodity base price (in $/bushel or $/MT) used as the reference point for flex rent adjustment calculations. When the actual commodity price exceeds this threshold, additional rent is triggered. Applicable only for flex_rent lease type.
reference: USDA WASDE; DTN market data; Granular Farm Management

description: Maximum allowable flex rent payment per acre per year, capping the upside obligation for the tenant regardless of commodity price or yield performance. Applicable only for flex_rent lease type.
reference: Granular Farm Management; USDA ERS

description: The mechanism that activates the flex rent adjustment above the base cash rent. Price trigger: based on commodity market price. Yield trigger: based on actual field yield (YPM). Revenue trigger: based on gross revenue per acre. None: not applicable for non-flex leases.
reference: USDA ERS Flex Lease guidance; Granular Farm Management

description: USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) assigned farm number for the leased land. Required for federal program enrollment, crop insurance, and USDA compliance reporting. Links to FSA farm records.
reference: USDA FSA; USDA Farm Records; FSMA compliance

description: USDA FSA tract number identifying the specific tract of land within the FSA farm record. A farm may contain multiple tracts; this field identifies the specific tract(s) covered by this lease.
reference: USDA FSA; USDA Farm Records

description: Indicates whether the lease agreement permits the tenant to make permanent improvements to the land (e.g., drainage tile installation, building construction, irrigation infrastructure). Relevant for CAPEX planning and land stewardship.
reference: Granular Farm Management; USDA NRCS conservation practice standards

description: Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the lease agreement. Used in correspondence with landowners, FSA filings, and internal reference. Format: LSE-YYYY-NNNNNN.
reference: Granular Farm Management; USDA FSA lease documentation standards

description: Current lifecycle state of the lease agreement. Active: in force and binding. Expired: past end date without renewal. Terminated: ended early by either party. Pending: executed but not yet effective. Under negotiation: terms being discussed. Draft: not yet executed.
reference: Granular Farm Management; SAP S/4HANA RE-FX contract lifecycle

description: Classification of the lease agreement structure. Cash rent: fixed $/acre payment. Crop share: landlord receives a percentage of crop proceeds. Flex rent: base rent adjusted by commodity price or yield triggers. Custom farming: operator provides services for a fee. Pasture lease: grazing rights. Hunting lease: recreational use. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: cash_rent|crop_share|flex_rent|custom_farming|pasture_lease|hunting_lease — promote to reference product]
reference: USDA Economic Research Service (ERS) land tenure classifications; Granular Farm Management

description: Formal legal description of the leased land parcel(s) as recorded in the deed or title document. Typically expressed in Public Land Survey System (PLSS) notation (e.g., Section-Township-Range) or metes and bounds.
reference: USDA FSA; Bureau of Land Management (BLM) PLSS; Esri ArcGIS

description: Free-text field for capturing additional terms, special conditions, negotiation history, or operational notes related to the lease agreement that are not captured in structured fields.
reference: Granular Farm Management

description: Calendar month (1–12) in which the primary annual rent payment is due to the landowner. For semi-annual schedules, this represents the first payment month. Used by the finance domain to schedule AP obligations.
reference: Granular Farm Management; SAP S/4HANA FI-AP

description: Frequency at which cash rent payments are due to the landowner under the lease agreement. Drives accounts payable scheduling in the finance domain. Common agricultural practice is annual or semi-annual.
reference: Granular Farm Management; SAP S/4HANA FI-AP; IFRS 16

description: Number of days prior to the lease end date by which written notice of non-renewal or termination must be provided by either party. Typically 30, 60, or 90 days for agricultural leases. Drives automated renewal alert workflows.
reference: Granular Farm Management; state agricultural lease statutes

description: Indicates whether the lease agreement grants the tenant/operator a right of first refusal (ROFR) to purchase the land if the landowner decides to sell. When True, the operator must be offered the opportunity to match any third-party purchase offer.
reference: Granular Farm Management; standard agricultural lease contract terms; USDA FSA

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this lease record was ingested. Supports data lineage and reconciliation across Granular Farm Management, SAP RE-FX, and Oracle NetSuite.
reference: Databricks Lakehouse Silver layer data lineage standards

description: The date on which the lease agreement becomes effective and the tenant/operator gains the right to use the land. Typically March 1 or the start of the crop year for agricultural leases.
reference: USDA FSA; Granular Farm Management; GLOBALG.A.P. land tenure documentation

description: Two-letter US state abbreviation (or ISO 3166-2 subdivision code for international operations) identifying the state in which the leased land is located.
reference: USDA FSA; ISO 3166-2

description: The actual date on which the lease was terminated early, if applicable. Populated only when lease_status is 'terminated'. Distinct from end_date which is the scheduled expiry.
reference: Granular Farm Management; SAP S/4HANA RE-FX

description: Total land area covered under this lease agreement, expressed in acres. Used for cash rent calculation, FSA reporting, and land tenure analytics. Sourced from FSA farm records or GIS boundary measurement.
reference: USDA FSA; Esri ArcGIS; Granular Farm Management

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the lease record. Used for change detection, incremental ETL processing, and audit compliance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: ISO 8601; SOX audit trail requirements; Databricks Lakehouse Silver layer conventions

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each land ownership record in the system. Primary key for the land_ownership data product.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard

description: Reference to the legal owner party (individual, entity, trust, LLC, or partnership) holding an ownership interest in this parcel.
reference: USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS); GDPR Article 4

description: Reference to the land parcel that is subject to this ownership record. Links to the parcel master record in the land domain.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) Parcel Identification Standards

description: Self-referencing identifier pointing to the immediately preceding ownership record in the chain of title for this parcel. Enables traversal of the full ownership history and chain-of-title lineage.
reference: ISO 19152 Land Administration Domain Model (LADM); USDA FSA Land Records

description: The Assessor Parcel Number (APN) assigned by the county assessor's office for property tax assessment purposes. Also known as a parcel identification number (PIN) or tax parcel number. Used for cross-referencing with county tax records.
reference: County Assessor Standards; USDA FSA Farm Records

description: Sequential integer indicating the position of this ownership record in the chain of title for the parcel. A value of 1 represents the earliest recorded ownership; higher values represent more recent ownership records. Supports chain-of-title history and ownership lineage analysis.
reference: ISO 19152 Land Administration Domain Model (LADM); USDA FSA Land Records

description: Indicates whether this parcel is subject to a conservation easement that restricts certain land uses in perpetuity or for a defined term. Conservation easements are commonly held by land trusts or government agencies under USDA NRCS programs.
reference: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) Easement Programs; Internal Revenue Code Section 170(h)

description: The date on which the ownership interest was conveyed (transferred) from the prior owner to the current owner, as stated in the deed instrument. Distinct from recording_date (when filed) and effective_date (when legally binding).
reference: County Recorder Standards; USDA FSA Land Records

description: Three-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the country in which the parcel is located. Supports international operations and COOL (Country of Origin Labeling) compliance.
reference: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; COOL (Country of Origin Labeling) Regulations

description: Name of the county in which the parcel is located and where the deed is recorded. Used for jurisdictional routing of legal documents and regulatory reporting to USDA FSA county offices.
reference: USDA FSA County Office Structure; FIPS County Codes

description: The timestamp when this ownership record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and compliance with FSMA record-keeping requirements.
reference: FSMA Record-Keeping Requirements; ISO 22000; SOX Section 404

description: Indicates the data quality and verification status of this ownership record. 'Verified' means the record has been validated against official county recorder or title company sources; 'unverified' means the record has not yet been validated; 'under_review' means validation is in progress; 'rejected' means the record failed validation.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; GLOBALG.A.P. Record-Keeping Requirements

description: The deed book (volume) number in the county recorder's office where the deed instrument is officially recorded. Used in conjunction with deed_page for precise legal document retrieval.
reference: County Recorder Standards; Uniform Real Property Transfer Act

description: Classification of the legal deed instrument used to convey ownership. Warranty deeds provide full title guarantees; quitclaim deeds convey only the grantor's existing interest; grant deeds include implied warranties; trustee and sheriff deeds arise from trust or court proceedings.
reference: Uniform Real Property Transfer on Death Act; County Recorder Standards

description: The page number within the deed book at the county recorder's office where the deed instrument is officially recorded. Used in conjunction with deed_book for precise legal document retrieval.
reference: County Recorder Standards; Uniform Real Property Transfer Act

description: Unique reference number assigned to the deed instrument conveying ownership of this parcel. Used to cross-reference with county recorder and title company records for chain-of-title verification.
reference: County Recorder Standards; USDA FSA Land Records

description: Free-text notes describing the nature of any ownership dispute, legal challenge, or title defect associated with this ownership record. Populated when ownership_status is 'disputed'. Supports legal team review and resolution tracking.
reference: Internal Legal Governance Standards; American Land Title Association (ALTA)

description: The date on which the ownership interest legally became effective, which may differ from the recording date. For example, a deed may be executed and effective on one date but recorded later. This is the MASTER_AGREEMENT EFFECTIVE_FROM field for this ownership record.
reference: USDA FSA Land Tenure Standards; ISO 19152 Land Administration Domain Model (LADM)

description: Narrative description of any encumbrances, liens, easements, mortgages, conservation easements, or other title restrictions affecting this ownership record. Populated when encumbrance_flag is True.
reference: American Land Title Association (ALTA) Standards; USDA NRCS Conservation Easement Program

description: Indicates whether this ownership record is subject to any encumbrances, liens, easements, mortgages, or other claims against the title that may affect the owner's full use and enjoyment of the parcel.
reference: American Land Title Association (ALTA) Standards; USDA FSA Land Records

description: The date on which the ownership interest expires or terminates, applicable for term interests such as life estates or time-limited ownership arrangements. Null for perpetual fee simple ownership. This is the MASTER_AGREEMENT EFFECTIVE_UNTIL field.
reference: USDA FSA Land Tenure Standards; Uniform Real Property Transfer on Death Act

description: The USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) tract number assigned to this parcel for farm program eligibility, commodity program enrollment, and conservation program participation tracking.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) Farm Records System

description: Full legal description of the parcel as recorded on the deed, typically expressed in metes and bounds, Public Land Survey System (PLSS) section-township-range notation, or lot-block-subdivision format. This is the authoritative legal boundary description for the parcel.
reference: USDA FSA Farm Records; Public Land Survey System (PLSS); ISO 19152 LADM

description: General free-text notes or remarks related to this ownership record, including special conditions, legal caveats, or administrative observations not captured in structured fields.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard

description: Classification of the legal entity type of the owner. Distinguishes between natural persons and legal entities for regulatory reporting, USDA farm program eligibility, and compliance with FSMA and COOL requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: individual|corporation|llc|partnership|trust|government|cooperative|nonprofit — promote to reference product]
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) Payment Eligibility Rules; IRS Entity Classification

description: Current lifecycle state of this ownership record. 'Current' indicates active legal ownership; 'historical' indicates a past ownership interest that has been transferred or extinguished; 'disputed' flags records under legal challenge; 'pending' indicates a transfer in progress; 'transferred' indicates completed conveyance to a new owner.
reference: USDA FSA Land Tenure Data Standards; ISO 19152 Land Administration Domain Model (LADM)

description: Legal classification of the ownership interest held by the owner in this parcel. Fee simple is the most complete form of ownership; joint tenancy includes right of survivorship; tenancy in common allows fractional interests without survivorship; life estate is limited to the owner's lifetime; trust and LLC membership reflect entity-held interests.
reference: Uniform Real Property Transfer on Death Act; USDA FSA Land Ownership Classification

description: Fractional ownership interest held by this owner in the parcel, expressed as a percentage (e.g., 50.0000 for a 50% undivided interest). Supports multi-owner parcels with tenancy-in-common or LLC membership fractional interest tracking. All ownership records for a parcel should sum to 100%.
reference: Uniform Partition of Heirs Property Act; USDA FSA Payment Limitation Rules

description: Externally-known unique reference number assigned to this ownership record, used for cross-referencing with county recorder offices, title companies, and legal documentation. Serves as the business identifier for chain-of-title tracking.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA); County Recorder Standards

description: The date on which the deed or ownership instrument was officially recorded with the county recorder's office. Establishes the legal priority of the ownership claim in the chain of title.
reference: County Recorder Standards; Uniform Real Property Transfer Act

description: Identifies the operational system of record from which this ownership record was sourced or last updated. Supports data lineage and master data management. Typical sources include Granular Farm Management, Esri ArcGIS, SAP S/4HANA, Oracle NetSuite, or manual entry.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; FMIS (Farm Management Information System) Integration Standards

description: Two-letter USPS state abbreviation for the state in which the parcel is located. Used for jurisdictional compliance, USDA FSA state office routing, and regulatory reporting.
reference: USPS State Abbreviation Standards; USDA FSA State Office Structure

description: Name of the title insurance underwriter or company that issued the title insurance policy for this ownership record. Used for claims processing and title defect resolution.
reference: American Land Title Association (ALTA) Standards

description: The policy number of the title insurance policy issued to protect the owner's interest in this parcel against title defects, liens, or encumbrances not discovered during the title search. Issued by a licensed title insurance underwriter.
reference: American Land Title Association (ALTA) Standards; State Insurance Regulations

description: The reason or mechanism by which ownership was transferred to the current owner. Used for USDA FSA farm program eligibility determination, estate planning analysis, and land tenure reporting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: sale|inheritance|gift|foreclosure|condemnation|partition|exchange|court_order — promote to reference product]
reference: USDA FSA Land Tenure Data Standards; USDA Economic Research Service (ERS) Land Ownership Survey

description: The timestamp when this ownership record was last modified in the system. Supports audit trail, change tracking, and data lineage for compliance with SOX and FSMA record-keeping requirements.
reference: FSMA Record-Keeping Requirements; SOX Section 404; ISO 22000

description: The USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) farm number associated with this parcel, used for enrollment in commodity support programs, conservation programs, and crop insurance. A single farm number may encompass multiple tracts and parcels.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) Farm Records System; USDA Agricultural Act

description: Unique system-generated surrogate identifier for the water right record. Primary key for the water_right data product in the land domain.

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the water right entitlement record governing the permitted water withdrawal volume for this irrigation zone. Supports regulatory compliance with state water authority permit requirements.

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Ratio of water beneficially used by the crop to the total water applied by the irrigation system, expressed as a percentage. Key performance indicator for water use efficiency benchmarking against USDA NRCS and GLOBALG.A.P. standards.

description: Indicates whether this irrigation or drainage zone is currently operating in compliance with applicable Best Management Practices (BMP) for water management as defined by USDA NRCS and state environmental agencies. Supports ISO 14001 environmental compliance reporting.

reference: USDA NRCS Conservation Practice Standards; EQIP Program Requirements; FSMA Compliance

description: Timestamp when this irrigation zone record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver Layer ingestion tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.
reference: ISO 8601; SOX Audit Trail Requirements; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity)

description: Engineered water application rate of the irrigation system expressed in inches per hour. Used to match application rate to soil infiltration capacity to prevent runoff and ensure uniform distribution. Sourced from system design specifications.
reference: USDA NRCS Irrigation Guide; ASABE Standards; Trimble Ag Software

description: Total land area served by the subsurface tile drainage system in this zone, measured in acres. Used for drainage coefficient calculations, drainage district permit compliance, and BMP reporting. Applicable when zone_type = 'subsurface_drainage'.

description: Design drainage rate of the subsurface tile system expressed in inches of water removed per day. Determines system capacity to handle peak rainfall events and maintain trafficable field conditions. Applicable when zone_type = 'subsurface_drainage'.
reference: USDA NRCS Conservation Practice Standard 606; ASABE EP480

description: Permit number or reference code issued by the local drainage district authority governing the subsurface tile drainage system. Required for regulatory compliance and environmental reporting. Applicable when zone_type = 'subsurface_drainage'.
reference: State Drainage District Regulations; EPA Clean Water Act; USDA NRCS Conservation Compliance

description: Indicates whether this irrigation zone uses Evapotranspiration (ET)-based scheduling to determine irrigation timing and volume. ET-based scheduling integrates weather data and crop coefficients to optimize water use efficiency.
reference: USDA NRCS Irrigation Water Management; Climate FieldView ET Scheduling; ASCE Standardized Reference ET

description: Reference identifier or layer name for the zone boundary polygon stored in Esri ArcGIS. Enables spatial analysis, overlap detection, and RTK-accurate field mapping for precision water management.
reference: Esri ArcGIS; John Deere Operations Center; USDA FSA CLU (Common Land Unit)

description: Name of the contractor or company that installed the irrigation system or subsurface tile drainage system. Used for warranty claims, maintenance coordination, and capital expenditure (CAPEX) documentation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PM Module; Granular Farm Management

description: Total capital expenditure (CAPEX) incurred for the installation of the irrigation or drainage system, expressed in US dollars. Used for asset valuation, depreciation calculations, and ROI analysis in SAP S/4HANA FI-AA and Granular Farm Management financial planning.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; GAAP/IFRS Capital Expenditure Standards; FASB ASC 360

description: Calendar year in which the irrigation or drainage system was installed. Used for asset age tracking, depreciation scheduling, and infrastructure replacement planning in SAP S/4HANA Fixed Assets.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA (Fixed Asset Accounting); GAAP/IFRS Asset Depreciation Standards

description: Total land area served by this irrigation zone measured in acres. Used for permitted volume compliance calculations, water use efficiency reporting, and USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) acreage reporting.

description: Date of the most recent physical inspection of the irrigation or drainage system infrastructure. Used to track maintenance compliance intervals and trigger inspection work orders in SAP S/4HANA PM.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PM Module; ISO 55000 Asset Management; GLOBALG.A.P. Infrastructure Maintenance

description: Free-text operational notes or remarks about the irrigation or drainage zone, including known issues, special operating conditions, or historical context not captured in structured fields. Used by farm managers and agronomists in Granular Farm Management.
reference: Granular Farm Management; John Deere Operations Center

description: Maximum annual water withdrawal volume authorized under the associated water right permit, expressed in acre-feet. Compliance ceiling for seasonal irrigation scheduling and water use reporting to state water authorities.
reference: State Water Authority Permit Frameworks; USDA NRCS Water Rights; EPA Clean Water Act

description: Number of soil moisture sensor locations deployed within this irrigation zone for real-time soil water status monitoring. Supports IoT-driven precision irrigation scheduling via John Deere Operations Center integration.
reference: John Deere Operations Center IoT Integration; USDA NRCS Soil Moisture Monitoring

description: GPS coordinate string or GIS reference describing the placement locations of soil moisture sensors within the zone (e.g., WKT MULTIPOINT or comma-separated lat/lon pairs). Supports precision water management and IoT sensor mapping in Esri ArcGIS.
reference: Esri ArcGIS; John Deere Operations Center; RTK GPS Standards

description: Current physical condition assessment of the irrigation or drainage infrastructure. Drives maintenance prioritization, capital replacement planning, and OEE reporting in SAP S/4HANA PM and John Deere Operations Center.
reference: SAP S/4HANA PM Module; USDA NRCS Conservation Practice Standards; ISO 55000 Asset Management

description: Classification of the irrigation delivery system technology installed in this zone. Determines application efficiency benchmarks, scheduling parameters, and maintenance requirements. reference: USDA NRCS Irrigation Guide; ASABE Standards; Climate FieldView

description: Installation depth of the subsurface drainage tile below the soil surface in inches. Affects drainage effectiveness, frost protection, and interaction with soil horizons. Applicable when zone_type = 'subsurface_drainage'.
reference: USDA NRCS Conservation Practice Standard 606; ASABE EP480

description: Internal diameter of the subsurface drainage tile pipe in inches. Determines hydraulic capacity and drainage coefficient. Used for system capacity calculations and replacement planning. Applicable when zone_type = 'subsurface_drainage'.
reference: USDA NRCS Conservation Practice Standard 606; ASABE EP480

reference: Esri ArcGIS; USDA NRCS Conservation Practice Standard 606

description: Material composition of the subsurface drainage tile pipe installed in this zone. Corrugated plastic/HDPE is the modern standard; clay and concrete are legacy materials found in older installations. Applicable when zone_type = 'subsurface_drainage'.
reference: USDA NRCS Conservation Practice Standard 606; ASABE EP480

description: GPS latitude coordinate of the subsurface tile drainage system outlet location in decimal degrees (WGS84). Used for field mapping in Esri ArcGIS and environmental monitoring of drainage discharge points. Applicable when zone_type = 'subsurface_drainage'.
reference: Esri ArcGIS; WGS84 Coordinate Reference System; EPA Clean Water Act Section 404

description: GPS longitude coordinate of the subsurface tile drainage system outlet location in decimal degrees (WGS84). Used for field mapping in Esri ArcGIS and environmental monitoring of drainage discharge points. Applicable when zone_type = 'subsurface_drainage'.
reference: Esri ArcGIS; WGS84 Coordinate Reference System; EPA Clean Water Act Section 404

description: Classification of the subsurface tile drainage system layout installed in this zone. reference: USDA NRCS Conservation Practice Standard 606 (Subsurface Drain); ASABE EP480

Critical for water right compliance and drought risk assessment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: well|river|reservoir|canal|municipal|recycled — promote to reference product if additional sources are needed]
reference: USDA NRCS Water Management; EPA Clean Water Act; State Water Authority Regulations

description: Current operational lifecycle status of the irrigation or drainage zone. Drives scheduling eligibility, maintenance planning, and asset reporting in SAP S/4HANA PM and John Deere Operations Center.

reference: USDA NRCS Conservation Practice Standards; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

description: Unique system-generated identifier for each individual soil sampling event record. Primary key for the soil_sample data product in the land domain.
reference: ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems; USDA NRCS Soil Survey Standards

description: Reference to the agricultural field from which this soil sample was collected. Links to the land domain field master record for GIS boundary and parcel context.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Field Mapping; John Deere Operations Center Field Registry

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

reference: Trimble Ag Software VRA Zone Management; USDA Precision Agriculture Guidelines
