reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Percentage of the soil's Cation Exchange Capacity (CEC) occupied by base cations (calcium, magnesium, potassium, sodium). Calculated from individual cation concentrations relative to CEC. Used to assess nutrient balance and guide lime and fertilizer application strategies.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Fertility Assessment; Mehlich-3 Base Saturation Calculation Method

description: Buffer pH value measured using a buffered solution (e.g., Shoemaker-McLean-Pratt or Sikora buffer) to determine the lime requirement for acidic soils. Used in conjunction with water pH to calculate the amount of agricultural lime needed to raise soil pH to target levels.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Testing Methods; SMP Buffer pH Method; Sikora Buffer Method

description: Plant-available calcium (Ca) concentration in parts per million (ppm). Calcium is a secondary macronutrient essential for cell wall development and root growth. Also used in calculating percent base saturation and Cation Exchange Capacity (CEC) balance.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Fertility Guidelines; Mehlich-3 Extraction Method; GLOBALG.A.P. Soil Nutrient Standards

description: Cation Exchange Capacity (CEC) of the soil expressed in milliequivalents per 100 grams of soil (meq/100g). CEC measures the soil's ability to hold and supply positively charged nutrient ions (Ca, Mg, K, Na, H). Higher CEC indicates greater nutrient-holding capacity and influences fertilizer efficiency.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Survey Laboratory Methods; ISO 14235 Soil Quality; GLOBALG.A.P. Soil Health

description: Unique reference number of the Certificate of Analysis (COA) issued by the laboratory for this soil sample. The COA is the official document certifying the analytical results and chain of custody.
reference: ISO/IEC 17025; USDA NRCS Soil Testing Standards; GLOBALG.A.P. Record Keeping Requirements

description: Timestamp when this soil sample record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail, data lineage, and Silver layer ingestion tracking.
reference: ISO 8601 Date and Time Standards; SOX Audit Trail Requirements; GDPR Article 5 Data Integrity

description: The four-digit crop production year associated with this soil sampling event (e.g., 2024). Used to align soil test results with the corresponding growing season for fertilizer prescription planning and year-over-year soil health trend analysis.
reference: USDA NRCS Nutrient Management Planning; Granular Farm Management Financial Planning

description: Electrical Conductivity (EC) of the soil measured in deciSiemens per meter (dS/m). EC is an indicator of soil salinity and total dissolved salt concentration. High EC values indicate salinity stress risk and influence irrigation management and crop selection decisions.
reference: USDA NRCS Salinity Laboratory Methods; ISO 11265 Soil EC Measurement; GLOBALG.A.P. Soil Health

description: Horizontal positional accuracy of the GPS coordinates in meters at time of sample collection. RTK-corrected readings typically achieve sub-0.05m accuracy. Used to assess spatial data quality for precision agriculture applications.
reference: John Deere Operations Center RTK GPS Standards; Esri ArcGIS Data Quality; ISO 19157 Geographic Data Quality

description: Official accreditation or certification number of the laboratory that analyzed the sample, issued by a recognized accreditation body (e.g., A2LA, NELAP). Supports regulatory compliance and audit traceability.
reference: ISO/IEC 17025; USDA AMS Laboratory Accreditation Program; NELAP Standards

description: Date on which the laboratory issued the official analytical results report for this soil sample. Used to calculate lab turnaround time and determine data currency for fertilizer prescriptions.
reference: ISO/IEC 17025 Laboratory Competence; USDA AMS Laboratory Accreditation Program

description: Date on which the collected soil sample was submitted to the analytical laboratory for processing. Used to track turnaround time and chain-of-custody compliance.
reference: USDA AMS Laboratory Accreditation Program; ISO/IEC 17025 Laboratory Competence

description: GPS latitude coordinate (decimal degrees, WGS84 datum) of the soil sample collection point. Captured via RTK-accurate GPS equipment for precise spatial referencing in GIS systems and VRA prescription mapping.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Spatial Reference Standards; John Deere Operations Center RTK GPS; WGS84 Datum

description: Laboratory-recommended agricultural lime application rate in pounds per acre, calculated from soil pH and buffer pH results to raise soil pH to the target level for the planned crop. Directly used in fertilizer prescription and VRA lime application planning.
reference: USDA NRCS Lime Requirement Calculation Methods; Trimble Ag Software VRA Prescriptions

description: GPS longitude coordinate (decimal degrees, WGS84 datum) of the soil sample collection point. Captured via RTK-accurate GPS equipment for precise spatial referencing in GIS systems and VRA prescription mapping.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Spatial Reference Standards; John Deere Operations Center RTK GPS; WGS84 Datum

description: Plant-available magnesium (Mg) concentration in parts per million (ppm). Magnesium is a secondary macronutrient and central component of chlorophyll. Used in CEC base saturation calculations and dolomitic lime application decisions.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Fertility Guidelines; Mehlich-3 Extraction Method; GLOBALG.A.P. Soil Nutrient Standards

description: Plant-available nitrate nitrogen (NO3-N) concentration in parts per million (ppm) as measured in the soil sample. A key component of the Nitrogen-Phosphorus-Potassium (NPK) nutrient profile. Directly informs nitrogen fertilizer application rates and VRA prescriptions.
reference: USDA NRCS Nutrient Management Planning; EPA Nitrate Leaching Standards; GLOBALG.A.P. Nutrient Management

description: Laboratory or agronomist-recommended nitrogen (N) fertilizer application rate in pounds per acre based on soil nitrate-N test results, organic matter nitrogen credit, and planned crop yield goal. Core input for NPK fertilizer prescription and VRA planning.
reference: USDA NRCS Nutrient Management Planning; EPA Nitrogen Management Best Practices; Trimble Ag VRA

description: Percentage of organic matter (OM) in the soil sample, measured by loss-on-ignition or Walkley-Black method. Organic matter is a key indicator of soil health, water-holding capacity, and biological activity. Drives nitrogen credit calculations and carbon sequestration assessments.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Health Assessment; ISO 14001 Soil Carbon Monitoring; GLOBALG.A.P. Soil Organic Matter Standards

description: Soil pH measured using the 1:1 soil-to-water suspension method, representing the Potential of Hydrogen (pH) — the primary indicator of soil acidity or alkalinity. Values range from 0-14; optimal crop production typically falls between 6.0-7.0. Drives lime application recommendations.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Survey Laboratory Methods Manual; Mehlich-3 / 1:1 Water pH Method; GLOBALG.A.P. Soil Health

description: Laboratory extraction method used to determine plant-available phosphorus concentration. Bray-1 is standard for acidic soils; Mehlich-3 is a universal extractant; Olsen is used for calcareous/alkaline soils. Method must be recorded as results are not directly comparable across methods.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Testing Methods Manual; North Central Regional Publication 221

description: Plant-available phosphorus (P) concentration in parts per million (ppm), measured by Bray-1 or Mehlich-3 extraction method. A key component of the Nitrogen-Phosphorus-Potassium (NPK) nutrient profile. Drives phosphate fertilizer recommendations and VRA prescription maps.
reference: USDA NRCS Nutrient Management; Bray-1 / Mehlich-3 Extraction Methods; EPA Phosphorus Loss Risk Assessment

description: Laboratory or agronomist-recommended phosphate (P2O5) fertilizer application rate in pounds per acre based on soil phosphorus test results and planned crop yield goal. Core input for NPK fertilizer prescription and VRA planning.
reference: USDA NRCS Nutrient Management Planning; EPA Phosphorus Index; Trimble Ag VRA Prescriptions

description: Plant-available potassium (K) concentration in parts per million (ppm), measured by Mehlich-3 or ammonium acetate extraction. A key component of the Nitrogen-Phosphorus-Potassium (NPK) nutrient profile. Drives potash fertilizer recommendations and VRA prescription planning.
reference: USDA NRCS Nutrient Management Planning; Mehlich-3 Extraction Method; GLOBALG.A.P. Nutrient Management

description: Laboratory or agronomist-recommended potash (K2O) fertilizer application rate in pounds per acre based on soil potassium test results and planned crop yield goal. Core input for NPK fertilizer prescription and VRA planning.
reference: USDA NRCS Nutrient Management Planning; Trimble Ag Software VRA Prescriptions

description: Calendar date on which the soil sample was physically collected from the field. Critical for seasonal trend analysis and determining the agronomic context (pre-plant, post-harvest, etc.).
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Sampling Protocols; GLOBALG.A.P. Soil Health Standards

description: Depth in inches at which the soil sample was collected from the surface. Standard agronomic sampling depths are 0-6 inches (topsoil) or 6-12 inches (subsoil). Critical for interpreting nutrient availability relative to root zone.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Sampling Depth Standards; GLOBALG.A.P. Soil Management; Trimble Ag Software

description: Method used to collect the soil sample. Grid sampling uses a systematic spatial grid; zone sampling collects within defined management zones; composite combines multiple cores; benchmark uses fixed reference points for longitudinal tracking.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Sampling Protocols; Trimble Ag Software VRA Sampling; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Externally-known, human-readable sample identifier assigned at time of collection, used for lab submission tracking and field cross-referencing. Typically formatted as a lab accession or farm-assigned code (e.g., FARM-2024-F01-Z3).
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Sampling Guidelines; GLOBALG.A.P. Soil Management Standards

description: Current lifecycle status of the soil sample record, tracking progression from field collection through laboratory analysis to agronomic approval for use in fertilizer prescriptions.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Sampling Workflow; ISO 14001 Environmental Records Management

description: Name or identifier of the agronomist, certified crop advisor (CCA), or field technician who physically collected the soil sample. Used for chain-of-custody documentation and quality assurance traceability.
reference: GLOBALG.A.P. Chain of Custody Requirements; USDA NRCS Soil Sampling SOPs; FSMA Traceability Rule

description: USDA soil texture classification based on the relative proportions of sand, silt, and clay particles. Texture class influences water-holding capacity, drainage, tillage requirements, and nutrient management. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: sand|loamy_sand|sandy_loam|loam|silt_loam|silt|sandy_clay_loam|clay_loam|silty_clay_loam|sandy_clay|silty_clay|clay — promote to reference product]
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Texture Classification System; USDA Soil Survey Manual

description: Plant-available sulfur (S) concentration in parts per million (ppm). Sulfur is a secondary macronutrient critical for protein synthesis and enzyme function. Deficiencies are increasingly common in high-yield cropping systems and drive sulfur fertilizer recommendations.
reference: USDA NRCS Nutrient Management; GLOBALG.A.P. Soil Nutrient Standards

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this soil sample record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change detection, incremental data pipeline processing, and audit compliance.
reference: ISO 8601 Date and Time Standards; SOX Audit Trail Requirements; GDPR Article 5 Data Integrity

description: Plant-available zinc (Zn) micronutrient concentration in parts per million (ppm), measured by Mehlich-3 or DTPA extraction. Zinc deficiency is common in high-pH soils and drives micronutrient fertilizer recommendations for corn and other sensitive crops.
reference: USDA NRCS Micronutrient Management; Mehlich-3 / DTPA Extraction Methods; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the management zone record in the Databricks Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
reference: ISO 11179 - Metadata Registry

description: Reference to the parent agricultural field within which this management zone is spatially defined. Links to the land domain field entity.
reference: GLOBALG.A.P. Control Point CB 1.1 - Field Identification

description: Reference to the growing season for which this management zone configuration is active. Management zone boundaries and soil attribute values may be updated between growing seasons as new soil sampling and yield data become available.
reference: Granular Farm Management - Season Planning; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 1.1

description: Foreign key linking to land.soil_profile. Business justification: A management zone is delineated based on soil characteristics (EC, pH, OM, CEC, texture) that are authoritatively captured in the soil_profile entity. Linking management_zone to soil_profile formalize
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Free-text field for agronomist or crop consultant observations about the management zone, including special management considerations, historical problem areas, or recommendations for upcoming season. Captured in Granular Farm Management or Trimble Ag Software during field scouting.
reference: Granular Farm Management - Field Notes; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 1.3 - Record Keeping

description: Calculated spatial area of the management zone expressed in acres, derived from the GIS polygon geometry. Used for VRA prescription rate calculations, input cost allocation, and yield-per-acre (YPM) reporting. Precision to four decimal places supports sub-acre zone granularity.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Spatial Analysis; USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) Field Acreage Standards

description: Calculated spatial area of the management zone expressed in hectares for international reporting and metric-system compliance. Supports GLOBALG.A.P. and ISO 14001 environmental reporting requirements.
reference: GLOBALG.A.P. CB 1.1; ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems; Codex Alimentarius

description: Mean cation exchange capacity (CEC) of the management zone soil expressed in milliequivalents per 100 grams (meq/100g). Measures the soil's ability to hold and supply positively charged nutrient ions (Ca, Mg, K, Na). Higher CEC indicates greater nutrient-holding capacity. Used for fertilizer rate calibration and soil amendment planning.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Survey; ISO 11260 Soil Quality - CEC Determination; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 4.2

description: Latitude coordinate of the management zone polygon centroid in decimal degrees (WGS84). Used for GPS (Global Positioning System) navigation, weather station proximity matching, and spatial analytics in Esri ArcGIS.
reference: Esri ArcGIS - Coordinate Reference Systems; WGS84 Standard; John Deere Operations Center GPS

description: Longitude coordinate of the management zone polygon centroid in decimal degrees (WGS84). Used for GPS navigation, weather data correlation, and spatial analytics in Esri ArcGIS.
reference: Esri ArcGIS - Coordinate Reference Systems; WGS84 Standard; John Deere Operations Center GPS

description: USDA NRCS conservation practice standard code applied to this management zone (e.g., 590 - Nutrient Management, 329 - Residue and Tillage Management, 340 - Cover Crop, 412 - Grassed Waterway). Supports USDA EQIP (Environmental Quality Incentives Program) compliance reporting and ISO 14001 environmental management documentation.
reference: USDA NRCS Conservation Practice Standards; USDA EQIP Program Requirements; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

description: Timestamp when this management zone record was first created in the lakehouse Silver Layer, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.
reference: ISO 8601 Date and Time Standards; SOX Section 404 - Data Audit Trail; GDPR Article 5 - Data Integrity

description: Method used to spatially delineate the management zone boundary. EC (Electrical Conductivity) scanning uses Veris or EM38 sensors; yield history uses multi-year combine yield monitor data from Climate FieldView or John Deere Operations Center; satellite NDVI uses remote sensing imagery; manual uses operator-drawn boundaries in Esri ArcGIS or Trimble Ag; soil sampling uses interpolated soil test point data; topographic analysis uses digital elevation model (DEM) data.
reference: Trimble Ag Software - Prescription Management; Climate FieldView Analytics; John Deere Operations Center

description: Calendar year in which the management zone boundary was originally delineated or most recently revised. Used to assess zone data currency and schedule periodic re-delineation based on updated EC scanning, yield history, or satellite imagery data.
reference: Trimble Ag Software - Zone Version Management; USDA NRCS BMP Guidelines

description: USDA NRCS soil drainage class for the management zone, indicating the natural rate of water removal from the soil profile. Affects crop selection, planting date decisions, and tile drainage infrastructure planning. Poorly drained zones may qualify for wetland conservation programs.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Survey - Drainage Class Definitions; USDA Farm Service Agency Conservation Programs

description: Apparent soil electrical conductivity (EC) reading at deep depth (typically 0-90 cm) expressed in deciSiemens per meter (dS/m). Measured via Veris 3100 or EM38 sensor. Reflects subsoil characteristics including clay pan depth and water-holding capacity. Complements shallow EC for comprehensive zone delineation.
reference: Trimble Ag Software - EC Zone Delineation; USDA NRCS Soil EC Standards; Veris Technologies Measurement Protocol

description: Date on which the soil electrical conductivity (EC) scanning survey was conducted for this management zone. Used to assess data currency and schedule re-scanning intervals (typically every 3-5 years per BMP guidelines).
reference: Trimble Ag Software - EC Scanning Protocol; USDA NRCS BMP Guidelines

description: Apparent soil electrical conductivity (EC) reading at shallow depth (typically 0-30 cm) expressed in deciSiemens per meter (dS/m). Measured via Veris 3100 or EM38 sensor during EC scanning. Correlates with soil texture, clay content, and salinity. Used as primary input for EC-based zone delineation and VRA (Variable Rate Application) prescription generation.
reference: Trimble Ag Software - EC Zone Delineation; USDA NRCS Soil EC Standards; Veris Technologies Measurement Protocol

description: Native identifier of this management zone in the originating source system (e.g., Trimble Ag zone GUID, John Deere Operations Center zone ID, Esri ArcGIS feature OID). Enables bidirectional synchronization and traceability between the lakehouse Silver Layer and operational precision agriculture platforms.
reference: Trimble Ag Software - Zone API; John Deere Operations Center - Field Boundary API; Esri ArcGIS REST API

description: Spatial boundary of the management zone stored as Well-Known Text (WKT) polygon geometry in WGS84 coordinate reference system (EPSG:4326). Sourced from Esri ArcGIS or John Deere Operations Center RTK-accurate field mapping. Enables spatial joins with soil sampling points, yield data, and satellite imagery layers.
reference: Esri ArcGIS - Feature Class Standards; OGC Simple Features Standard; ISO 19125

description: Date of the most recent composite soil sampling event conducted within this management zone. Used to assess soil data currency and trigger re-sampling workflows. GLOBALG.A.P. and USDA NRCS BMP guidelines recommend soil sampling every 2-4 years.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Sampling Guidelines; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 4.2; ISO 10381 Soil Sampling Standards

description: Date on which the satellite or aerial imagery used to calculate the current NDVI value was captured. Critical for assessing data currency and seasonal relevance of the vegetation index reading.
reference: Climate FieldView - Imagery Metadata; Sentinel-2 / Landsat Data Standards

description: Most recent NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) value for the management zone, ranging from -1.0 to 1.0. Derived from satellite or aerial multispectral imagery. Values above 0.5 indicate dense, healthy vegetation; values below 0.2 indicate sparse or stressed vegetation. Used for in-season crop monitoring and zone reclassification.
reference: Climate FieldView - NDVI Analytics; NASA Landsat / Sentinel-2 Remote Sensing Standards; USDA NASS Crop Monitoring

description: Mean available nitrogen (N) level in the management zone soil expressed in pounds per acre (lbs/acre), derived from composite soil sampling. Component of NPK (Nitrogen Phosphorus Potassium) nutrient profile. Used to calculate nitrogen fertilizer application rates in VRA prescriptions and comply with nutrient management plan requirements.
reference: USDA NRCS Nutrient Management Practice Standard 590; EPA Nutrient Management Guidelines; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 4.2

description: Mean soil organic matter (OM) content expressed as a percentage of dry soil weight for the management zone. Measured via loss-on-ignition or Walkley-Black method from composite soil samples. Higher OM improves water retention, nutrient cycling, and soil structure. Key indicator for carbon sequestration reporting under ISCC and sustainability programs.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Health Framework; ISO 14235 Soil Quality - Organic Carbon; ISCC Carbon Certification

description: Mean available phosphorus (P) level in the management zone soil expressed in pounds per acre (lbs/acre), derived from composite soil sampling. Component of NPK nutrient profile. Used to calculate phosphorus fertilizer application rates in VRA prescriptions and support EPA water quality compliance for phosphorus runoff management.
reference: USDA NRCS Nutrient Management Practice Standard 590; EPA Clean Water Act - Nutrient Runoff; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 4.2

description: Mean available potassium (K) level in the management zone soil expressed in pounds per acre (lbs/acre), derived from composite soil sampling. Component of NPK nutrient profile. Used to calculate potassium fertilizer application rates in VRA prescriptions.
reference: USDA NRCS Nutrient Management Practice Standard 590; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 4.2

description: Agronomic productivity classification of the management zone based on historical yield performance and soil capability. High productivity zones receive premium input rates; low productivity zones may receive reduced inputs or conservation treatment under BMP (Best Management Practices) guidelines.
reference: USDA NRCS Land Capability Classification; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 1.1; BMP Guidelines

description: Mean slope gradient of the management zone expressed as a percentage (rise over run × 100), derived from digital elevation model (DEM) analysis in Esri ArcGIS. Used for erosion risk assessment, drainage planning, and equipment operation safety. Slopes above 8% may require conservation practices under USDA NRCS BMP guidelines.
reference: USDA NRCS Land Capability Classification; Esri ArcGIS Terrain Analysis; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

description: Mean soil pH (Potential of Hydrogen) value for the management zone, representing average soil acidity or alkalinity on a 0-14 scale. Calculated from composite soil samples within the zone. Critical for nutrient availability assessment and lime application rate determination in VRA prescriptions. Optimal range for most crops is 6.0-7.0.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Health Assessment; ISO 10390 Soil Quality - pH Determination; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 4.2

description: USDA soil texture classification for the dominant soil type within the management zone, based on relative proportions of sand, silt, and clay particles. Determines water infiltration rate, water-holding capacity, and tillage characteristics. Used for irrigation scheduling and equipment operation planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: sand|loamy_sand|sandy_loam|loam|silt_loam|silt|sandy_clay_loam|clay_loam|silty_clay_loam|sandy_clay|silty_clay|clay — promote to reference product]
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Texture Triangle Classification; ISO 11277 Soil Particle Size Analysis

description: Operational system of record from which this management zone record was originated or last updated. Supports data lineage tracking and conflict resolution when zone data is synchronized across multiple precision agriculture platforms.
reference: Databricks Lakehouse Data Lineage Standards; ISO 8000 Data Quality

description: Timestamp when this management zone record was most recently modified in the lakehouse Silver Layer, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used to detect stale zone configurations and trigger re-synchronization with source precision agriculture systems.
reference: ISO 8601 Date and Time Standards; SOX Section 404 - Data Audit Trail; GDPR Article 5 - Data Integrity

description: Indicates whether this management zone is eligible for variable rate application (VRA) prescription generation in Trimble Ag Software or John Deere Operations Center. Zones must meet minimum area thresholds and have current soil data to qualify for VRA. True = eligible for VRA prescriptions; False = not eligible.
reference: Trimble Ag Software - VRA Prescription Rules; John Deere Operations Center - Prescription Management

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the management zone within the farm management information system (FMIS). Used as the business key in Trimble Ag Software and John Deere Operations Center for variable rate application (VRA) prescription generation.
reference: Trimble Ag Software - Zone Management; John Deere Operations Center Field Mapping

description: Human-readable descriptive name assigned to the management zone (e.g., 'North Field High Productivity Zone', 'EC Zone 3 - Sandy Loam'). Used in FMIS reporting and VRA prescription labeling.
reference: Trimble Ag Software - Zone Management; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 1.1

description: Current lifecycle status of the management zone. Active zones are used in current-season VRA prescriptions; inactive zones are temporarily suspended; archived zones are retained for historical analysis; draft zones are pending agronomist review and approval.
reference: Granular Farm Management - Zone Lifecycle; GLOBALG.A.P. CB 1.1

description: Classification of the zone based on the primary agronomic criterion used to define it. Soil type zones are delineated by soil series; EC (Electrical Conductivity) zones by apparent soil EC readings; yield zones by multi-year yield history; topographic zones by elevation and slope; NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) zones by satellite-derived vegetation index; management zones by operator-defined boundaries.
reference: Trimble Ag Software - Zone Types; USDA NRCS Soil Survey; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

description: Sequential version number of the management zone boundary definition, incremented each time the zone polygon or classification attributes are revised. Supports audit trail and historical comparison of zone configurations across growing seasons.
reference: Granular Farm Management - Data Versioning; ISO 14001 Environmental Records Management

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the legal land parcel record in the enterprise data platform (Silver Layer primary key).
reference: ISO 19152 Land Administration Domain Model (LADM)

description: Reference to the operational farm unit to which this parcel is administratively assigned for crop planning, workforce, and equipment management.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) Farm Records

description: Total purchase price or capitalized cost at which the enterprise acquired fee-simple title to the parcel, recorded in USD for fixed asset accounting, CAPEX tracking, and land valuation analysis.
reference: GAAP ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment; IFRS IAS 16; SOX Financial Reporting Controls

description: Date the enterprise acquired operational control of the parcel (purchase closing date for owned parcels, lease commencement date for leased parcels), used for depreciation schedules, lease accounting (ASC 842), and tenure analysis.
reference: GAAP ASC 842 Lease Accounting; IFRS 16; USDA FSA Farm Records

description: Most recent annual property tax levy assessed by the county on this parcel in USD, used for OPEX budgeting, land cost-per-acre analysis, and financial planning in Granular Farm Management.
reference: County Tax Assessor; GAAP; IFRS; SOX Financial Reporting Controls

description: County assessor-assigned Assessor Parcel Number (APN) uniquely identifying the parcel within the county tax roll. Primary government-issued cadastral identifier used for title searches, deed recording, and property tax assessment.
reference: County Assessor / Land Registry; USDA NRCS Cadastral Standards

description: Unique feature identifier within the Esri ArcGIS parcel boundary layer, enabling direct linkage to the authoritative GIS polygon geometry for spatial analysis, field mapping, and environmental monitoring.
reference: Esri ArcGIS; ISO 19152 LADM; USDA NRCS Geospatial Data Gateway

description: County assessor's most recent assessed market value of the parcel in USD, used for property tax calculation, financial reporting, and land portfolio valuation.
reference: County Assessor; GAAP ASC 360; IFRS IAS 40 Investment Property

description: WGS84 decimal-degree latitude of the parcel centroid as derived from Esri ArcGIS or John Deere Operations Center RTK-accurate field mapping, used for geospatial analysis, weather data correlation, and GIS integration.
reference: Esri ArcGIS; John Deere Operations Center; WGS84 (EPSG:4326); ISO 6709

description: WGS84 decimal-degree longitude of the parcel centroid as derived from Esri ArcGIS or John Deere Operations Center RTK-accurate field mapping, used for geospatial analysis, weather data correlation, and GIS integration.
reference: Esri ArcGIS; John Deere Operations Center; WGS84 (EPSG:4326); ISO 6709

description: USDA FSA Common Land Unit (CLU) identifier — the smallest unit of land with a permanent, contiguous boundary used for farm program administration, acreage determination, and geospatial analysis.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) CLU Program; USDA NRCS Geospatial Data Gateway

description: USDA conservation program in which this parcel is currently enrolled (e.g., Conservation Reserve Program (CRP), Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP), Conservation Stewardship Program (CSP)), affecting land use restrictions and payment eligibility.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) Conservation Programs; USDA NRCS; 2018 Farm Bill

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 three-letter country code for the country in which the parcel is located, supporting international operations and Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) compliance.
reference: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; USDA COOL (Country of Origin Labeling) 7 CFR Part 60

description: Name of the county in which the parcel is physically located, used for tax jurisdiction, FSA county office assignment, regulatory compliance, and geospatial reporting.
reference: USDA FSA County Office Records; FIPS County Codes (FIPS 6-4)

description: Timestamp when the parcel record was first created in the enterprise data platform, used for data lineage, audit trail, and Silver Layer ingestion tracking.
reference: ISO 8601; SOX Internal Controls; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

description: County recorder deed book reference (book number or volume) where the current title instrument for this parcel is recorded, supporting title chain verification and encumbrance searches.
reference: County Recorder / Register of Deeds; ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey Standards

description: County recorder deed page reference within the deed book where the current title instrument is recorded, used in conjunction with deed_book for precise title document retrieval.
reference: County Recorder / Register of Deeds; ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey Standards

description: Date the current deed or title instrument was officially recorded with the county recorder, establishing the effective date of ownership transfer and priority in the title chain.
reference: County Recorder / Register of Deeds; ALTA/NSPS Land Title Survey Standards

description: FEMA National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) flood zone designation for the parcel, used for crop insurance underwriting, lender requirements, conservation planning, and drainage infrastructure investment decisions.
reference: FEMA National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP); FEMA Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRM); EPA

description: USDA FSA-determined cropland acres within the parcel eligible for commodity program enrollment, ARC/PLC payments, and conservation program base acre calculations.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) 7 CFR Part 718; USDA 2018 Farm Bill

description: USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) assigned farm number linking this parcel to the FSA farm record for program eligibility, commodity reporting, and conservation compliance.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) Farm Records; USDA 7 CFR Part 718

description: USDA FSA tract number subdividing the FSA farm into contiguous land units under common ownership or control, used for acreage reporting and program payment calculations.
reference: USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) Farm Records; USDA 7 CFR Part 718

description: Total acres within the parcel served by an irrigation system (surface, drip, pivot, or flood), used for water right allocation, irrigation scheduling, and USDA program reporting.
reference: USDA NRCS Irrigation Water Management; State Water Resources Control Board

description: Primary land use classification for the parcel as designated by the county assessor or USDA FSA, determining eligible farm programs, conservation requirements, and operational planning. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: cropland|pasture|rangeland|woodland|wetland|farmstead|idle|conservation|orchard|vineyard|fallow — promote to reference product]
reference: USDA NRCS Land Use Classification; USDA FSA 7 CFR Part 718; ISO 19152 LADM

description: Full legal description of the parcel as recorded in the county deed or land registry, including metes-and-bounds, lot-block-subdivision, or Public Land Survey System (PLSS) section-township-range narrative.
reference: County Recorder / Register of Deeds; USDA NRCS PLSS Standards

description: USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) land capability class (I–VIII) and subclass (e, w, s, c) rating the parcel's suitability for cultivation, indicating erosion risk, drainage limitations, and conservation treatment needs.
reference: USDA NRCS Land Capability Classification System; USDA Agriculture Handbook 210

description: Current USDA National Organic Program (NOP) certification status of the parcel, indicating whether the land meets organic production requirements, is in the 3-year transition period, or is managed under conventional practices.
reference: USDA National Organic Program (NOP) 7 CFR Part 205; GLOBALG.A.P. Organic Standard

description: Date on which the parcel began the USDA NOP-required 36-month transition period from conventional to certified organic production, used to track certification eligibility and compliance timelines.
reference: USDA National Organic Program (NOP) 7 CFR Part 205.202

description: Classification of the operational control arrangement for this parcel — whether the enterprise holds fee-simple title (owned), operates under a cash rent lease, crop-share lease, or custom farming agreement.
reference: USDA Economic Research Service (ERS) Farmland Tenure; GAAP ASC 842 Lease Accounting

description: Operational or colloquial name assigned to the parcel by the farm operation (e.g., 'North Quarter', 'River Bottom Field') for internal identification and communication.
reference: Granular Farm Management; USDA FMIS Best Practices

description: Current lifecycle status of the parcel record indicating its operational and administrative state within the enterprise land management system.
reference: ISO 19152 LADM; Granular Farm Management

description: Range designation (e.g., R5E) within the PLSS grid, representing the east-west position relative to a principal meridian.
reference: USDA NRCS PLSS; Bureau of Land Management (BLM) General Land Office Records

description: Section number (1–36) within the Public Land Survey System (PLSS) township-range grid identifying the one-square-mile land division containing this parcel.
reference: USDA NRCS PLSS; Bureau of Land Management (BLM) General Land Office Records

description: Township designation (e.g., T12N) within the PLSS grid, representing the north-south position relative to a principal meridian baseline.
reference: USDA NRCS PLSS; Bureau of Land Management (BLM) General Land Office Records

description: USDA NRCS prime farmland classification indicating the land's capability for sustained agricultural production, used for conservation program eligibility (ACEP, RCPP), environmental impact assessments, and land use planning.
reference: USDA NRCS Prime Farmland Policy (7 CFR Part 657); USDA NRCS Land Capability Classification

description: USDA NRCS Web Soil Survey map unit symbol (e.g., 'HrA', 'MnB2') identifying the dominant soil series and slope class for the parcel, used for soil health planning, conservation program eligibility, and variable rate application (VRA) prescriptions.
reference: USDA NRCS Web Soil Survey; USDA SSURGO Database

description: Two-letter USPS state abbreviation for the state in which the parcel is located, used for regulatory jurisdiction, FSA state office routing, and geospatial classification.
reference: USPS State Abbreviations; FIPS 5-2 State Codes; USDA FSA

description: Total land area of the parcel as recorded in the county deed or land registry, expressed in acres. Represents the legal boundary area and is the authoritative acreage for title, tax assessment, and FSA program enrollment.
reference: County Recorder / Register of Deeds; USDA FSA Acreage Reporting; USDA NRCS

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the parcel record in the enterprise data platform, supporting change data capture (CDC), audit compliance, and data freshness monitoring.
reference: ISO 8601; SOX Internal Controls; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

description: Flag indicating whether any portion of the parcel contains USDA NRCS-delineated wetlands subject to Swampbuster provisions (Food Security Act), EPA Section 404 permitting, and conservation program restrictions.
reference: USDA NRCS Wetland Conservation Provisions (Swampbuster) 7 CFR Part 12; EPA Clean Water Act Section 404

description: County or municipal zoning designation for the parcel (e.g., A-1 Agricultural, A-2 Rural Residential, EFU Exclusive Farm Use) governing permitted land uses, structure placement, and development rights.
reference: County Planning and Zoning Ordinances; USDA NRCS; EPA Land Use Regulations

description: Unique system-generated identifier for the soil profile record. Primary key for the soil_profile data product within the land domain.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Survey Manual

description: Reference to the agricultural field or parcel to which this soil profile belongs. Links the soil profile to its geographic land unit as mapped in Esri ArcGIS and John Deere Operations Center.
reference: Esri ArcGIS; John Deere Operations Center

description: Free-text field for certified crop adviser (CCA) or agronomist observations about this soil profile, including anomalies, historical land use context, or special management considerations not captured in structured fields. Supports GLOBALG.A.P. and USDA NRCS conservation planning documentation.
reference: GLOBALG.A.P.; USDA NRCS; American Society of Agronomy

description: Available Water Capacity (AWC) expressed as centimeters of water per centimeter of soil depth (cm/cm), representing the volume of water held between field capacity and permanent wilting point. Critical input for irrigation scheduling and evapotranspiration (ET) modeling.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Survey Manual; FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56

description: Soil bulk density expressed in grams per cubic centimeter (g/cm³), representing the mass of dry soil per unit volume including pore space. Indicates soil compaction level; values above 1.6 g/cm³ typically restrict root growth. Informs tillage and cover crop decisions.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Survey Laboratory Methods Manual; ISO 11272

description: Cation Exchange Capacity (CEC) expressed in milliequivalents per 100 grams of soil (meq/100g). Measures the soil's ability to hold and supply positively charged nutrient ions (Ca, Mg, K, Na). Higher CEC indicates greater nutrient-holding capacity and influences fertilizer recommendations.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Survey Laboratory Methods Manual; Soil Science Society of America

description: USDA NRCS Conservation Practice Standard code(s) applied to this soil mapping unit (e.g., 340 Cover Crop, 600 Terrace, 412 Grassed Waterway). Supports EQIP/CSP program documentation, BMP compliance reporting, and ISO 14001 environmental management system records.
reference: USDA NRCS Conservation Practice Standards; EQIP; CSP; ISO 14001

description: Timestamp when this soil profile record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports data lineage, audit trail, and FSMA traceability requirements.
reference: FSMA; ISO 22000; GLOBALG.A.P.; SOX

description: Depth in centimeters from the soil surface to the first restrictive layer (e.g., fragipan, claypan, bedrock, seasonal high water table). Limits effective rooting depth and influences crop selection, drainage tile placement, and irrigation design.
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Survey Manual; SSURGO

description: USDA NRCS drainage class describing the natural soil drainage condition (e.g., well drained, poorly drained). Critical for tile drainage design, planting date decisions, and ISO 14001 environmental management. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: excessively drained|somewhat excessively drained|well drained|moderately well drained|somewhat poorly drained|poorly drained|very poorly drained — promote to reference product]
reference: USDA NRCS Soil Survey Manual; ISO 14001

description: Soil electrical conductivity (EC) measured in deciSiemens per meter (dS/m), indicating soil salinity level. Values above 4 dS/m may indicate salinity stress for most crops. Used for precision agriculture zone delineation and irrigation water quality management.
reference: USDA NRCS; FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Qualitative erosion risk classification for this soil profile based on USDA NRCS Universal Soil Loss Equation (USLE/RUSLE) factors including erodibility (K-factor), slope, and cover. Drives conservation practice selection and FSMA Produce Safety Rule compliance for water quality.
reference: USDA NRCS RUSLE2; EPA; FSMA Produce Safety Rule

description: Area of the soil mapping unit or management zone in hectares as calculated from the GIS polygon in Esri ArcGIS. Used for proportional nutrient application calculations, yield per acre metric (YPM) normalization, and land valuation.
reference: Esri ArcGIS; USDA NRCS SSURGO; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this soil is classified as a hydric soil by USDA NRCS criteria, meaning it formed under conditions of saturation, flooding, or ponding long enough to develop anaerobic conditions. Hydric soils are associated with wetlands and trigger regulatory review under Section 404 of the Clean Water Act and USDA NRCS wetland conservation provisions.
reference: USDA NRCS Hydric Soils List; Clean Water Act Section 404; USDA Farm Bill Wetland Conservation

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this soil mapping unit is designated as Prime Farmland, Farmland of Statewide Importance, or Unique Farmland by USDA NRCS. Prime farmland designation affects land use planning, conservation program eligibility (CRP, EQIP), and regulatory review for development.
reference: USDA NRCS; Farmland Protection Policy Act (FPPA); 7 CFR Part 658

description: USDA NRCS soil erodibility K-factor from the Universal Soil Loss Equation (USLE/RUSLE), ranging from 0.02 (least erodible) to 0.69 (most erodible). Quantifies the susceptibility of soil to detachment and transport by rainfall and runoff. Used in conservation planning and NRCS EQIP program applications.
reference: USDA NRCS RUSLE2; USDA Agricultural Handbook 703

description: External laboratory sample reference or accession number assigned by the certified soil testing laboratory. Enables traceability back to the original Certificate of Analysis (COA) and laboratory report for audit and GLOBALG.A.P. compliance verification.
reference: GLOBALG.A.P.; ISO/IEC 17025 (Laboratory Accreditation); USDA AMS

description: USDA NRCS Land Capability Classification (LCC) rating from Class I (fewest limitations) to Class VIII (unsuitable for cultivation). Used for conservation planning, crop insurance rating, and USDA program eligibility determination. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: I|II|III|IV|V|VI|VII|VIII — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: USDA NRCS Land Capability Classification; USDA FSA

description: USDA NRCS Land Capability Subclass modifier indicating the primary limitation type: 'e' (erosion), 'w' (wetness/drainage), 's' (soil limitations), 'c' (climate). Complements the land_capability_class for conservation practice planning under BMP guidelines.
reference: USDA NRCS Land Capability Classification

description: Agronomic management zone designation within the field (e.g., 'Zone 1 - High Productivity', 'Zone 3 - Low OM'). Used for variable rate application (VRA) prescriptions in Trimble Ag Software and Climate FieldView to optimize input use efficiency.
reference: Trimble Ag Software; Climate FieldView; USDA NRCS

description: USDA NRCS SSURGO (Soil Survey Geographic Database) Map Unit Key (MUKEY) — the unique national identifier for the soil map unit polygon. Enables direct linkage to the SSURGO database for detailed soil property lookup, Web Soil Survey integration, and NRCS program eligibility verification.
reference: USDA NRCS SSURGO; Web Soil Survey

description: Plant-available nitrogen (N) concentration in the soil expressed in parts per million (ppm), typically measured as nitrate-N or ammonium-N. Core component of NPK (Nitrogen-Phosphorus-Potassium) soil fertility assessment driving fertilization event planning.
reference: USDA NRCS; Soil Science Society of America; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Official USDA NRCS soil series name assigned to this mapping unit (e.g., 'Drummer', 'Tama', 'Clarion'). Derived from the SSURGO/Web Soil Survey database and used for agronomic benchmarking and land valuation.
reference: USDA NRCS SSURGO; Web Soil Survey

reference: GFSI Benchmarking Requirements v2020; SQF Code Edition 9; BRC Global Standard Issue 9; IFS Food Version 7; GLOBALG.A.P. IFA v6

description: Indicates whether this sample was collected as part of HACCP (Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points) critical control point monitoring or verification activities. True requires enhanced documentation and regulatory retention per FSMA Preventive Controls rule. Aligns with HACCP business jargon.
reference: HACCP Principle 4 - Monitoring CCPs; FSMA 21 CFR Part 117 Subpart C; Codex Alimentarius HACCP Guidelines

description: Human-readable batch or lot tracking identifier associated with the sampled material. Denormalized from the commodity lot for direct COA reporting and regulatory submission without requiring a join. Aligns with LOT (Lot Number) business jargon.
reference: FSMA Subpart S Traceability Rule; FDA 21 CFR Part 1 - Lot Traceability; USDA AMS

description: Indicates whether any test parameter in this sample exceeded the applicable Maximum Residue Limit (MRL) as defined by EPA, Codex Alimentarius, or customer specification. True triggers non-conformance workflow and regulatory notification procedures. Aligns with MRL business jargon.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 180 - Pesticide Tolerances; Codex Alimentarius MRL Database; EU Regulation 396/2005

description: Consolidated pass/fail determination for the sample based on all test parameters in the requested panel against defined acceptance criteria. Pass: all parameters within specification; Fail: one or more parameters exceeded MRL or acceptance threshold; Inconclusive: results require further review; Pending: testing not yet complete.
reference: SAP S/4HANA QM - Usage Decision; HACCP CCP Acceptance Criteria; MRL (Maximum Residue Limit) Compliance

description: Indicates whether the sample collection date was verified to be after the required Pre-Harvest Interval (PHI) for any applied crop protection products. True confirms PHI compliance at time of sampling. Critical for pesticide residue MRL compliance. Aligns with PHI business jargon.
reference: EPA FIFRA PHI Requirements; USDA AMS Pesticide Data Program; GLOBALG.A.P. IFA v6 CB 7.6.4

description: Date and time when the sample was officially received and logged at the testing laboratory. Used to calculate sample transit time, assess sample integrity, and enforce holding time limits per analytical method requirements.
reference: ISO/IEC 17025 Section 7.4 - Sample Handling; FDA Laboratory Accreditation

description: Target date by which laboratory testing and result reporting must be completed. Drives laboratory scheduling, SLA monitoring, and release-hold decisions for production lots awaiting quality clearance.
reference: SAP S/4HANA QM - Inspection Deadline; HACCP Verification Turnaround Requirements

description: Date and time when the laboratory officially released the test results and COA. Marks the completion of the testing lifecycle and triggers downstream quality disposition workflows in SAP QM.
reference: SAP S/4HANA QM - Usage Decision Timestamp; ISO/IEC 17025 Section 7.8

description: Assessment of the physical condition of the sample upon receipt at the laboratory. Acceptable: sample integrity maintained; Compromised: minor integrity issues noted but testing may proceed with caveats; Rejected: sample integrity failed, testing cannot proceed. Drives chain-of-custody decisions.
reference: ISO/IEC 17025 Section 7.4.2 - Sample Condition Assessment; FSMA Chain of Custody

description: Free-text field for additional observations, anomalies, or contextual information recorded at the time of sample collection or receipt. Captures field conditions, equipment calibration notes, or deviations from standard sampling protocol that may affect result interpretation.
reference: ISO/IEC 17025 Section 7.4.2; HACCP Monitoring Records; FSMA Preventive Controls Documentation

description: Externally-known, human-readable unique identifier assigned to the sample at collection or submission. Used for chain-of-custody documentation, COA traceability, and communication with external laboratories. Follows enterprise sample numbering convention (e.g., LAB-2024-000123).
reference: SAP S/4HANA QM Module - Inspection Lot Number; FSMA Subpart O Sampling Plan

description: Measured quantity of material collected for the sample (e.g., weight in grams, volume in milliliters). Used to verify adequacy of sample size per analytical method requirements and sampling plan specifications.
reference: AOAC Sampling Procedures; SAP S/4HANA QM - Sample Quantity; ISO/IEC 17025

description: Unit of measure for the sample quantity field. Standard units include grams (g), kilograms (kg), milliliters (mL), liters (L), milligrams (mg), and ounces (oz). Must align with the unit specified in the analytical method.
reference: SAP S/4HANA QM - Unit of Measure; ISO/IEC 17025 Section 7.4

description: Current lifecycle status of the laboratory sample from submission through disposition. Drives workflow routing in SAP QM and laboratory tracking systems. Values: submitted (collected and logged), received (confirmed at lab), in_testing (analysis underway), completed (results available), rejected (sample failed receipt criteria), disposed (sample destroyed or returned per protocol).
reference: SAP S/4HANA QM Module - Usage Decision; ISO/IEC 17025

description: Classification of the physical material collected for laboratory analysis. Determines applicable analytical methods, acceptance criteria, and regulatory reporting requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: grain|soil|water|tissue|feed|environmental_swab|air|product — promote to reference product]
reference: USDA AMS Sampling Procedures; FDA FSMA Environmental Monitoring; HACCP CCP Classification

description: Classification of why this sample was collected relative to the sampling plan schedule. Routine: scheduled periodic sampling; Triggered: collected in response to an event or non-conformance; Regulatory: mandated by USDA/FDA/EPA inspection; Verification: HACCP verification sampling; Validation: process or method validation sampling.
reference: HACCP Principle 6 - Verification; FSMA Preventive Controls Verification; GLOBALG.A.P. IFA v6

description: Temperature in degrees Celsius at which the sample was stored during transit and prior to analysis. Critical for maintaining sample integrity for microbiological and chemical analyses. Deviations may invalidate results per ISO/IEC 17025 requirements.
reference: ISO/IEC 17025 Section 7.4.2; FDA BAM Chapter 1 - Sample Handling; HACCP Cold Chain

description: System timestamp of the most recent modification to the lab sample record. Supports incremental data processing in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver layer and audit trail requirements.
reference: SOX Section 404 - Data Integrity Controls; ISO 22000 Record Management

Estimated annual cost in USD to maintain compliance with this quality standard, including audit fees, certification fees, testing costs, training expenses, and internal labor. Used for budgeting and cost-benefit analysis of quality programs.

Comma-separated list of facility or operation types to which this quality standard applies (e.g., farm, packing house, processing plant, cold storage, distribution center, retail). Defines the scope of operations covered.

Comma-separated list of product categories or commodity groups to which this quality standard applies (e.g., fresh produce, dairy, meat and poultry, processed foods, animal feed, packaging materials). Defines the scope of products covered.
Required frequency for third-party audits or internal assessments against this quality standard, expressed in months (e.g., 12 for annual, 24 for biennial). Null if no periodic audit is required.

Name of the accredited organization that issues or governs this quality standard (e.g., SQFI, BRC Global Standards, IFS Management GmbH, GLOBALG.A.P. c/o FoodPLUS GmbH, NSF International, SGS, Bureau Veritas). Null for internal or non-certified standards.

Validity period of certification issued under this quality standard, expressed in months (e.g., 12, 24, 36). After this period, recertification audit is required. Null for non-certification standards.

Maximum number of days allowed to implement corrective actions for non-conformances identified during audits or assessments under this quality standard. Timeframe varies by severity of finding (e.g., 30 days for major, 90 days for minor).
Comma-separated list of ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country codes where this quality standard is applicable or recognized (e.g., USA, CAN, MEX, DEU, GBR, CHN). Null for global standards applicable everywhere.
Timestamp when this quality standard record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

Maximum number of critical non-conformances allowed before automatic failure of audit or assessment. Critical defects are findings that pose immediate food safety risk or regulatory violation. Zero tolerance is common for many food safety standards.

Description of mandatory documentation, records, and evidence that must be maintained to demonstrate compliance with this quality standard (e.g., HACCP plans, SOPs, training records, COA files, corrective action logs, supplier approvals).
Date when this version of the quality standard becomes enforceable or recommended for adoption. Organizations must comply with the standard from this date forward for new certifications or audits.
Date when this version of the quality standard is superseded or retired. After this date, organizations must transition to the next version. Null for standards with indefinite validity.

Geographic applicability of the quality standard. Global standards apply worldwide (ISO, GFSI schemes), regional standards apply to multi-country regions (EU regulations), national standards apply to a single country (USDA, FDA), state standards apply to sub-national jurisdictions, and local standards apply to specific municipalities or districts.

Indicates whether this quality standard is benchmarked and recognized by the Global Food Safety Initiative (GFSI). GFSI recognition is a key requirement for many global retailers and food manufacturers. True if GFSI-recognized, false otherwise.

Name of the internal department or business unit responsible for managing compliance with this quality standard (e.g., Quality Assurance, Food Safety, Regulatory Affairs, Operations). Used for accountability and audit coordination.

Regulatory or governing body that mandates or oversees the standard (e.g., USDA, FDA, FSIS, European Commission, Codex Alimentarius, state agriculture departments). Applicable for regulatory and industry standards.

Date when this quality standard was last reviewed by internal quality management team for continued applicability, accuracy, and alignment with business needs. Used to ensure master data currency and trigger periodic reviews.
Timestamp when this quality standard record was most recently modified. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data freshness monitoring.

Maximum number of major non-conformances allowed before failure of audit or assessment. Major defects are significant deviations from standard requirements that could lead to food safety issues if not corrected.

Minimum audit score or compliance percentage required to achieve certification or pass assessment under this quality standard (e.g., 80.00 for 80% compliance). Null if the standard does not use numeric scoring.

Scheduled date for the next periodic review of this quality standard record. Used to trigger proactive review workflows and ensure master data remains current with evolving regulatory and industry requirements.

Free-text field for additional information, special considerations, implementation guidance, or historical context related to this quality standard. Used to capture nuances not covered by structured fields.
Web URL link to the official published standard document, guidance materials, or certification body website where the full standard text and requirements can be accessed.

Indicates whether compliance with this quality standard is legally required by government regulation (e.g., FSMA Preventive Controls, HACCP for seafood and juice). True if mandated by law, false if voluntary or industry-driven.

Detailed description of what the quality standard covers, including applicable products, processes, facilities, and supply chain stages. Defines the boundaries of compliance requirements and audit scope.

Primary functional category of the quality standard. Food safety covers pathogen control and contamination prevention (HACCP, FSMA), quality management covers systematic quality assurance (ISO 9001, SQF), good agricultural practices cover on-farm production (GLOBALG.A.P.), good manufacturing practices cover processing facility operations (GMP, cGMP), hazard analysis covers risk assessment methodologies (HACCP principles), and traceability covers supply chain tracking (PTI, FSMA 204).
Unique business identifier code for the quality standard (e.g., SQF-2000, BRC-8, IFS-7, HACCP-001, GAP-V5). Used for external reference and certification documentation.
Full official name of the quality standard (e.g., Safe Quality Food Level 2, British Retail Consortium Global Standard for Food Safety, International Featured Standards Food).

Classification of the quality standard by its origin and enforcement mechanism. Certification standards are third-party verified (GFSI schemes), regulatory are government-mandated (FDA, USDA, FSIS), internal are company-defined, industry are sector-wide best practices, customer-specific are buyer requirements, and voluntary are optional compliance frameworks.

Current lifecycle status of the quality standard. Active standards are in force and enforceable, superseded standards have been replaced by newer versions, draft standards are under development, under review standards are being evaluated for adoption, retired standards are no longer applicable, and suspended standards are temporarily not enforced.

Description of supplier qualification, approval, and monitoring requirements mandated by this quality standard (e.g., supplier audits, COA review, risk-based supplier verification, FSMA Foreign Supplier Verification Program requirements).

Description of mandatory testing, sampling, and analytical methods required by this quality standard (e.g., pathogen testing frequency, MRL testing protocols, environmental monitoring programs, finished product testing specifications).

Description of traceability and supply chain tracking requirements mandated by this quality standard (e.g., one-up/one-back traceability, lot coding requirements, recall readiness, FSMA 204 Key Data Elements for high-risk foods).

Description of mandatory training programs and competency requirements for personnel involved in activities covered by this quality standard (e.g., HACCP training for food safety team, GMP training for production staff, auditor qualification requirements).
Version or edition number of the quality standard (e.g., 8.0, 7.1, V5.2). Quality standards are periodically revised to incorporate new science, regulatory changes, and industry best practices.

description: Timestamp when the carrier master record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports data lineage, audit trail, and FSMA record-keeping requirements.

description: Rolling ratio of shipments resulting in a cargo damage claim to total shipments executed. Used to assess carrier handling quality for sensitive agricultural commodities and inform carrier tier scoring.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Vendor Evaluation; USDA Agricultural Marketing Act

description: Indicates whether the carrier supports EDI transaction sets (e.g., 204 Motor Carrier Load Tender, 214 Shipment Status, 210 Freight Invoice) for automated load tendering and status updates in the agricultural supply chain.

business_glossary_term: Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) Certification Expiry Date

reference: FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart O; FDA

business_glossary_term: Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) Sanitary Transportation Certified
description: Indicates whether the carrier holds a valid FSMA Sanitary Transportation of Human and Animal Food certification (21 CFR Part 1, Subpart O). Mandatory for carriers transporting food-grade agricultural products to food manufacturers.

business_glossary_term: Global Positioning System (GPS) Real-Time Tracking Capability Flag
description: Indicates whether the carrier provides real-time GPS-based shipment location tracking integrated with the TMS for visibility into in-transit agricultural commodity shipments.

description: Indicates whether the carrier holds USDOT hazardous materials (HAZMAT) certification for transporting regulated agricultural inputs such as pesticides, fertilizers, and fumigants with Safety Data Sheet (SDS) requirements.

description: Expiration date of the carrier's current insurance certificate (cargo liability, general liability, and auto liability). Carrier is ineligible for load assignment if this date has passed. Monitored for proactive renewal alerts.

Enables site managers to flag carriers that perform well globally but poorly at their specific location.

reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Vendor Evaluation; GLOBALG.A.P. Supply Chain Standard

description: Comma-delimited list of preferred origin-destination lane codes (e.g., 'MIDWEST-SOUTHEAST', 'CA-TX') where this carrier has committed capacity or preferred routing agreements. Used by TMS for primary carrier selection in route optimization.

reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Vendor Master

reference: GDPR Article 4; SAP S/4HANA MM Vendor Master

reference: SAP S/4HANA TMS; Manhattan Associates WMS

reference: SAP S/4HANA TMS; Manhattan Associates WMS

description: Rolling ratio of cold chain shipments where a temperature excursion (deviation outside the specified range) was recorded to total cold chain shipments. Critical metric for FSMA compliance and food safety risk management.
reference: FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule 21 CFR Part 1; ISO 22000 Food Safety Management

description: Cumulative count of shipments executed by this carrier within the current evaluation period. Provides volume context for interpreting rate-based KPIs (on-time, damage, temperature excursion) in carrier performance analysis.
reference: SAP S/4HANA TMS; Manhattan Associates WMS

reference: FMCSA Carrier Registration

reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

reference: Internal - M:N Association Attribute

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each carrier performance evaluation record in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: Internal Data Architecture Standard

reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Vendor Master; FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule 21 CFR Part 1

description: Foreign key linking to compliance.compliance_audit. Business justification: Carrier performance evaluations in agriculture incorporate results from compliance audits (FSMA sanitary transport audits, cold chain audits, GFSI audits). Linking carrier_performance to compliance_au
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Carrier performance evaluations in agriculture logistics are conducted by qualified logistics managers or procurement staff. Linking to the evaluating employee enables accountability reporting, evalua
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the active carrier rate agreement or 3PL contract under which the evaluated shipments were executed. Links to the contract master in SAP S/4HANA MM.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Contract Management; Internal Procurement Policy

description: Average actual transit time in hours across all shipments executed by the carrier during the evaluation period. Compared against contracted transit time to assess schedule adherence.
reference: Internal Supply Chain KPI Framework; SAP S/4HANA TM

business_glossary_term: Bill of Lading (BOL) Documentation Accuracy Rate
description: Percentage of Bills of Lading (BOL) submitted by the carrier that were complete, accurate, and compliant with FSMA traceability requirements during the evaluation period.
reference: FSMA Traceability Rule 21 CFR Part 1; ANSI ASC X12 EDI 211; SAP S/4HANA SD

description: Percentage of carrier freight invoices that matched the contracted rate without dispute during the evaluation period. Supports freight audit and payment (FAP) processes in SAP S/4HANA FI-AP.
reference: Internal Freight Audit and Payment Policy; SAP S/4HANA FI-AP

description: Number of shipments within the evaluation period that required temperature-controlled transport (cold chain). Used as the denominator for temperature excursion rate calculations.
reference: FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule 21 CFR Part 1; FDA Food Safety Modernization Act

description: Weighted composite score (0-100) aggregating all KPI dimensions (on-time delivery, damage claims, FSMA compliance, temperature excursions, invoice accuracy) into a single carrier scorecard value. Basis for performance_tier assignment.
reference: Internal Carrier Scorecard Methodology; GLOBALG.A.P. Supply Chain Assurance

description: Agreed transit time in hours as specified in the carrier contract or rate agreement for the evaluated lane. Baseline for transit time variance analysis and SLA compliance.
reference: Internal Carrier Contract Management; SAP S/4HANA MM Contract Management

description: Timestamp when the carrier performance evaluation record was first created in the Databricks Silver Layer. Audit trail field aligned with SOX data lineage requirements.
reference: SOX Section 404; GDPR Article 5; Internal Data Governance Policy

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the total_freight_cost field (e.g., USD, EUR, BRL). Supports multi-currency agricultural export operations.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IFRS; GAAP

description: Number of shipments for which a cargo damage claim was filed against the carrier during the evaluation period. Raw numerator for damage claim rate. Impacts food safety and HACCP compliance assessments.
reference: Internal Supply Chain KPI Framework; HACCP Principles; GFSI Standards

description: Percentage of shipments resulting in a cargo damage claim during the evaluation period. Calculated as (damage_claim_count / total_shipments) * 100. Critical for food safety compliance and insurance cost management.
reference: Internal Supply Chain KPI Framework; HACCP Principles; GFSI Standards; ISO 22000

description: Last date of the performance evaluation window. Together with evaluation_period_start_date defines the measurement interval for all KPI metrics in this record.
reference: Internal Supply Chain KPI Framework; GLOBALG.A.P. Supply Chain Assurance

description: First date of the performance evaluation window (e.g., start of month, quarter, or contract review period). Used to define the measurement interval for all KPI calculations.
reference: Internal Supply Chain KPI Framework; GLOBALG.A.P. Supply Chain Assurance

description: Granularity of the performance evaluation cycle. Determines the reporting cadence for carrier scorecards and 3PL contract renewal reviews.
reference: Internal Supply Chain KPI Framework

description: Workflow status of the carrier performance evaluation record. Draft: data being compiled; Under Review: pending analyst approval; Approved: scorecard finalized; Published: shared with carrier.
reference: Internal Supply Chain Governance; SOX Internal Controls

business_glossary_term: Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) Audit Date
description: Date of the most recent FSMA sanitary transportation compliance audit conducted for this carrier. Tracks audit currency for regulatory compliance management.
reference: FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule 21 CFR Part 1; FDA Food Safety Modernization Act

business_glossary_term: Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) Compliance Score
description: Composite score (0-100) measuring the carrier's adherence to FSMA Sanitary Transportation of Human and Animal Food rule requirements, including vehicle sanitation, temperature control documentation, and training records. Mandatory for food-grade agricultural shipments.
reference: FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule 21 CFR Part 1; FDA Food Safety Modernization Act; GFSI Standards

description: Indicates whether the carrier is currently operating under a formal Carrier Improvement Plan (CIP) due to performance deficiencies. True when a corrective action plan is in force; False otherwise.
reference: Internal Carrier Management Policy; ISO 9001 Corrective Action

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the destination end of the primary evaluated shipping lane. Used for cross-border compliance checks and lane performance analytics.
reference: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; USDA COOL Regulations 7 CFR Part 60

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the origin end of the primary evaluated shipping lane. Supports COOL (Country of Origin Labeling) compliance and lane-level performance segmentation.
reference: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; USDA COOL Regulations 7 CFR Part 60

description: Number of shipments delivered within the contracted delivery window during the evaluation period. Raw numerator for on-time delivery rate calculation.
reference: Internal Supply Chain KPI Framework; SAP S/4HANA TM

description: Percentage of shipments delivered within the contracted delivery window during the evaluation period. Calculated as (on_time_delivery_count / total_shipments) * 100. Primary KPI for carrier selection and 3PL contract renewals.
reference: Internal Supply Chain KPI Framework; GLOBALG.A.P. Supply Chain Assurance; FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule

description: Number of shipments where the carrier completed pickup within the contracted pickup window during the evaluation period. Raw numerator for on-time pickup rate calculation.
reference: Internal Supply Chain KPI Framework; SAP S/4HANA TM

description: Percentage of shipments where the carrier completed pickup within the contracted pickup window during the evaluation period. Calculated as (on_time_pickup_count / total_shipments) * 100. Key carrier KPI for agricultural supply chain reliability.
reference: Internal Supply Chain KPI Framework; GLOBALG.A.P. Supply Chain Assurance

description: Overall performance classification assigned to the carrier based on composite KPI scores for the evaluation period. Drives carrier selection priority in TMS route planning and 3PL contract renewal decisions. Values: preferred (top-tier, priority allocation), approved (meets standards), probation (below threshold, improvement plan required), suspended (disqualified from new loads).
reference: Internal Carrier Management Policy; GLOBALG.A.P. Supply Chain Assurance; GFSI Standards

description: Performance tier assigned to the carrier in the immediately preceding evaluation period. Enables tier trend analysis and escalation/de-escalation tracking for carrier management decisions.
reference: Internal Carrier Management Policy

description: Number of loads rejected by the carrier (carrier-caused refusals) or rejected at destination due to carrier-attributable non-conformances (e.g., temperature breach, contamination) during the evaluation period.
reference: Internal Supply Chain KPI Framework; FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule 21 CFR Part 1; HACCP

business_glossary_term: Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) Tracking Compliance Rate
description: Percentage of shipments where the carrier maintained continuous RFID tag scan compliance at all required checkpoints during the evaluation period. Supports FSMA traceability lot (LOT) tracking requirements.
reference: FSMA Traceability Rule 21 CFR Part 1; FDA Food Safety Modernization Act; GS1 RFID Standards

description: Operational system of record from which the carrier performance data was sourced (e.g., SAP S/4HANA TM, Manhattan Associates WMS). Supports data lineage and Silver Layer provenance tracking.
reference: Internal Data Governance Policy; Databricks Lakehouse Architecture Standards

description: Number of cold chain shipments where the carrier recorded a temperature excursion outside the contracted min/max range during the evaluation period. Raw numerator for temperature excursion rate.
reference: FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule 21 CFR Part 1; FDA Food Safety Modernization Act; ISO 22000

description: Percentage of cold chain shipments with a temperature excursion during the evaluation period. Calculated as (temp_excursion_count / cold_chain_shipments) * 100. Critical KPI for perishable agricultural commodity carriers under FSMA cold chain rules.
reference: FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule 21 CFR Part 1; FDA Food Safety Modernization Act; ISO 22000

description: Total freight charges invoiced by the carrier for all shipments executed during the evaluation period, in the reporting currency. Used for COGS allocation, carrier spend analysis, and contract benchmarking.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-CO; GAAP; IFRS 15

description: Total number of shipments executed by the carrier within the evaluation period. Serves as the denominator for all rate-based KPI calculations and statistical significance assessment.
reference: Internal Supply Chain KPI Framework; Manhattan Associates TMS

description: Difference between avg_transit_time_hours and contracted_transit_time_hours. Positive values indicate the carrier is running late on average; negative values indicate early delivery. Key input for route optimization and carrier negotiations.
reference: Internal Supply Chain KPI Framework

description: Primary mode of transportation used by the carrier for the evaluated shipment lanes (e.g., truck for domestic grain hauls, ocean for export containers). Aligns with BOL and AWB classification in SAP S/4HANA SD.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Transportation; INCOTERMS 2020; FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to the carrier performance evaluation record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Supports incremental data processing and audit trail requirements.
reference: SOX Section 404; GDPR Article 5; Internal Data Governance Policy

description: Total of all accessorial charges billed on this invoice, including but not limited to liftgate, inside delivery, residential delivery, hazmat handling, and temperature-controlled service premiums. Aggregated accessorial total; line-level detail captured in freight_invoice_line.
