description: SAP FI accounts payable document number assigned when the freight invoice is posted in the general ledger. Links the freight invoice to the financial accounting entry for payment processing and audit trail.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI — Accounting Document (BKPF-BELNR); GAAP; SOX Section 404

description: The amount approved for payment after freight audit and dispute resolution. May differ from invoice_total_amount when a variance is resolved in favor of the shipper. This is the amount that will be remitted to the carrier.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI — Approved Invoice Amount; GAAP AP; SOX Section 404

description: Status of the freight audit process specifically — distinct from overall invoice_status. Tracks whether the invoice charges have been validated against contracted rates and BOL details. 'pending' = not yet audited; 'in_review' = audit underway; 'matched' = charges match contracted rates; 'disputed' = discrepancy found; 'resolved' = dispute closed.
reference: GAAP Internal Controls; SOX Section 404; SAP S/4HANA MM Invoice Verification (MIRO)

description: Air Waybill number for air freight shipments referenced on this invoice. Nullable; populated only when transport mode is air freight. Serves as the air equivalent of the BOL for invoice matching.
reference: IATA Air Waybill Standards; SAP S/4HANA MM Foreign Trade

description: Core transportation charge billed by the carrier before surcharges and accessorials. Represents the line-haul rate applied to the shipment weight, distance, or commodity class. Primary component of total freight cost.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Condition Type (KOFI); GAAP COGS Classification; Uniform Freight Classification

description: Bill of Lading number referenced on this freight invoice. Used to match the carrier invoice against the shipment document for three-way match validation. A BOL is the legal contract between shipper and carrier.
reference: 49 CFR Part 373 — Bills of Lading; FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule; SAP S/4HANA SD/MM

description: Expected freight charge based on the negotiated carrier contract or rate confirmation for this lane and service type. Used as the benchmark in three-way match and freight audit to identify billing variances.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Purchasing Info Record / Rate Confirmation; GAAP; SOX AP Controls

description: Timestamp when this freight invoice record was first created in the system of record. Provides the audit trail creation marker for SOX compliance and data lineage tracking in the silver layer.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI — Document Entry Date (CPUDT); SOX Section 404; GAAP Audit Trail

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts on this freight invoice (e.g., USD, CAD, EUR, MXN). All amount fields are denominated in this currency.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SAP S/4HANA FI — Currency Key (WAERS); IFRS; GAAP

description: Charges billed for detention (truck waiting at shipper/consignee beyond free time) or demurrage (rail car or container held beyond allowed dwell time). Common in agricultural supply chains during harvest peak periods.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Detention Condition Type; 49 CFR Part 370; GAAP

description: Reason code or description for why this freight invoice is in disputed status. Populated when audit_status = 'disputed'. Common reasons include rate mismatch, duplicate invoice, incorrect weight, unauthorized accessorial, or service failure. Nullable when no dispute exists.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Invoice Verification — Blocking Reason; GAAP AP Dispute Management

description: Date on which a freight invoice dispute was formally resolved with the carrier. Nullable; populated only when a dispute has been closed. Used to measure dispute cycle time and carrier performance.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Invoice Verification Resolution; GAAP AP Controls; SOX

description: Freight payment responsibility terms indicating who bears the freight cost. 'prepaid' = shipper pays carrier; 'collect' = consignee pays carrier; 'third_party' = a third party is billed; 'prepaid_and_add' = shipper pays and adds to customer invoice.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD/MM — Incoterms / Freight Terms; UCC Article 2; GAAP

description: Carrier-applied fuel surcharge billed on this invoice, typically calculated as a percentage of base freight based on the DOE diesel fuel index. A standard variable component of freight invoices in agricultural logistics.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Condition Type (Fuel Surcharge); DOE Diesel Fuel Index; GAAP

description: SAP General Ledger account code to which the freight expense is posted (e.g., freight-in, freight-out, COGS transportation). Enables financial reporting and cost center allocation of freight expenses.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI/CO — GL Account (SKA1); GAAP Chart of Accounts; IFRS 15

description: Date the carrier issued the freight invoice. This is the principal business event date for the invoice and is used to determine payment due date and aging calculations in accounts payable.
reference: GAAP — Accounts Payable Recognition; SAP S/4HANA FI Invoice Date (BLDAT)

description: Externally assigned invoice number as printed on the carrier-issued freight invoice document. Used for three-way match, freight audit, and AP payment processing. Corresponds to the vendor invoice reference in SAP S/4HANA.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI — Vendor Invoice Reference (BKPF-XBLNR); GAAP AP documentation standards

description: Current lifecycle status of the freight invoice through the freight audit and payment workflow. 'received' = invoice received from carrier; 'under_audit' = freight audit in progress; 'matched' = three-way match passed; 'disputed' = variance identified and dispute raised with carrier; 'approved' = approved for payment; 'paid' = payment remitted; 'voided' = invoice cancelled. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: received|under_audit|matched|disputed|approved|paid|voided — promote to reference product]
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI — Invoice Verification Status; GAAP AP Controls; SOX Section 404

description: Total gross amount billed by the carrier on this invoice, representing the sum of base freight, fuel surcharge, accessorials, detention, lumper fees, stop-off charges, and any other line items. This is the amount subject to AP payment processing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI — Invoice Amount (WRBTR); GAAP AP Payables; SOX Section 404

description: Third-party labor charges for unloading agricultural commodities at the destination facility (lumper services). Common at food manufacturer and retailer distribution centers. Billed through the carrier on the freight invoice.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Lumper Condition Type; GAAP COGS; FSMA Sanitary Transportation

description: Actual date on which payment was remitted to the carrier. Nullable until payment is made. Used for cash flow reporting, on-time payment KPI tracking, and carrier relationship management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI — Payment Run Date (F110); GAAP AP Ledger; SOX

description: Date by which payment must be remitted to the carrier per the agreed payment terms. Derived from invoice date plus contracted payment terms (e.g., Net 30). Used for AP aging and cash flow planning.
reference: GAAP — AP Payment Terms; SAP S/4HANA FI Baseline Date (ZFBDT)

description: Current payment status of the freight invoice from the accounts payable perspective. 'unpaid' = no payment made; 'partial' = partial payment remitted; 'paid' = fully paid; 'overpaid' = payment exceeded invoice amount (requires credit memo).
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI — Payment Status; GAAP AP Ledger; SOX Section 404

description: Contracted payment terms applicable to this freight invoice as agreed with the carrier (e.g., Net 30, Net 15, 2/10 Net 30). Determines payment due date and any early payment discount eligibility.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI — Payment Terms (ZTERM); GAAP AP Terms; Carrier Contract

description: SAP Purchase Order number associated with the freight service procurement. Used in three-way match (PO vs. GRN vs. invoice) for freight payables processing and SOX compliance.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Purchase Order (EKKO-EBELN); GAAP AP Three-Way Match; SOX Section 404

description: Monetary difference between the carrier-invoiced amount and the contracted rate amount (invoice_total_amount minus contracted_rate_amount). Positive value indicates overbilling; negative indicates underbilling. Triggers dispute workflow when outside tolerance threshold.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Invoice Verification — Price Variance; GAAP; SOX Section 404 AP Controls

description: Rate variance expressed as a percentage of the contracted rate amount. Used to determine whether the variance falls within the acceptable tolerance threshold for auto-approval or requires manual freight audit review.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Invoice Verification — Tolerance Percentage; GAAP; SOX AP Controls

description: Carrier service level for this shipment. LTL (Less-Than-Truckload), FTL (Full Truckload), PTL (Partial Truckload), expedited, or spot market. Determines applicable rate tariff and service expectations.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Shipping Conditions; Manhattan Associates TMS Service Types

description: Operational system of record from which this freight invoice record was ingested into the Databricks silver layer. Supports data lineage, reconciliation, and audit trail requirements.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM/FI; Oracle NetSuite AP; Manhattan Associates TMS; GAAP Data Lineage

description: Additional charges billed for multi-stop shipments where the carrier makes intermediate delivery stops beyond the primary origin-destination pair. Common in agricultural distribution routes serving multiple food manufacturers.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Stop-Off Condition Type; NMFC Tariff; GAAP

description: Result of the three-way match validation comparing the contracted rate (rate confirmation), the BOL/shipment execution record, and the carrier invoice. 'passed' = all three documents align within tolerance; 'failed' = discrepancy detected; 'waived' = match bypassed with authorization. Critical SOX control for freight payables.
reference: SOX Section 404 — AP Three-Way Match Control; SAP S/4HANA MM Invoice Verification; GAAP

description: Mode of transportation for the shipment covered by this freight invoice. Determines applicable rate structures, regulatory requirements, and accessorial charge types. Critical for freight cost analytics by mode.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Shipment Type; FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule 21 CFR Part 1; DOT regulations

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this freight invoice record. Used for incremental data pipeline processing, change data capture, and audit trail maintenance in the Databricks silver layer.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI — Last Changed Timestamp; SOX Section 404; GAAP Audit Trail

description: Unique system-generated identifier for a freight rate record. Primary key for the freight_rate data product within the supply domain.

description: Reference to the carrier or third-party logistics (3PL) provider with whom this freight rate is contracted. Links to the carrier master record for carrier selection optimization and freight audit.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - Vendor Master; TMS Carrier Management

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - Plant/Storage Location; TMS Lane Management

description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Freight rates are used to pre-accrue freight costs to GL accounts during rate-based accrual processes. Agriculture logistics finance teams use rate cards to generate freight expense accruals by GL acc
reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Reference to the origin facility, farm, elevator, or distribution center for the freight lane covered by this rate. Defines the starting point of the origin-destination (O-D) lane for carrier selection and route optimization.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - Plant/Storage Location; TMS Lane Management

description: Reference to the parent freight contract or rate agreement under which this rate schedule is established. Supports contract lifecycle management and volume commitment tracking.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - Outline Agreement; TMS Contract Management

description: The contracted base freight rate amount, expressed in the unit defined by rate_type (e.g., USD per mile, USD per CWT, USD per MT, USD per BU, or flat USD amount). This is the principal monetary fact for the rate record, excluding fuel surcharge and accessorial charges. Used as the foundation for freight cost estimation and carrier invoice audit.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - Condition Amount; GAAP; IFRS 15 Revenue Recognition

description: Percentage discount applied to the base rate when the contracted volume commitment tier is met or exceeded. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.05 = 5% discount). Incentivizes volume commitment with carriers and 3PLs for agricultural commodity lanes.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - Condition Discount; GAAP Revenue Recognition

description: Timestamp when this freight rate record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and SOX financial reporting controls. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) - Internal Controls; GAAP Audit Trail Requirements

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code in which the freight rate is denominated (e.g., USD for US Dollar, CAD for Canadian Dollar, EUR for Euro). Required for multi-currency freight cost estimation and financial reporting under GAAP/IFRS.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; GAAP; IFRS

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the destination of the freight lane. Required for export documentation, customs compliance, and international freight rate applicability.
reference: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; USDA COOL Regulations; Codex Alimentarius

description: ZIP code of the destination point for the freight lane. Used for lane-level rate matching in TMS when a specific facility ID is not available. Supports zone-based and mileage-based rate calculations.
reference: USPS ZIP Code Standard; TMS Lane Rate Management

description: Accessorial charge rate applied per hour when a carrier's equipment is detained beyond the contracted free time at origin or destination. A key component of the accessorial rate schedule for agricultural commodity shipments where loading/unloading delays are common.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - Accessorial Condition; Carrier Tariff - Detention/Demurrage Rules

description: Date from which this freight rate becomes binding and applicable for freight cost estimation and carrier selection. Aligns with contract start date in carrier agreements. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - Condition Record Validity Start; GAAP Contract Accounting

description: Type of transportation equipment required for this rate. Refrigerated (reefer) equipment is required for cold chain management of perishable agricultural commodities. Hopper trailers are used for bulk grain. Tankers for liquid commodities. Critical for cold chain compliance under FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule.
reference: FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule (21 CFR Part 1, Subpart O); SAP S/4HANA TM Equipment Type

description: Date after which this freight rate is no longer valid for new shipment cost estimation. Null indicates an open-ended rate with no defined expiration. Retained post-expiry for freight audit variance analysis. Format: yyyy-MM-dd.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - Condition Record Validity End; GAAP Contract Accounting

description: Number of hours of free loading/unloading time included in the base rate before detention charges begin to accrue. Standard free time for agricultural commodity shipments is typically 2 hours. Critical for managing detention/demurrage cost exposure at grain elevators and processing facilities.
reference: Carrier Tariff - Detention Rules; SAP S/4HANA TM Freight Agreement

description: Contractual freight payment terms defining who bears the freight cost and when title transfers. FOB (Free On Board) origin and destination are standard agricultural commodity trade terms. Prepaid = shipper pays; Collect = consignee pays; Third Party = billed to a third party. Aligns with SAP S/4HANA SD billing and SAP MM purchasing conditions.
reference: Incoterms 2020 (ICC); SAP S/4HANA SD - Freight Terms; GAAP

description: Indicates whether this freight rate is associated with a carrier that has been verified as compliant with the FSMA Sanitary Transportation of Human and Animal Food Rule (21 CFR Part 1, Subpart O). True = carrier has confirmed FSMA compliance for this lane and equipment type. Required for food safety audit and carrier qualification.
reference: FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) - Sanitary Transportation Rule (21 CFR Part 1, Subpart O)

description: Description or formula code defining how the fuel surcharge is calculated, typically indexed to the US Department of Energy (DOE) weekly diesel retail price index. Examples: 'DOE_TABLE_LOOKUP', 'DOE_PERCENT_OF_BASE', 'FIXED_CPM' (cents per mile). Drives dynamic fuel surcharge computation in TMS freight cost estimation.
reference: US Department of Energy (DOE) Diesel Retail Price Index; SAP S/4HANA MM Condition Supplement

description: The current or baseline fuel surcharge rate expressed as a percentage of the base rate or as a fixed amount per mile (depending on fuel_surcharge_formula). Updated periodically based on DOE index triggers. Used in freight cost estimation and carrier invoice audit.
reference: US Department of Energy (DOE) Diesel Retail Price Index; SAP S/4HANA MM Condition Rate

description: Contracted or calculated mileage for the origin-destination freight lane. Used for per-mile rate calculations, fuel surcharge computation, and route optimization analysis. Typically derived from PC*MILER or equivalent mileage engine integrated with TMS.
reference: PC*MILER Mileage Standard; SAP S/4HANA TM - Distance Calculation

description: Accessorial charge for lumper (third-party unloading labor) services at destination facilities such as food manufacturer warehouses and retail distribution centers. Included in the accessorial rate schedule when the carrier is responsible for arranging unloading labor.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - Accessorial Condition; Manhattan Associates WMS - Receiving Labor

description: The minimum freight charge applicable regardless of shipment weight, volume, or distance. Ensures carrier cost recovery for small or short-haul shipments. Applied during freight cost estimation when the calculated base rate falls below this threshold.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - Minimum Condition Value; Carrier Tariff Standards

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the origin of the freight lane. Required for cross-border agricultural commodity movements and Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) compliance.
reference: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3; USDA COOL (Country of Origin Labeling) Regulations

description: ZIP code of the origin point for the freight lane. Used for lane-level rate matching in TMS when a specific facility ID is not available. Supports zone-based and mileage-based rate calculations.
reference: USPS ZIP Code Standard; TMS Lane Rate Management

description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier for the freight rate record, used in carrier negotiations, freight audit, and SAP S/4HANA condition record references. Enables cross-system traceability between TMS, ERP, and carrier portals.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - Condition Record Number; TMS Rate Management

description: Current lifecycle status of the freight rate record. Active rates are available for freight cost estimation and carrier selection. Expired rates are retained for freight audit variance analysis against historical invoices. Pending rates are awaiting carrier confirmation. Suspended rates are temporarily unavailable.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - Condition Record Status; TMS Rate Management

description: Classification of how the freight rate is calculated and applied. Per mile applies to truckload movements; per CWT (Hundredweight) and per MT (Metric Ton) apply to weight-based commodity pricing; per BU (Bushel) applies to grain and oilseed movements; flat rate applies to fixed-price lane agreements. Drives freight cost estimation logic in TMS.
reference: NMFC (National Motor Freight Classification); SAP S/4HANA MM Condition Type

description: Operational system of record from which this freight rate record originated. SAP_S4HANA indicates the rate was created in SAP S/4HANA MM condition records; TMS indicates origin from the Transportation Management System; MANUAL indicates direct entry. Supports data lineage and freight audit traceability.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - Condition Record; Oracle NetSuite Procurement

description: Accessorial charge applied for each additional stop beyond the primary origin-destination pair on a multi-stop shipment. Common in agricultural distribution routes serving multiple farm locations or delivery points. Part of the accessorial rate schedule.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM - Accessorial Condition; NMFTA Tariff Rules

description: Maximum allowable temperature in degrees Celsius for cold chain shipments covered by this rate. Applicable to refrigerated equipment rates for perishable agricultural commodities. Enforces FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule cold chain requirements.
reference: FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule (21 CFR Part 1, Subpart O); FDA Food Safety Regulations; ISO 22000

description: Minimum required temperature in degrees Celsius for cold chain shipments covered by this rate. Applicable to refrigerated equipment rates for perishable agricultural commodities (produce, dairy, meat). Enforces FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule cold chain requirements.
reference: FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule (21 CFR Part 1, Subpart O); FDA Food Safety Regulations; ISO 22000

description: Contracted standard transit time in calendar days for the origin-destination lane at this rate. Used for delivery scheduling, cold chain management planning, and carrier service level evaluation. Critical for perishable agricultural commodity shipments.
reference: SAP S/4HANA TM - Transit Time; FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule

description: Mode of transportation for which this freight rate applies. Truckload (TL) and less-than-truckload (LTL) are primary modes for domestic agricultural commodity movements; rail and intermodal for bulk grain; ocean for export; air for high-value perishables. Aligns with BOL and AWB documentation requirements.
reference: SAP S/4HANA TM - Freight Order; FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule (21 CFR Part 1, Subpart O)

description: Timestamp when this freight rate record was last modified. Supports change tracking, freight audit variance analysis, and Silver Layer incremental processing in the Databricks Lakehouse. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: SOX (Sarbanes-Oxley Act) - Internal Controls; Databricks Delta Lake Change Data Feed

description: Maximum contracted volume (in the unit defined by rate_type) applicable for this rate tier. Null indicates no upper bound. Defines the upper boundary of the volume commitment tier for tiered discount rate structures.

description: Unit of measure for the volume tier commitment quantities (volume_tier_min, volume_tier_max). Aligns with the rate_type unit. reference: NOAA NWS Ensemble Forecast Products; WASDE (USDA); DTN Weather Services

description: Qualitative confidence level assigned by the forecast provider indicating the reliability of this forecast record. High confidence forecasts are used for firm operational commitments; low confidence forecasts trigger contingency planning.
reference: NOAA NWS Forecast Confidence Guidance; DTN Weather Services

description: Timestamp when this forecast record was first ingested into the agricultural data lakehouse. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver Layer processing compliance. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: ISO 8601; SOX Audit Trail Requirements; FSMA Record-Keeping

description: Forecast dew point temperature in degrees Celsius for the valid period. Used in disease pressure models (e.g., fungal blight risk) and to assess condensation risk on crops and equipment.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; IPM Disease Forecasting Models

description: Elevation of the forecast location above mean sea level in meters. Influences temperature lapse rate adjustments, frost risk calculations, and ET evapotranspiration estimates for high-altitude agricultural fields.
reference: USDA NRCS; Esri ArcGIS Terrain Analysis

description: Forecast reference evapotranspiration (ET) in millimeters for the valid period, calculated using the FAO Penman-Monteith method. Primary input for irrigation scheduling decisions and water resource management in Climate FieldView and Trimble Ag Software.
reference: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56 (Penman-Monteith); USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView

description: Externally assigned identifier or reference code from the source forecast provider (e.g., NOAA NWS product ID, DTN forecast package ID, Climate FieldView forecast run ID). Enables traceability back to the originating provider record for dispute resolution and data quality audits.
reference: NOAA NWS Product Identification; DTN Weather Services; Climate FieldView

description: Current lifecycle state of the forecast record. Active forecasts are in use for operational decisions; superseded forecasts have been replaced by a newer issue; expired forecasts have passed their valid period; cancelled forecasts were withdrawn by the provider.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services

description: Temporal resolution and horizon of the forecast record. Hourly forecasts support spray window scheduling; daily and 7-day support planting window decisions; seasonal forecasts align with WASDE outlooks and crop insurance documentation.
reference: NOAA NWS Forecast Products; DTN Weather Services; WASDE (USDA)

description: Boolean flag indicating whether forecast minimum temperature is at or below -2.2°C (28°F), triggering a hard freeze alert. Distinguishes from frost risk for crop damage severity classification and crop insurance loss event documentation.
reference: NOAA NWS Freeze Warning Criteria; USDA RMA Crop Insurance; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Boolean flag indicating whether forecast minimum temperature is at or below 0°C, triggering a frost alert. Supports frost protection decisions including irrigation-based frost protection, smudge pot activation, and harvest acceleration.
reference: NOAA NWS Frost/Freeze Advisories; USDA NRCS; GLOBALG.A.P.

business_glossary_term: Growing Degree Day (GDD) Base Temperature Celsius
description: Base temperature in degrees Celsius used in the GDD growing degree day calculation for this forecast record. Varies by crop species (e.g., 10°C for corn, 4.4°C for wheat). Ensures GDD values are interpreted correctly for the target crop.
reference: USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView; Crop-Specific GDD Standards

description: Forecast growing degree day accumulation for the valid period, calculated from forecast max and min temperatures relative to a crop-specific base temperature. Supports crop development stage prediction, pest emergence timing, and planting window optimization.
reference: USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView; NOAA NWS Agricultural Weather

description: Number of hours from the issued timestamp to the end of the forecast valid period. Indicates how far into the future the forecast extends, supporting confidence assessment and operational planning lead time.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services

description: Forecast relative humidity as a percentage for the valid period. Influences fungal disease pressure prediction, spray efficacy windows, and ET evapotranspiration calculations for irrigation scheduling.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; USDA NRCS; IPM Guidelines

description: Date and time when the forecast was officially issued or published by the source provider. Used to determine forecast freshness and to sequence superseding forecast versions. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; ISO 8601

description: Decimal latitude coordinate of the forecast location or field polygon centroid. Used for spatial alignment with GIS field maps and IoT sensor networks. Expressed in decimal degrees (WGS84).
reference: Esri ArcGIS; GPS/RTK Positioning Standards; WGS84

description: Decimal longitude coordinate of the forecast location or field polygon centroid. Used for spatial alignment with GIS field maps and IoT sensor networks. Expressed in decimal degrees (WGS84).
reference: Esri ArcGIS; GPS/RTK Positioning Standards; WGS84

description: Version identifier of the numerical weather prediction model used to generate this forecast (e.g., GFS 16.3.0, NAM 4.1, ECMWF CY47R3). Enables traceability and reproducibility of forecast-driven agricultural decisions for audit and compliance purposes.
reference: NOAA NWS NWP Model Documentation; ECMWF; DTN Weather Services

description: Forecast total precipitation amount in millimeters for the valid period. Used for irrigation scheduling decisions, soil moisture modeling, and crop insurance documentation under USDA Risk Management Agency guidelines.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; USDA RMA Crop Insurance; FSMA

description: Forecast probability of measurable precipitation occurring during the valid period, expressed as a percentage (0–100). Key input for spray window scheduling — high probability suppresses pesticide application recommendations per IPM Integrated Pest Management protocols.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; EPA IPM Guidelines

description: Forecast type of precipitation expected during the valid period. Distinguishes rain from snow, hail, or freezing rain, which have different implications for field operations, equipment deployment, and crop damage risk assessment.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services

business_glossary_term: Solar Radiation Megajoules Per Square Meter
description: Forecast incoming solar radiation in megajoules per square meter for the valid period. Direct input to the FAO Penman-Monteith ET calculation and photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) models for crop growth simulation.
reference: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper No. 56; USDA NRCS; NOAA NWS

description: Originating data provider or system for this forecast record. Identifies whether the forecast was sourced from DTN Data Transmission Network, NOAA National Weather Service, Climate FieldView, custom IoT field sensors, or WASDE World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates seasonal outlook.
reference: DTN Weather Services; NOAA NWS; Climate FieldView; WASDE (USDA)

description: Boolean flag indicating whether forecast conditions (wind speed, precipitation probability, temperature, humidity) meet the criteria for a safe and effective pesticide or herbicide application window. Derived from EPA application guidelines and IPM Integrated Pest Management protocols.
reference: EPA Pesticide Application Standards; IPM Guidelines; GLOBALG.A.P.; FSMA

description: Forecast mean air temperature in degrees Celsius for the valid period. Used as the base input for GDD growing degree day accumulation calculations and pest pressure prediction models.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; USDA NRCS

description: Forecast maximum air temperature in degrees Celsius for the valid period. Used in growing degree day (GDD) accumulation calculations, heat stress assessments, and crop development stage modeling.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; USDA NRCS; ISO 80000-5

description: Forecast minimum air temperature in degrees Celsius for the valid period. Critical for frost and freeze alert generation, PHI pre-harvest interval compliance, and cold stress risk assessment for crops.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; USDA NRCS; ISO 80000-5

description: Timestamp when this forecast record was last modified or refreshed in the data lakehouse, such as when a forecast is superseded or corrected by the provider. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: ISO 8601; SOX Audit Trail Requirements; FSMA Record-Keeping

description: Forecast prevailing wind direction in meteorological degrees (0–360, where 0/360 = North). Used in spray drift modeling to protect adjacent fields, buffer zones, and sensitive areas per EPA and GLOBALG.A.P. requirements.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; EPA Spray Drift Guidelines; GLOBALG.A.P.

business_glossary_term: Wind Gust Speed Kilometers Per Hour
description: Forecast maximum wind gust speed in kilometers per hour for the valid period. Used to assess equipment safety thresholds for aerial application and tall crop operations.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; EPA Pesticide Application Standards; OSHA

description: Forecast average wind speed in kilometers per hour for the valid period. Critical for spray window determination — wind speeds above threshold trigger spray application restrictions per EPA and REI Restricted Entry Interval guidelines.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; EPA Pesticide Application Standards; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Start of the period for which this forecast is valid. For hourly forecasts this is the start of the forecast hour; for daily forecasts it is the start of the forecast day. Used to align forecast data with field operation scheduling windows.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; ISO 8601

description: End of the period for which this forecast is valid. Defines the forecast window boundary for planting, spraying, and irrigation scheduling decisions.
reference: NOAA NWS; DTN Weather Services; ISO 8601

description: Unique system-generated identifier for each meteorological observation record. Primary key for the weather observation time-series table in the Silver Layer lakehouse.
reference: ISO 8601; FMIS data standards

description: Reference to the agricultural field or land parcel associated with this observation, enabling field-level weather correlation for irrigation scheduling, spray window determination, and crop insurance documentation.
reference: Esri ArcGIS; Trimble Ag Software; FMIS

description: Reference to the weather station or IoT field sensor that captured this observation. Links to the station master record for location, calibration, and ownership metadata.
reference: John Deere Operations Center; Climate FieldView; IoT sensor registry

description: FK to weather.weather_station.weather_station_id — Every weather observation is captured at a specific station. Without this FK, weather data cannot be attributed to a location — breaking all spatial weather queries and field-level weather correlation

Atmospheric pressure measured during the observation interval, in hectopascals (hPa). Used for weather front detection, storm prediction, and calibration of altitude-adjusted ET calculations. Supports short-term weather forecasting for field operations planning.
reference: WMO No. 8; FAO-56 Penman-Monteith altitude correction

description: Timestamp when this observation record was first ingested and created in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Used for audit trail, data freshness monitoring, and SLA compliance tracking for weather data feeds.
reference: ISO 8601; FSMA data integrity requirements; SOX audit trail standards

description: Identifies the originating system or feed that provided this observation record. Supports data lineage, quality weighting, and source reconciliation across IoT field sensors, DTN weather feeds, Climate FieldView integrations, and manual entries.
reference: Climate FieldView; DTN Data Transmission Network; John Deere Operations Center; IoT sensor standards

description: Dew point temperature in degrees Celsius, representing the temperature at which air becomes saturated with moisture. Used for frost risk prediction, fungal disease pressure modeling (e.g., gray mold, downy mildew), and spray window determination under IPM frameworks.
reference: WMO No. 8; IPM disease pressure models; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Reference evapotranspiration (ET₀) calculated for the observation interval using the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith method, in millimeters. SSOT for irrigation scheduling, water balance modeling, and crop water use estimation. Integrates with Climate FieldView and Granular Farm Management irrigation modules.
reference: FAO-56 Penman-Monteith ET method; USDA NRCS; Climate FieldView; Granular Farm Management

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this observation triggered a frost or freeze alert condition (temperature at or below 0°C). Drives automated notifications for frost protection actions (e.g., wind machine activation, irrigation frost protection), crop insurance event documentation, and PHI compliance tracking.
reference: USDA RMA crop insurance frost event documentation; GLOBALG.A.P.; Climate FieldView alert framework

description: Growing Degree Day (GDD) accumulation for the observation interval using a base temperature of 10°C, calculated as max(0, (temp_max_c + temp_min_c)/2 - 10). Used for crop phenology tracking, pest emergence prediction, and harvest timing optimization. Standard base for corn and many broadacre crops.
reference: USDA crop GDD standards; Climate FieldView GDD models; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Configured measurement interval for this observation record. Determines the temporal resolution of the time-series data. Supported intervals: 5-minute, 15-minute, hourly, and daily aggregations. Drives GDD and ET calculation granularity.
reference: Climate FieldView; DTN weather feed standards; WMO No. 8

description: Duration of leaf surface wetness during the observation interval, in hours. Critical input for fungal and bacterial disease pressure models under IPM frameworks (e.g., fire blight, late blight, botrytis). Drives spray timing recommendations and PHI (Pre-Harvest Interval) compliance tracking.
reference: IPM (Integrated Pest Management) disease models; GLOBALG.A.P.; EPA PHI compliance

description: Quality lifecycle status of the observation record. Raw records are ingested as-is; validated records have passed QC checks; flagged records have anomalies under review; corrected records have been adjusted; rejected records are excluded from downstream calculations.
reference: WMO No. 8 Quality Control procedures; FSMA data integrity requirements; ISO 22000

description: Classifies whether the record represents an instantaneous point reading, an interval average, a daily summary aggregation, or a forecast value ingested from DTN or WASDE feeds. Drives downstream processing logic for GDD and ET calculations.
reference: WMO No. 8; DTN Data Transmission Network standards; WASDE reporting framework

description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the meteorological measurement was captured at the sensor or station. This is the principal real-world event time used for time-series analysis, GDD accumulation, ET computation, and crop insurance documentation. Stored in yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX format.
reference: ISO 8601; WMO No. 8 Guide to Meteorological Instruments; FSMA traceability requirements

description: Total liquid precipitation (rainfall) accumulated during the observation interval, in millimeters. Core input for irrigation scheduling, water balance calculations, crop insurance loss documentation, and FSMA water quality compliance tracking.
reference: WMO No. 8; USDA NRCS; FSMA Produce Safety Rule; crop insurance MPCI standards

description: Free-text notes from the automated QC process or manual data reviewer describing the reason for a suspect, fail, or estimated quality flag. Supports audit trail requirements for crop insurance documentation and FSMA traceability.
reference: WMO No. 8; FSMA traceability requirements; USDA RMA crop insurance audit standards

description: WMO-aligned quality control flag for the observation record. Pass = all values within expected range; Suspect = one or more values outside climatological bounds but not definitively erroneous; Fail = confirmed erroneous values; Missing = one or more required measurements absent; Estimated = gap-filled using interpolation or neighboring station data.
reference: WMO No. 8 Quality Control; USDA NRCS data quality standards; ISO 22000 data integrity

description: Relative humidity as a percentage (0–100%) measured during the observation interval. Critical input for spray window determination (REI compliance), fungal disease pressure modeling under IPM frameworks, and ET calculation via the Penman-Monteith method.
reference: WMO No. 8; FAO-56 Penman-Monteith; EPA REI (Restricted Entry Interval) compliance; IPM standards

description: Depth below the soil surface at which soil temperature and soil moisture readings were captured, in centimeters. Required for multi-depth sensor arrays to correctly attribute readings to the appropriate soil horizon. Null for atmospheric measurements.
reference: USDA NRCS soil monitoring standards; IoT sensor installation specifications

description: Height above ground level at which atmospheric measurements (temperature, humidity, wind) were captured, in meters. Standard WMO height is 2m for temperature/humidity and 10m for wind. Required for ET calculation height corrections and data quality validation.
reference: WMO No. 8 instrument siting standards; FAO-56 Penman-Monteith height correction

description: Snowfall accumulation during the observation interval expressed as millimeters of water equivalent. Used for spring soil moisture forecasting, field access planning, and crop insurance documentation in winter crop regions.
reference: WMO No. 8; USDA NRCS; MPCI crop insurance standards

description: Volumetric soil moisture content as a percentage of field capacity, measured at the sensor depth. Core input for irrigation scheduling decisions, drought stress monitoring, and VRA (Variable Rate Application) prescription generation. Integrates with John Deere Operations Center and Trimble Ag Software.
reference: USDA NRCS; FAO irrigation scheduling guidelines; VRA standards; John Deere Operations Center

description: Soil temperature measured at the sensor depth during the observation interval, in degrees Celsius. Used for planting window determination (germination threshold monitoring), soil microbial activity modeling, and fertilizer application timing optimization.
reference: USDA NRCS; Trimble Ag Software; Climate FieldView; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Incoming solar radiation (shortwave) measured during the observation interval, in watts per square meter (W/m²). Primary driver of ET (Evapotranspiration) calculations via the Penman-Monteith method and NDVI-based crop growth modeling. Also used for solar energy resource assessment on farm.
reference: WMO No. 8; FAO-56 Penman-Monteith; NDVI calculation standards; USDA NRCS

description: Original record identifier from the upstream source system (e.g., DTN feed message ID, Climate FieldView observation UUID, John Deere Operations Center telemetry record ID). Enables end-to-end data lineage tracing from raw ingestion to Silver Layer.
reference: DTN Data Transmission Network; Climate FieldView; John Deere Operations Center; FSMA data lineage requirements

description: Boolean flag indicating whether current meteorological conditions (wind speed, temperature, relative humidity, precipitation) meet the criteria for a safe and compliant pesticide or fertilizer application window. Derived from EPA label requirements and IPM BMP thresholds. Supports REI and PHI compliance.
reference: EPA pesticide application label requirements; IPM BMP standards; GLOBALG.A.P.; FSMA

description: Mean air temperature for the observation interval, in degrees Celsius. Computed as (max + min) / 2 for daily intervals or as a true average for sub-daily intervals. Primary input for ET (Evapotranspiration) calculations and irrigation scheduling models.
reference: WMO No. 8; FAO-56 Penman-Monteith ET method; USDA NRCS

description: Maximum air temperature recorded during the observation interval, in degrees Celsius. Used for GDD (Growing Degree Day) accumulation calculations, heat stress threshold monitoring, and crop insurance documentation. Paired with temperature_min_c for daily range analysis.
reference: WMO No. 8; USDA NRCS; GDD calculation standards; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Minimum air temperature recorded during the observation interval, in degrees Celsius. Critical for frost/freeze alert generation, GDD base temperature calculations, chilling hour accumulation, and crop protection decision support.
reference: WMO No. 8; USDA NRCS; GDD calculation standards; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Timestamp when this observation record was last modified in the Silver Layer, such as after QC correction, status change, or data enrichment. Supports audit trail and change data capture (CDC) for downstream consumers.
reference: ISO 8601; FSMA data integrity requirements; SOX audit trail standards

description: Prevailing wind direction during the observation interval, expressed in meteorological degrees (0–360°, where 0/360 = North). Used for spray drift modeling, pesticide application compliance, and field-level wind exposure analysis.
reference: WMO No. 8; EPA pesticide application label requirements; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Maximum instantaneous wind gust speed recorded during the observation interval, in meters per second. Used for equipment safety alerts, spray application go/no-go decisions, and crop lodging risk assessment.
reference: WMO No. 8; EPA pesticide application label requirements; OSHA field safety standards

description: Average wind speed during the observation interval, in meters per second. Used for spray window determination (drift risk assessment), ET calculation, and wind damage risk alerts. EPA pesticide label compliance requires wind speed checks before application.
reference: WMO No. 8; EPA pesticide application label requirements; FAO-56 Penman-Monteith; GLOBALG.A.P.

business_glossary_term: Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) Reference Number

business_glossary_term: Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) Violation Count

business_glossary_term: GLOBALG.A.P. (Global Good Agricultural Practices) Compliance Required Flag

description: The ISO 639-1 language code (optionally with ISO 3166-1 region subtag) specifying the language in which COOL labels must be printed for this customer (e.g., 'en', 'es', 'fr-CA'). Supports bilingual or multilingual labeling requirements for export or cross-border distribution.

business_glossary_term: Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) Label Placement Requirement

'principal_display_panel' is the most prominent face; 'information_panel' is the secondary panel; 'any_panel' allows flexibility; 'customer_specified' requires reference to customer SOP documentation.

business_glossary_term: Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) Labeling Format

'full_origin' indicates a single country of origin; 'mixed_origin' indicates multiple countries; 'derived_from' is used for processed commodities; 'product_of' denotes full production in one country; 'born_raised_slaughtered' applies to muscle cut beef and pork per USDA COOL rules.

business_glossary_term: Last Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) Compliance Review Date

business_glossary_term: Last Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) Violation Date
