reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Primary active ingredient(s) in crop protection chemicals or veterinary products (e.g., 'glyphosate', 'chlorpyrifos', 'azoxystrobin'). Critical for MRL compliance, PHI determination, and HACCP hazard analysis. Null for non-chemical inputs.
reference: EPA FIFRA Active Ingredient Definition; Codex Alimentarius MRL Standards; FDA FSMA

description: Concentration of the active ingredient expressed as a percentage of the total formulation (e.g., 41.0 for 41% glyphosate). Used for application rate calculations, MRL compliance verification, and SDS documentation.
reference: EPA FIFRA Label Requirements; Codex Alimentarius; ISO 22000 Food Safety Management

business_glossary_term: Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) Permit Category
description: USDA APHIS permit classification for biological inputs including biocontrol agents, plant pests, and veterinary biologicals. Required for import, interstate movement, and field release of regulated biological organisms. Null or 'not_applicable' for non-biological inputs.
reference: USDA APHIS 7 CFR Part 330; APHIS Biotechnology Regulatory Services; USDA APHIS VS

description: Date on which this input was approved and added to the active procurement catalog following vendor qualification, regulatory compliance verification, and internal approval workflow. Supports audit trail for GLOBALG.A.P. and GFSI certification.
reference: GLOBALG.A.P. Input Approval Process; GFSI Benchmarked Standards; SAP S/4HANA MM Material Release

description: Primary unit of measure for procurement and inventory transactions (e.g., KG, MT, L, GAL, BU, CWT, EA). Aligns with SAP S/4HANA MM base UOM and drives GRN quantity validation and stock position calculations.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Unit of Measure (MARA-MEINS); ISO 80000-1 Quantities and Units

description: Current lifecycle status of the input in the master catalog. Controls whether the input is available for purchase requisition and PO creation in SAP S/4HANA MM. 'restricted' indicates regulatory or internal procurement hold.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Status (MARA-MMSTA); GLOBALG.A.P. Approved Input List

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code indicating the country where this input was manufactured or produced. Required for COOL (Country of Origin Labeling) compliance, import documentation, and APHIS phytosanitary permit requirements.
reference: USDA COOL 7 CFR Part 60; APHIS Import Permit Requirements; CBP 19 CFR Part 102; ISO 3166-1

description: Primary crop or crop group for which this input is registered, approved, or intended (e.g., 'corn', 'soybean', 'wheat', 'cotton', 'all_crops'). Drives crop-specific procurement planning, VRA prescription compatibility, and EPA label compliance.
reference: EPA FIFRA Registered Uses; GLOBALG.A.P. Crop Protection Module; USDA NASS Crop Classification

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the standard cost and pricing fields (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'BRL'). Supports multi-currency procurement operations and IFRS financial reporting.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IFRS IAS 21 Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates; GAAP

description: Pesticide or fertilizer formulation type code (e.g., EC=Emulsifiable Concentrate, WP=Wettable Powder, SC=Suspension Concentrate, WG=Water Dispersible Granule, GR=Granule, SL=Soluble Liquid). Affects application equipment compatibility and handling procedures. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: EC|WP|SC|WG|GR|SL|CS|not_applicable — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: FAO/WHO Pesticide Specifications; EPA FIFRA Label; CropLife International Formulation Codes

description: Indicates whether the input (primarily seeds) is genetically modified (GMO), non-GMO, conventional (no GMO claim), or not applicable for non-seed inputs. Required for USDA APHIS biotech regulatory compliance, COOL labeling, and customer supply chain transparency.
reference: USDA APHIS 7 CFR Part 340; USDA National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: DOT hazardous materials classification code for transport and storage compliance (e.g., '3' for flammable liquids/fuels, '6.1' for toxic substances, '8' for corrosives). Null for non-hazardous inputs. Required for BOL documentation and TMS routing.
reference: DOT 49 CFR Parts 171-180; EPA RCRA; OSHA HazCom; GHS Classification

description: High-level classification of the agricultural input type. Drives procurement workflows, regulatory compliance checks, and SDS documentation requirements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: seed|fertilizer|crop_protection|feed_ingredient|fuel|spare_part|operational_supply|biological — promote to reference product]
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Type; USDA APHIS Input Classification; EPA Pesticide Registration

description: Human-readable commercial or trade name of the agricultural input (e.g., 'Roundup PowerMAX', 'Pioneer P1197AM', 'Urea 46-0-0'). Used for display, reporting, and procurement communications.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Description; GLOBALG.A.P. Input Register

description: Granular classification within the input category (e.g., for crop_protection: herbicide, insecticide, fungicide, nematicide; for fertilizer: nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, micronutrient, organic). Supports IPM program management and NPK spend analytics.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Group; EPA Pesticide Product Classification; USDA NOP

description: Date of the most recent regulatory and compliance review of this catalog entry, including EPA registration status, MRL updates, SDS currency, and vendor qualification renewal. Supports periodic review cycle management per GLOBALG.A.P. and FSMA requirements.
reference: GLOBALG.A.P. Annual Review Requirements; FDA FSMA Preventive Controls; ISO 22000 Management Review

description: Standard procurement lead time in calendar days from PO issuance to GRN for this input from the preferred vendor. Used for reorder point calculation, planting season procurement planning, and supply chain risk management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM MRP Planning (MARC-PLIFZ); Granular Farm Management Procurement Planning

description: Indicates whether this input requires lot/batch number tracking throughout the supply chain for traceability, recall management, and FSMA compliance. True for seeds, crop protection chemicals, feed ingredients, and biologicals.
reference: FDA FSMA 21 CFR Part 1 Subpart S Traceability; SAP S/4HANA MM Batch Management; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Externally-known unique material number assigned in SAP S/4HANA MM or Oracle NetSuite for this agricultural input. Used as the primary cross-system business identifier for procurement, inventory, and AP processing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Master (MARA-MATNR); Oracle NetSuite Item Record

description: Minimum quantity per purchase order as required by the preferred vendor, expressed in the purchase UOM. Prevents creation of POs below vendor minimums and supports procurement cost optimization.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Purchasing Info Record (EINE-MINBM); Oracle NetSuite Vendor Item Record

description: Biochemical mode of action classification for crop protection chemicals using HRAC (herbicides), IRAC (insecticides), or FRAC (fungicides) group codes (e.g., 'HRAC Group 9', 'IRAC Group 4A'). Critical for IPM resistance management programs.
reference: HRAC (Herbicide Resistance Action Committee); IRAC (Insecticide Resistance Action Committee); FRAC (Fungicide Resistance Action Committee); EPA IPM Guidelines

business_glossary_term: Maximum Residue Limit (MRL) in Parts Per Million (PPM)
description: Maximum Residue Limit for the active ingredient on the target crop, expressed in parts per million (PPM). Regulatory threshold set by EPA, Codex Alimentarius, or importing country standards. Drives pre-harvest interval enforcement and food safety compliance.
reference: EPA 40 CFR Part 180; Codex Alimentarius MRL Database; EU Regulation 396/2005; FDA FSMA

description: NPK nutrient analysis expressed as N-P-K percentage (e.g., '46-0-0' for urea, '18-46-0' for DAP, '0-0-60' for potash). Mandatory for all fertilizer inputs. Null for non-fertilizer inputs. Drives soil fertility planning and nutrient management compliance.
reference: AAPFCO (Association of American Plant Food Control Officials) Official Publication; USDA NRCS Nutrient Management

description: Indicates whether this input is certified for use in USDA National Organic Program (NOP) certified operations. True only for inputs on the USDA NOP National List of Allowed and Prohibited Substances. Critical for organic farm procurement compliance.
reference: USDA NOP 7 CFR Part 205; USDA National List of Allowed Substances; GLOBALG.A.P. Organic Module

description: Name of the USDA-accredited certifying agent that issued the organic certification for this input (e.g., 'CCOF', 'Oregon Tilth', 'OMRI'). Required when organic_certified is True. Supports NOP audit trail and supplier qualification.
reference: USDA NOP 7 CFR Part 205.501; OMRI (Organic Materials Review Institute); Fair Trade USA

description: Minimum number of days that must elapse between the last application of a crop protection chemical and harvest, as specified on the EPA-registered label. Enforced during crop protection event scheduling to ensure MRL compliance.
reference: EPA FIFRA Label Requirements; GLOBALG.A.P. Crop Protection Module; FSMA Produce Safety Rule

description: Unit of measure used on purchase orders and vendor invoices, which may differ from the base UOM (e.g., purchased in MT but stocked in KG). Supports PO creation and AP invoice matching in SAP S/4HANA MM.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Purchasing Info Record; Oracle NetSuite Purchase UOM

description: Minimum number of hours workers must stay out of treated areas after pesticide application, as mandated by EPA Worker Protection Standard (WPS). Critical for workforce safety compliance and OSHA reporting.
reference: EPA Worker Protection Standard (WPS) 40 CFR Part 170; OSHA 29 CFR 1928.110; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Indicates whether this crop protection chemical is classified as a Restricted Use Pesticide (RUP) by the EPA, requiring a certified pesticide applicator license for purchase and application. Drives applicator certification verification in procurement workflow.
reference: EPA FIFRA Section 3(d); 40 CFR Part 152 Subpart I; USDA APHIS

description: Indicates whether a Safety Data Sheet (SDS) is required for this input under OSHA Hazard Communication Standard (HazCom) and EPA regulations. True for all crop protection chemicals, fertilizers, and fuels. Drives SDS document management workflow.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200 HazCom Standard; EPA FIFRA; GHS (Globally Harmonized System)

description: Indicates whether seeds are chemically treated (fungicide/insecticide coating), untreated, organically treated, or not applicable for non-seed inputs. Affects handling requirements, PHI/REI applicability, and USDA NOP organic certification eligibility.
reference: USDA NOP 7 CFR Part 205; EPA FIFRA Seed Treatment Registration; GLOBALG.A.P. Seed Module

description: Maximum number of days this input remains effective and safe from the date of manufacture or receipt, as specified by the manufacturer. Drives FIFO/FEFO inventory management, reorder policy, and expiry-based quarantine holds in the WMS.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Shelf Life Management; Manhattan Associates WMS Expiry Management; GMP

description: EPA-mandated signal word on the pesticide label indicating acute toxicity level: DANGER (highest toxicity, Category I/II), WARNING (moderate toxicity, Category III), CAUTION (lowest toxicity, Category IV), or not_applicable for non-pesticide inputs. Required for SDS and worker safety training.
reference: EPA FIFRA 40 CFR Part 156.64; GHS Hazard Communication; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200

description: Vendor-assigned or internal SKU code for this input, used for order management, barcode scanning, and RFID tracking in the warehouse. Supports Manhattan Associates WMS receiving and inventory control operations.

description: Required storage condition for this input to maintain efficacy, safety, and regulatory compliance. Drives WMS bin location assignment in Manhattan Associates and warehouse task planning for proper segregation of incompatible materials.
reference: EPA FIFRA Label Storage Requirements; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.106; GMP Storage Guidelines; ISO 22000

description: The gross weight of this component in kilograms as included in the bundle, used for total bundle weight calculation, freight cost estimation, shipping label generation, and logistics planning. Aligns with SAP material master weight data.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Material Master Weight; USDA Commodity Weight Standards; DOT Freight Weight Regulations

description: The timestamp when this bundle component association record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for audit trail, data lineage, and SOX financial reporting controls.
reference: SOX — Sarbanes-Oxley Act Section 404; GDPR Article 5 (Data Integrity); ISO 22000 Record Keeping

description: The date after which this component is no longer valid within the bundle. Null indicates an open-ended association with no planned expiry. Used for seasonal bundle management, promotional period control, and regulatory compliance (e.g., MRL threshold changes requiring bundle reformulation).
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM/SD — Validity Period; FDA FSMA Product Labeling; USDA NOP Organic Certification

description: The date from which this component is valid and active within the bundle. Supports seasonal agricultural product bundles (e.g., spring planting kits) and time-bound promotional bundles. Aligns with SAP validity period configuration.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM/SD — Validity Period; Granular Farm Management — Seasonal Planning

description: Indicates whether this component may be fulfilled separately from other bundle components (True) or must be shipped together with all other components in a single shipment (False). Supports split-shipment scenarios for agricultural bundles where seed and agrochemicals may ship from different warehouses.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD — Delivery Split; Manhattan Associates WMS — Order Splitting; USDA Shipping Requirements

description: Indicates the GMO status of this component within the bundle: gmo (contains genetically modified organisms), non_gmo (does not contain GMOs but not certified), gmo_free_certified (third-party certified non-GMO), or not_applicable (for non-biological components). Required for COOL labeling and USDA reporting.
reference: USDA APHIS Biotechnology Regulatory Services; FDA GMO Labeling; Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) Act; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Indicates whether this component is classified as a hazardous material requiring special handling, storage, and shipping documentation (e.g., certain agrochemicals, pesticides, or fertilizers). Triggers HAZMAT compliance workflows in logistics and warehouse operations.
reference: EPA FIFRA Hazardous Material Classification; DOT 49 CFR Hazardous Materials Regulations; OSHA SDS Requirements; SAP S/4HANA QM — Dangerous Goods

description: Indicates whether inventory for this component should be reserved at the component level upon bundle order placement (True) or managed at the bundle level only (False). Drives Manhattan Associates WMS inventory reservation logic for component-level stock allocation.
reference: Manhattan Associates WMS — Inventory Reservation; SAP S/4HANA MM — Reservation Management

description: The timestamp when this bundle component association record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change tracking, data synchronization with SAP S/4HANA and Oracle NetSuite, and audit compliance.
reference: SOX — Sarbanes-Oxley Act Section 404; SAP S/4HANA Change Document; GDPR Article 5

description: The procurement or production lead time in days for this component, used for bundle availability planning and supply chain scheduling. Critical for seasonal agricultural inputs where seed, fertilizer, and crop protection products must be available before planting windows.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Material Lead Time; Granular Farm Management — Supply Planning; FMIS Planning

description: Indicates whether this component is mandatory for the bundle to be valid and fulfillable. True = component must be present for bundle fulfillment; False = component is optional and may be excluded. Distinct from substitution_allowed_flag which governs product swaps rather than component inclusion.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — BOM Item Relevancy; Manhattan Associates WMS — Order Fulfillment Rules

description: The maximum quantity of this component that may be included in the bundle, applicable for variable-quantity bundles. Enforces upper limits for regulatory compliance (e.g., maximum agrochemical quantity per bundle per EPA/MRL restrictions) and inventory allocation controls.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD — Maximum Order Quantity; EPA MRL Compliance; FDA FSMA

description: The minimum quantity of this component that must be included in the bundle, applicable for variable-quantity bundles where customers may select quantities within a defined range (e.g., minimum 1 bag of seed per bundle). Used in order validation and fulfillment planning.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD — Minimum Order Quantity; Oracle NetSuite — Item Quantity Rules

description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, special handling instructions, or agronomic guidance specific to this component within the bundle context (e.g., 'Apply within 48 hours of seed treatment', 'Store separately from fertilizer', 'Requires cold chain handling'). Not for regulatory documentation.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM — Material Long Text; Granular Farm Management — Field Notes

description: Indicates whether this specific component within the bundle is certified organic under the USDA National Organic Program (NOP). Critical for maintaining bundle-level organic certification integrity — all mandatory components must be organic-certified for the bundle to carry an organic label.
reference: USDA National Organic Program (NOP) 7 CFR Part 205; GLOBALG.A.P. Organic Certification; ISO 22000

description: The monetary value attributed to this component within the overall bundle price, representing the component's share of the bundle's total selling price. Used for revenue allocation, cost-of-goods-sold (COGS) decomposition, and component-level profitability analysis.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD — Condition Pricing; Oracle NetSuite — Item Pricing; GAAP Revenue Allocation (ASC 606); IFRS 15

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the component pricing contribution amount (e.g., USD, EUR, CAD). Supports multi-currency agricultural commodity trading and international supply chain operations.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IFRS; GAAP

description: The percentage of the total bundle price attributable to this component, expressed as a decimal percentage (e.g., 35.50 for 35.5%). Used alongside the absolute pricing contribution amount for proportional revenue recognition and margin analysis per component.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD — Pricing Conditions; GAAP ASC 606 Performance Obligation Allocation; IFRS 15

description: Indicates whether the component quantity within the bundle is fixed (False) or variable/customer-selectable (True) within the min/max quantity bounds. Supports configurable agricultural input bundles where farmers select quantities based on acreage or herd size.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD — Configurable Product (Variant Configuration); Oracle NetSuite — Assembly Configuration

description: Indicates whether this component requires specific regulatory approval or certification before it can be included in a bundle for sale (e.g., EPA-registered pesticides, USDA-approved seed varieties, FDA-regulated food additives). Triggers compliance review workflows.
reference: EPA FIFRA Registration; USDA APHIS; FDA FSMA; GLOBALG.A.P. Certification Requirements

description: The display sort order for this component in customer-facing product catalogs, sales order entry screens, and bundle configuration interfaces. Distinct from component_sequence which governs fulfillment/picking order; sort_order governs presentation layer ordering.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD — Catalog Display; Salesforce CRM — Product Catalog Configuration; Oracle NetSuite — Item Display

description: Code identifying the storage compatibility class of this component, used to ensure incompatible components within a bundle are not co-located in warehouse storage (e.g., separating oxidizers from flammables, or keeping seed away from agrochemicals). Aligns with EPA and OSHA storage segregation requirements.
reference: EPA Storage and Disposal Requirements; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.106; SAP S/4HANA WM — Storage Type Indicator; Manhattan Associates WMS

description: Indicates whether this component may be substituted with an alternative product during order fulfillment when the primary component is out of stock or unavailable. True = substitution permitted; False = component is mandatory and cannot be substituted. Supports Manhattan Associates WMS substitution logic.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD — Material Substitution; Manhattan Associates WMS — Substitution Rules; GLOBALG.A.P. Product Specification

description: Unique system-generated identifier for each agricultural commodity record in the enterprise catalog. Serves as the primary key for the commodity reference table. Role: MASTER_RESOURCE.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module - Material Master

description: Reference to the applicable Maximum Residue Limit (MRL) threshold record for this commodity. MRL defines the maximum concentration of pesticide residues legally permitted in or on food and feed commodities per EPA and Codex Alimentarius standards.
reference: EPA Pesticide Tolerances (40 CFR Part 180); Codex Alimentarius MRL Database; EU Regulation 396/2005

description: Indicates whether this commodity is classified as a major food allergen under FDA regulations (e.g., wheat, soybeans, peanuts, tree nuts, milk, eggs, fish, shellfish, sesame). Triggers allergen labeling and cross-contact prevention requirements.
reference: FDA Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA) - 21 USC 343; FDA FSMA Preventive Controls for Human Food

description: Specific allergen classification when allergen_flag is True (e.g., 'gluten/wheat', 'soy', 'peanut', 'tree nut', 'milk', 'egg', 'fish', 'shellfish', 'sesame'). Required for FDA-compliant allergen labeling and HACCP allergen control plans.
reference: FDA Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA); FASTER Act of 2021 (sesame addition)

description: Secondary unit of measure used for conversion, international trade, or customer-specific reporting (e.g., MT as alternate to BU for export contracts). Supports dual-unit inventory management in SAP MM. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BU|CWT|MT|LB|KG|TON|BBL|GAL|DOZ|HEAD|OTHER — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module - Unit of Measure Conversion; ISO 80000-1

description: Reference benchmark price per standard unit of measure for this commodity, typically derived from the nearest futures contract or USDA AMS market report. Used for budget planning, contract pricing, and financial reporting. Expressed in USD.
reference: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) Market News; WASDE Report; CBOT/CME Futures Settlement Prices

description: High-level classification of the commodity by agricultural category. Drives domain-specific processing rules, storage requirements, and regulatory compliance workflows. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: grain|oilseed|fiber|produce|livestock|dairy|poultry|aquaculture|other — promote to reference product]
reference: USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) Commodity Classification

description: Externally-known enterprise code uniquely identifying the commodity across operational systems (SAP MM material number, Granular Farm Management commodity code). Used for cross-system reconciliation and procurement referencing.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module - Material Number

description: Human-readable name of the agricultural commodity (e.g., 'Yellow Corn No. 2', 'Hard Red Winter Wheat', 'Soybeans'). Used in reporting, labeling, and trade documentation.
reference: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) Commodity Standards

description: Current lifecycle status of the commodity record in the enterprise catalog. Active = currently traded/produced; Inactive = temporarily suspended; Discontinued = no longer produced or traded; Pending Approval = awaiting regulatory or internal approval for new commodity onboarding.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module - Material Status

description: Sub-classification within the commodity class providing finer granularity (e.g., 'cereal grain', 'legume', 'root vegetable', 'red meat', 'whole milk'). Supports product hierarchy analytics and USDA reporting segmentation.
reference: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) Commodity Classification

business_glossary_term: Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) Required Flag
description: Indicates whether Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) is mandatory for this commodity under USDA AMS regulations. True = COOL labeling required at retail (e.g., beef, pork, lamb, chicken, fish, fresh/frozen produce); False = exempt.
reference: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) - 7 CFR Part 65; Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946

description: Timestamp when this commodity record was first created in the enterprise data catalog. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and SOX financial reporting controls for master data governance.
reference: SOX Section 404 - Internal Controls over Financial Reporting; GDPR Article 5 - Data Integrity and Accountability

description: The marketing crop year associated with this commodity definition (e.g., 2024 for the 2024/25 marketing year). Used for WASDE alignment, USDA program eligibility, and seasonal price benchmarking. Follows USDA marketing year conventions by commodity.
reference: USDA World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates (WASDE); USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS)

description: Date from which this commodity record is valid and active in the enterprise catalog. Used for temporal data management, crop year transitions, and regulatory compliance period tracking.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module - Material Validity Period; USDA Program Eligibility Dates

description: Primary futures exchange where this commodity is traded (e.g., CBOT for grains, ICE for cotton and sugar). Determines which price feed and contract specifications apply for hedging and mark-to-market valuation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: CBOT|CME|ICE|NYMEX|KCBT|MGE|EURONEXT|OTHER — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT); CME Group; ICE Futures

description: Exchange ticker symbol for the commodity on futures markets (e.g., 'ZC' for CBOT Corn, 'ZS' for CBOT Soybeans, 'ZW' for CBOT Wheat, 'CT' for ICE Cotton). Used for market price benchmarking, hedging, and DTN/WASDE price feed integration.
reference: Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT); Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME); ICE Futures; DTN Market Data

description: Date on which this commodity record expires or is superseded in the enterprise catalog. Null indicates an open-ended active record. Used for catalog version management and regulatory compliance period end dates.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module - Material Validity Period

business_glossary_term: Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) Covered Commodity Flag
description: Indicates whether this commodity is subject to FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) requirements, including the Produce Safety Rule (21 CFR Part 112) or Preventive Controls for Human Food rule. Drives food safety plan and traceability requirements.
reference: FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) - 21 CFR Part 112 Produce Safety Rule; FDA FSMA Preventive Controls

description: Indicates whether the commodity is derived from genetically modified organisms (GMO), is non-GMO, or holds a certified GMO-free designation. Critical for labeling compliance (USDA National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard), export market access, and customer segregation requirements.
reference: USDA National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard (NBFDS); EU Regulation 1829/2003; Non-GMO Project Standard

business_glossary_term: Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) Category
description: HACCP food safety category classification for this commodity. Determines the applicable HACCP plan type and critical control point requirements for processing and handling. Aligns with GFSI, SQF, and BRC food safety management standards.
reference: Codex Alimentarius HACCP Guidelines (CAC/RCP 1-1969); FDA FSMA Preventive Controls; GFSI Benchmarking Requirements; SQF Code; BRC Global Standard for Food Safety

description: Harmonized System (HS) tariff classification code used for international trade documentation, customs declarations, import/export compliance, and duty rate determination. Typically 6–10 digits per WCO standard.
reference: World Customs Organization (WCO) Harmonized System Nomenclature; U.S. International Trade Commission (USITC) HTS Schedule

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this commodity record. Used for change data capture (CDC) in the Databricks Silver Layer pipeline, audit trail maintenance, and master data synchronization across SAP S/4HANA, Granular, and Climate FieldView.
reference: SOX Section 404; SAP S/4HANA MM Change Document; Databricks Delta Lake CDC

description: Maximum allowable moisture content percentage for this commodity at point of acceptance or storage. Exceeding this threshold triggers drying requirements or grade dockage. Critical for grain quality management per USDA GIPSA grading standards (e.g., corn ≤15.5%, soybeans ≤13%).
reference: USDA Grain Inspection, Packers and Stockyards Administration (GIPSA) Official Grain Standards; USDA AMS

description: Reference Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) baseline value for this commodity crop type at optimal growth stage, used for remote sensing yield estimation and crop health benchmarking in Climate FieldView and Esri ArcGIS analytics.
reference: NASA MODIS NDVI Product; Climate FieldView Analytics; Esri ArcGIS Remote Sensing Standards

description: USDA National Organic Program (NOP) classification for this commodity. Certified organic = fully compliant with 7 CFR Part 205; Transitional = in 3-year transition period; Conventional = standard production; Not applicable = non-crop commodity.
reference: USDA National Organic Program (NOP) - 7 CFR Part 205; USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS)

description: Indicates whether this commodity is eligible for organic certification under the USDA National Organic Program (NOP). True = eligible for organic production and labeling; False = not eligible (e.g., synthetic inputs required). Drives segregation requirements in storage and logistics.
reference: USDA National Organic Program (NOP) - 7 CFR Part 205

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code indicating the primary country of origin for this commodity (e.g., USA, BRA, ARG). Required for COOL compliance, import/export documentation, and country-of-origin risk assessment.
reference: ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3 Country Codes; USDA COOL Regulations (7 CFR Part 65); WTO Agreement on Rules of Origin

description: Indicates whether the commodity is perishable and requires temperature-controlled storage or expedited handling. True = perishable (e.g., fresh produce, dairy, eggs); False = non-perishable (e.g., dry grains, cotton). Drives warehouse task prioritization in Manhattan Associates WMS.
reference: FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) - Produce Safety Rule; USDA Perishable Agricultural Commodities Act (PACA)

description: Minimum number of days that must elapse between the last pesticide application and harvest for this commodity, as required by EPA label regulations. Ensures MRL compliance at point of harvest. Populated from agrochemical_product PHI data for the commodity's primary crop protection program.
reference: EPA Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA); EPA Pesticide Label Requirements (40 CFR Part 156)

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the benchmark_price (e.g., USD, EUR, BRL). Supports multi-currency operations for international commodity trading and export contracts.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; IFRS 21 Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates

description: Primary unit of measure used for trading, pricing, and inventory tracking of this commodity (e.g., BU = Bushel for grains, CWT = Hundredweight for livestock, MT = Metric Ton for export). Aligns with SAP MM base unit of measure and USDA reporting standards. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BU|CWT|MT|LB|KG|TON|BBL|GAL|DOZ|HEAD|OTHER — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS); SAP S/4HANA MM Unit of Measure Configuration; ISO 80000-1 Quantities and Units

description: Maximum allowable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for this commodity. Exceeding this threshold triggers quality alerts and may result in grade downgrade or rejection per USDA grading standards.
reference: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) Commodity Storage Standards; FDA FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule

description: Minimum allowable storage temperature in degrees Celsius for this commodity to maintain quality and safety. Used to configure cold chain requirements in warehouse management and transportation planning.
reference: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) Commodity Storage Standards; FDA FSMA Sanitary Transportation Rule

description: Minimum acceptable test weight in pounds per bushel for grade determination of this grain commodity (e.g., US No. 2 Yellow Corn = 54 lbs/bu). Used in USDA GIPSA official grading and price dockage calculations.
reference: USDA Grain Inspection, Packers and Stockyards Administration (GIPSA) Official Grain Standards of the United States

description: Reference average yield per acre for this commodity under standard production conditions, expressed in the standard_uom (e.g., 180 BU/acre for corn, 50 BU/acre for soybeans). Used as baseline for yield variance analysis, crop insurance, and USDA APH (Actual Production History) calculations.
reference: USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) Yield Surveys; USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA) APH

description: Numeric factor to convert from standard_uom to alternate_uom (e.g., 1 BU corn = 0.0254 MT; factor = 0.0254). Essential for export documentation, international invoicing, and cross-system inventory reconciliation.
reference: USDA Grain Inspection, Packers and Stockyards Administration (GIPSA) Weight and Measure Standards

business_glossary_term: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Commodity Code
description: Official USDA commodity code assigned by the Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) or Farm Service Agency (FSA). Required for USDA program participation, federal reporting, and commodity loan eligibility determination.
reference: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS); USDA Farm Service Agency (FSA) Commodity Codes

business_glossary_term: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Grade Standard
description: Reference to the applicable USDA grade standard designation for this commodity (e.g., 'US No. 1', 'US No. 2', 'US Extra Fancy', 'USDA Choice'). Determines quality thresholds, price premiums/discounts, and market eligibility. Linked to grading_standard reference product.
reference: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) Grade Standards; USDA GIPSA Official Grain Standards

business_glossary_term: Commodity Broker Authorization - Commodity Broker Authorization Id
description: Primary key for the commodity_broker_authorization association
reference: Internal - M:N Association PK

description: Foreign key linking to the broker master record who holds this commodity authorization. Identifies which broker entity is authorized to sell the associated commodity.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: Foreign key linking to the agricultural commodity that the broker is authorized to facilitate. Identifies which specific commodity (e.g., Yellow Corn No. 2, Hard Red Winter Wheat) is covered by this authorization.
reference: Internal - M:N Association FK

description: Current lifecycle status of this broker-commodity authorization. Controls whether the broker is currently permitted to facilitate sales of this commodity. Managed independently of the broker's overall relationship_status.

Commission rate expressed as a percentage of net sales order value applicable specifically to this broker-commodity combination. Overrides the broker master's standard commission_rate_pct when a commodity-specific rate has been negotiated. Belongs to the authorization, not to either master entity, because the same broker may have different rates for corn vs. soybeans.
reference: ISO 4217 currency context applies via broker.commission_currency_code

description: Comma-separated list of agricultural commodity types the broker is authorized and experienced to transact (e.g., corn, soybeans, wheat, cattle, hogs, fresh produce). Used for opportunity matching and compliance with USDA commodity-specific licensing requirements. [Moved from broker: This is a denormalized multi-value string field encoding the M:N broker-commodity relationship directly on the broker master record. Once the commodity_broker_authorization association is in place, each authorized commodity is represented as a proper row in the association table. The commodity_specializations field should be deprecated and removed from the broker master to eliminate the data integrity risk of a free-text multi-value field diverging from the structured authorization records.]
reference: USDA AMS Commodity Licensing; WASDE Commodity Classifications; GLOBALG.A.P. Commodity Scope

description: Date on which this broker-commodity authorization becomes legally effective and the broker is permitted to facilitate sales of this commodity. Enables time-bounded authorization management — a broker may be authorized for corn starting in one crop year and wheat in another.
reference: ISO 8601 date format

description: Indicates whether this broker holds exclusive rights to facilitate sales of this specific commodity within their geographic territory. Commodity-level exclusivity is distinct from broker.exclusivity_flag which is a general indicator — a broker may be exclusive for soybeans but non-exclusive for corn.

Date on which this broker-commodity authorization expires or is terminated. Null indicates an open-ended authorization. Enables the enterprise to manage time-limited commodity authorizations independently of the broker's overall contract dates.
reference: ISO 8601 date format

description: Agreed annual commodity volume target in Metric Tons that the broker is expected to facilitate for this specific commodity under this authorization. Distinct from broker.annual_volume_target_mt which is an aggregate across all commodities. Belongs to the authorization because targets are negotiated per commodity.
reference: Unit: Metric Tons (MT)

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each node in the product hierarchy. Primary key for the product_hierarchy data product in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM/SD Product Hierarchy (PRODH)

description: Self-referencing identifier pointing to the immediate parent node in the product hierarchy tree. Null for root-level Division nodes. Enables recursive traversal for roll-up reporting across crop commodities, livestock products, and processed goods.
reference: SAP S/4HANA Product Hierarchy parent-child structure

description: Broad commodity grouping for this hierarchy node aligned with USDA and market reporting conventions. Examples: Grains & Oilseeds, Fruits & Vegetables, Dairy, Poultry & Eggs, Meat & Livestock, Fiber Crops, Specialty Crops, Crop Inputs. Used in WASDE reporting and market price benchmarking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: Grains & Oilseeds|Fruits & Vegetables|Dairy|Poultry & Eggs|Meat & Livestock|Fiber Crops|Specialty Crops|Crop Inputs — promote to reference product]
reference: USDA WASDE (World Agricultural Supply and Demand Estimates); USDA NASS commodity groups

business_glossary_term: Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) Required Flag
description: Indicates whether Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) is mandatory for products in this hierarchy node under USDA AMS regulations. True = COOL labeling required on all products in this node; False = COOL not required. Drives labeling compliance workflows and retail packaging requirements.
reference: USDA Agricultural Marketing Act; COOL (Country of Origin Labeling) 7 CFR Part 60 and 65

description: Timestamp when this product hierarchy node record was first created in the system. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and Silver Layer ingestion tracking. Format: yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: ISO 8601 timestamp standard; SOX audit trail requirements; GDPR Article 5 (data integrity)

description: Name or identifier of the business data steward responsible for maintaining the accuracy and completeness of this hierarchy node. Supports data governance accountability, change management workflows, and master data management (MDM) ownership tracking.
reference: Internal data governance policy; DAMA DMBOK data stewardship framework

description: SAP S/4HANA Sales Division code associated with this hierarchy node. Drives pricing, sales organization assignment, and profit center determination. Examples: CROP (Crop Commodities), LVST (Livestock Products), PROC (Processed Goods), SEED (Seed & Inputs), VADD (Value-Added Products).
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Sales Division (SPART); USDA Agricultural Marketing Service

description: Date from which this product hierarchy node is valid and active for product classification. Supports temporal hierarchy management and ensures historical accuracy when hierarchy structures change. Used in SAP S/4HANA time-dependent product hierarchy configurations.
reference: SAP S/4HANA time-dependent product hierarchy; ISO 8601 date standard

description: Date after which this product hierarchy node is no longer valid for new product assignments. Null indicates an open-ended, currently active node. Supports hierarchy versioning and ensures products are not assigned to expired classification nodes.
reference: SAP S/4HANA time-dependent product hierarchy; ISO 8601 date standard

description: Cross-reference code mapping this hierarchy node to an external classification system such as UNSPSC (United Nations Standard Products and Services Code), HS (Harmonized System) tariff code, or trading partner category code. Supports EDI, customs documentation, and global trade compliance.
reference: UN/SPSC commodity classification; World Customs Organization Harmonized System (HS); GS1

value_regex: Ready-to-Eat|Raw Agricultural Commodity|Processed Food|Animal Feed|Non-Food|Crop Input
description: FDA/USDA food safety classification for products in this hierarchy node. Determines applicable food safety regulations, inspection requirements, and labeling rules. Ready-to-Eat products require stricter controls than Raw Agricultural Commodities. Non-Food and Crop Input nodes are exempt from food safety rules.
reference: FDA 21 CFR food safety classifications; USDA FSIS product categories; FSMA Preventive Controls rule

business_glossary_term: Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) Regulatory Category
value_regex: Produce Safety Rule|Preventive Controls Human Food|Preventive Controls Animal Food|Foreign Supplier Verification|Not Applicable
description: FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) regulatory category applicable to products in this hierarchy node. Determines which FSMA rules govern production, handling, and supply chain requirements. Drives compliance program assignment and audit scope.
reference: FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA); 21 CFR Parts 112, 117, 507; FDA FSVP

business_glossary_term: Global Food Safety Initiative (GFSI) Certification Scheme
description: Primary Global Food Safety Initiative (GFSI)-recognized certification scheme applicable to products in this hierarchy node. Drives supplier qualification, audit requirements, and customer contract compliance. Values: SQF (Safe Quality Food), BRC (British Retail Consortium), IFS (International Featured Standards), GLOBALG.A.P., Not Applicable.
reference: Global Food Safety Initiative (GFSI) benchmarking requirements; SQF Institute; BRC Global Standards; IFS; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Indicates the Genetically Modified Organism (GMO) status applicable to products in this hierarchy node. Values: GMO (contains genetically modified material), Non-GMO (no GMO material, not certified), GMO-Free Certified (third-party verified non-GMO), Not Applicable (e.g., agrochemicals). Required for COOL labeling, USDA BE (Bioengineered) disclosure, and export documentation.
reference: USDA National Bioengineered Food Disclosure Standard (7 CFR Part 66); COOL (Country of Origin Labeling); Non-GMO Project Standard

business_glossary_term: GS1 Global Product Classification (GPC) Brick Code
description: GS1 Global Product Classification (GPC) Brick-level code for this hierarchy node. Enables standardized product categorization for retail trading partners, EDI transactions, and global supply chain interoperability. Particularly relevant for produce, dairy, and packaged goods nodes.
reference: GS1 Global Product Classification (GPC) standard; GS1 US

description: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) grading standard code applicable to products in this hierarchy node (e.g., US No. 1, US Grade A, USDA Choice). Governs quality grading, inspection requirements, and grade-based pricing. Used in SAP QM quality inspection and COA documentation.
reference: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) grading standards; 7 CFR grading regulations

business_glossary_term: Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) Applicable Flag
description: Indicates whether Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points (HACCP) plans are required for products in this hierarchy node. True = HACCP plan mandatory (e.g., meat, poultry, juice, seafood); False = HACCP not required. Drives food safety program assignment and FSIS/FDA audit requirements.
reference: USDA FSIS HACCP regulations (9 CFR Part 417); FDA 21 CFR Part 120; Codex Alimentarius HACCP guidelines

description: Indicates whether products in this hierarchy node are classified as hazardous materials requiring special handling, storage, and transportation documentation (e.g., certain agrochemicals, fertilizers). True = HAZMAT classification applies; False = standard handling. Drives SDS (Safety Data Sheet) requirements and DOT/EPA compliance.
reference: EPA hazardous materials regulations; DOT 49 CFR hazmat transportation; OSHA Hazard Communication Standard (29 CFR 1910.1200)

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this hierarchy node. Corresponds to the SAP S/4HANA PRODH (Product Hierarchy) field used in SD pricing and MM material classification. Used for cross-system integration with SAP, Oracle NetSuite, and Granular Farm Management.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD/MM Product Hierarchy (PRODH); USDA Agricultural Marketing Service commodity codes

description: Detailed business description of this hierarchy node, including the scope of products it encompasses, applicable production methods, and any relevant regulatory or quality notes. Used in training materials, data catalogs, and business user documentation.
reference: Internal data governance standards; SAP S/4HANA Product Hierarchy text

description: Numeric depth of this node within the hierarchy tree. Level 1 = Division (e.g., Crop Commodities), Level 2 = Category (e.g., Grains), Level 3 = Sub-Category (e.g., Cereal Grains), Level 4 = Product Family (e.g., Corn), Level 5 = SKU/Item. description: Name of the seed company, research institution, or individual breeder that developed and holds intellectual property rights over this variety (e.g., 'Bayer Crop Science', 'Corteva Agriscience', 'Syngenta'). Required for licensing compliance and royalty tracking.
reference: USDA Plant Variety Protection (PVP) Act; International Union for the Protection of New Varieties of Plants (UPOV)

description: The crop year (4-digit year) for which this seed variety is listed in the commercial product catalog. Used for annual catalog management, variety retirement tracking, and historical performance analysis in Granular Farm Management and Climate FieldView.
reference: Granular Farm Management Catalog Management; Climate FieldView Variety Database; Internal Product Lifecycle Policy

description: Timestamp when this seed variety record was first created in the master catalog system. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and Silver Layer ingestion tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.
reference: ISO 8601 Timestamp Standard; Internal Data Governance Audit Policy; SOX Compliance (Record Creation Audit)

description: Botanical species name of the crop (e.g., 'Zea mays' for corn, 'Glycine max' for soybean, 'Triticum aestivum' for wheat). Aligns with USDA PLANTS Database taxonomy and supports regulatory reporting to APHIS and EPA.
reference: USDA PLANTS Database; APHIS Biotechnology Regulatory Services; Codex Alimentarius Commission

description: High-level agronomic classification of the crop category. Used for product hierarchy segmentation, supply chain routing, and USDA commodity code alignment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: grain|oilseed|fiber|forage|vegetable|fruit|pulse|tuber|specialty|cover_crop — promote to reference product]
reference: USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) Crop Classification; USDA Agricultural Marketing Service

description: Average number of calendar days from planting to physiological maturity under typical growing conditions for the primary production region. Used for crop scheduling, harvest planning, and frost risk assessment in Climate FieldView and Granular Farm Management.
reference: USDA NASS Crop Progress Reports; Climate FieldView Variety Performance Data; Trimble Ag Software Crop Calendar

description: Date on which this seed variety was officially discontinued from commercial sale or production. Null if the variety is still active. Used for catalog management, inventory clearance planning, and historical crop planning records.
reference: Internal Product Lifecycle Policy; Granular Farm Management; SAP S/4HANA MM Material Lifecycle

description: Structured description of the variety's resistance or tolerance ratings to key crop diseases (e.g., 'Gray Leaf Spot: R, Northern Corn Leaf Blight: MR, Goss's Wilt: S'). Ratings typically follow industry conventions: R=Resistant, MR=Moderately Resistant, MS=Moderately Susceptible, S=Susceptible. Informs crop protection planning and IPM programs.
reference: USDA ARS Plant Disease Resistance Database; Crop Protection Network Disease Rating Standards; IPM Guidelines

description: Categorical rating of the variety's ability to maintain yield under water-deficit stress conditions. Used for irrigation planning, water resource management, and ET (Evapotranspiration)-based irrigation scheduling in precision agriculture systems.
reference: USDA ARS Drought Tolerance Research; Climate FieldView Variety Analytics; Trimble Ag Software Agronomic Ratings

description: Minimum guaranteed germination rate percentage for this seed variety as tested under AOSA (Association of Official Seed Analysts) standard germination test conditions. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 95.00 = 95%). Required for Federal Seed Act label compliance and quality assurance.
reference: Federal Seed Act (7 U.S.C. § 1551); Association of Official Seed Analysts (AOSA) Rules for Testing Seeds; USDA AMS Seed Regulatory Program

description: Indicates whether the seed variety contains genetically modified traits as defined by USDA APHIS and FDA regulations. 'gmo' = contains approved biotech traits; 'non_gmo' = verified non-GMO (e.g., Non-GMO Project Verified); 'conventional' = traditionally bred, no biotech traits; 'under_evaluation' = APHIS regulatory review in progress. Critical for COOL labeling, customer segregation, and export compliance.
reference: USDA APHIS Biotechnology Regulatory Services (BRS); FDA Coordinated Framework for Regulation of Biotechnology; Non-GMO Project Standard; COOL (Country of Origin Labeling) Regulations

description: Comma-separated list of herbicide tolerance traits present in this variety (e.g., 'glyphosate, glufosinate, dicamba'). Used for agrochemical selection, VRA prescription compatibility, and EPA resistance management compliance. Supports IPM resistance group tracking.
reference: EPA Pesticide Registration; Weed Science Society of America (WSSA) Herbicide Resistance Classification; IPM Guidelines

description: Comma-separated list of insect resistance traits (e.g., 'Bt Cry1Ab, Cry3Bb1, VIP3A') present in this variety. Used for EPA insect resistance management (IRM) compliance, refuge planning, and IPM program design. Required for APHIS regulatory documentation on Bt crops.
reference: EPA Insect Resistance Management (IRM) Policy; USDA APHIS BRS; Entomological Society of America IRM Guidelines

description: Date on which this seed variety was first commercially introduced to the market or added to the internal product catalog. Used for variety lifecycle management, performance trend analysis, and regulatory documentation.
reference: USDA Plant Variety Protection Office; Internal Product Lifecycle Policy; Granular Farm Management

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this seed variety record in the master catalog. Used for change tracking, data freshness monitoring, and incremental ETL processing in the Databricks Lakehouse Silver Layer.
reference: ISO 8601 Timestamp Standard; Internal Data Governance Audit Policy; SOX Compliance (Record Modification Audit)

description: Unique identifier for the seed licensor or technology provider as registered in the ERP procurement master. Used to link seed variety to licensing agreements, royalty schedules, and supplier records in SAP S/4HANA MM.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Vendor Master; USDA Plant Variety Protection Office

description: Indicates whether this seed variety has received third-party non-GMO verification (e.g., Non-GMO Project Verified, USDA Process Verified Program). Distinct from NOP organic eligibility — a variety can be non-GMO verified without being organically produced. Supports customer segregation and premium market positioning.
reference: Non-GMO Project Standard; USDA Process Verified Program (PVP); FDA Voluntary Labeling Guidance for Bioengineered Foods

business_glossary_term: National Organic Program (NOP) Organic Seed Eligibility Flag
description: Indicates whether this seed variety is eligible for use in USDA National Organic Program (NOP) certified organic production. True = organically produced seed available and eligible; False = not eligible (e.g., treated with prohibited substances or GMO). Drives organic crop planning and NOP compliance documentation.
reference: USDA National Organic Program (NOP); 7 CFR Part 205 Organic Regulations; GLOBALG.A.P. Organic Standard

description: Net weight of the standard commercial seed package in kilograms. Used for freight calculation, warehouse storage planning, and logistics management in Manhattan Associates WMS and TMS (Transportation Management System).
reference: Manhattan Associates WMS Item Master; SAP S/4HANA MM Material Master; USDA AMS Seed Labeling Requirements

description: Categorical classification of the variety's typical plant height at maturity. Used for equipment calibration (combine header height), lodging risk assessment, and field operation planning in John Deere Operations Center.
reference: Crop Science Society of America Variety Description Standards; John Deere Operations Center Field Data

description: USDA Plant Variety Protection Office certificate number assigned to this variety, granting intellectual property protection to the breeder. Null if the variety is not PVP-protected or is in the public domain. Required for licensing compliance and royalty management.
reference: USDA Plant Variety Protection Act (7 U.S.C. § 2321); UPOV Convention

description: Percentage of pure seed (by weight) of the labeled variety in the seed lot, as determined by official seed analysis. Required for Federal Seed Act label compliance. Expressed as a percentage (e.g., 99.50 = 99.5% pure seed).
reference: Federal Seed Act (7 U.S.C. § 1551); AOSA Rules for Testing Seeds; USDA AMS Seed Regulatory Program

description: Comma-separated list of geographic regions, states, or USDA Plant Hardiness Zones where this variety is agronomically recommended for commercial production (e.g., 'Corn Belt, Northern Plains, Zone 5-7'). Supports geographic segmentation in Esri ArcGIS field mapping and regional sales planning.
reference: USDA Plant Hardiness Zone Map; USDA AMS Regional Variety Trial Data; Trimble Ag Software Regional Recommendations

description: Numeric relative maturity rating indicating the number of days or heat units required for the variety to reach physiological maturity relative to a standard check variety (e.g., 108.5 for a 108.5-day corn hybrid, 3.8 for a 3.8 maturity group soybean). Critical for crop planning, planting date optimization, and frost risk management in Climate FieldView and Trimble Ag Software.
reference: USDA AMS Seed Variety Performance Trials; North American Soybean Maturity Group Classification; Corn Belt Relative Maturity Standards

description: Official seed certification class indicating the generation and purity level of the seed as defined by the Association of Official Seed Certifying Agencies (AOSCA). Classes: 'breeder' (source seed from originating breeder), 'foundation' (first generation from breeder seed), 'registered' (second generation), 'certified' (commercially distributed certified seed), 'commercial' (uncertified commercial seed).
reference: Association of Official Seed Certifying Agencies (AOSCA) Seed Certification Standards; USDA AMS Federal Seed Act

description: Physical size classification of the seed kernel used for planter plate selection, seeding equipment calibration, and seed unit weight calculations. Affects planter population accuracy and is required for John Deere Operations Center equipment setup.
reference: John Deere Operations Center Planter Configuration; AOSA Seed Testing Standards; Equipment Calibration SOPs

description: Comma-separated list of active ingredients (AI) in the seed treatment formulation (e.g., 'clothianidin, metalaxyl, fludioxonil'). Required for MRL compliance, EPA registration cross-reference, and FSMA produce safety rule documentation.
reference: EPA Active Ingredient Registry; USDA FSMA Produce Safety Rule; Codex Alimentarius MRL Standards

description: Name or code of the seed treatment product(s) applied to the seed lot prior to sale or planting (e.g., 'Poncho 1250 + Acceleron', 'Cruiser Maxx Vibrance'). Includes fungicide, insecticide, and biological seed treatments. Required for EPA label compliance, PHI/REI tracking, and NOP organic eligibility determination.
reference: EPA Pesticide Registration (FIFRA); USDA NOP 7 CFR Part 205.204 (Seed Treatment Restrictions); SDS (Safety Data Sheet) Requirements

description: Manufacturer or agronomist-recommended seeding rate expressed as seeds per acre for optimal stand establishment. Used for VRA (Variable Rate Application) prescription generation in Trimble Ag Software and seed quantity planning in Granular Farm Management.
reference: Trimble Ag Software VRA Prescription Standards; Climate FieldView Planting Recommendations; USDA Extension Agronomic Guidelines

description: Number of seeds per standard commercial unit (e.g., seeds per 80,000-count bag for corn, seeds per 140,000-count bag for soybean). Used for inventory management, seeding rate calculations, and order quantity planning in SAP S/4HANA MM and Manhattan Associates WMS.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Unit of Measure Configuration; Manhattan Associates WMS Item Master; USDA AMS Seed Labeling

description: Descriptive label of the bundled biotechnology or conventionally bred trait stack applied to this variety (e.g., 'RoundupReady2Xtend + Bollgard3', 'Enlist E3', 'LibertyLink GT27'). Captures herbicide tolerance, insect resistance, drought tolerance, and other engineered or selected traits. Used for IPM planning, agrochemical compatibility, and regulatory reporting.
reference: USDA APHIS BRS Trait Registry; EPA Pesticide Registration (for Bt traits); Integrated Pest Management (IPM) Framework

description: Internally assigned alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the seed variety in ERP and FMIS systems (e.g., SAP S/4HANA material master number or Trimble Ag Software variety code). Used as the business key for cross-system integration and SKU linkage.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Module Material Master; Trimble Ag Software Variety Database

description: Commercial or proprietary name of the seed variety as registered by the breeder or licensor (e.g., 'DeKalb DKC62-08', 'Pioneer P1197AM'). This is the primary human-readable identifier used in field operations, procurement, and sales.
reference: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) Variety Registration; GLOBALG.A.P. Seed Traceability Standard

description: Current lifecycle status of the seed variety in the product catalog. 'active' indicates commercially available; 'discontinued' indicates no longer sold or planted; 'under_review' indicates pending regulatory or internal evaluation; 'pending_approval' indicates awaiting APHIS or NOP certification; 'withdrawn' indicates removed due to regulatory or quality issues.
reference: APHIS Biotechnology Regulatory Services; USDA National Organic Program (NOP); Internal Product Lifecycle Policy

description: Categorical rating of the variety's yield potential relative to comparable varieties in the same crop class and maturity group, as determined by multi-environment trial (MET) data. Used for variety selection, agronomic planning, and YPM (Yield Per Acre Metric) benchmarking in Granular Farm Management.
reference: USDA NASS Variety Performance Trials; Association of Official Seed Certifying Agencies (AOSCA); Climate FieldView Variety Analytics

description: Unique system-generated identifier for the product substitution rule record. Primary key for the substitution_rule data product in the SAP S/4HANA MM material substitution configuration context.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Substitution

description: Reference to the SAP S/4HANA plant (production facility, grain elevator, processing plant, or distribution center) where this substitution rule is applicable. Null indicates the rule applies enterprise-wide across all plants.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Organizational Structure

description: Reference to the primary agricultural product or commodity (e.g., grain, produce, livestock product, seed input) that is subject to substitution when unavailable or constrained. Links to product.product_master.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; USDA Commodity Classification

description: Reference to the approved substitute agricultural product or commodity that can replace the primary product in order fulfillment, procurement, or feed formulation scenarios. Links to product.product_master.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; USDA Commodity Classification

description: Reference to the SAP S/4HANA sales organization for which this substitution rule is valid in order fulfillment scenarios. Null indicates applicability across all sales organizations.
reference: SAP S/4HANA SD Organizational Structure

description: Name or role of the business authority (e.g., Procurement Manager, Quality Assurance Director, Feed Nutritionist) who approved this substitution rule. Supports audit trail and regulatory compliance documentation.
reference: USDA; FDA; GLOBALG.A.P.; ISO 22000

description: Date on which the substitution rule was formally approved by the designated approval authority. Required for regulatory audit trails under FSMA and GLOBALG.A.P. compliance frameworks.
reference: FSMA; GLOBALG.A.P.; ISO 22000; USDA

description: Indicates whether the system (SAP S/4HANA MM) may automatically apply this substitution rule without manual intervention when the trigger condition is met. False requires a planner or procurement officer to manually confirm the substitution.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Substitution

description: Indicates whether a Certificate of Analysis (COA) must accompany the substitute product shipment to validate quality equivalency with the primary product. Supports GFSI, SQF, and BRC compliance requirements.
reference: GFSI; SQF; BRC Global Standards; ISO 22000

business_glossary_term: Country of Origin Labeling (COOL) Country Code
description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code indicating the country of origin of the substitute product for COOL (Country of Origin Labeling) compliance. May differ from the primary product's origin and must be disclosed to customers and on product labels.
reference: USDA COOL (Country of Origin Labeling); AMS; FSMA

description: Timestamp when this substitution rule record was first created in the system. Provides audit trail for data governance and regulatory compliance documentation.
reference: ISO 22000; FSMA; SOX; GDPR

description: Indicates whether explicit customer approval must be obtained before applying this substitution in a sales order fulfillment context. True requires customer confirmation; False allows automatic substitution. Relevant for COOL and customer contract compliance.
reference: COOL (Country of Origin Labeling); FSMA; Salesforce CRM

description: Identifies a specific customer segment or customer group (e.g., food manufacturers, retail chains, export accounts) for which this substitution rule is restricted. Null means the rule applies to all customers. Aligns with Salesforce CRM customer segmentation.
reference: Salesforce CRM; SAP S/4HANA SD

description: Calendar date from which this substitution rule becomes valid and may be applied in order fulfillment, procurement, or feed formulation. Aligns with SAP S/4HANA MM validity start date for material substitution.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Calendar date after which this substitution rule is no longer valid. Null indicates an open-ended rule with no planned expiration. Used to manage seasonal and emergency substitution windows.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; GLOBALG.A.P.

business_glossary_term: Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) Traceability Required Flag
description: Indicates whether this substitution triggers additional traceability documentation requirements under the FDA Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) Food Traceability Rule (Section 204). True requires lot-level tracking and Key Data Elements (KDEs) to be captured.
reference: FDA FSMA Food Traceability Rule (Section 204); ISO 22000

description: Indicates whether the substitution maintains compliance with Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) standards for both the primary and substitute products. Required for GLOBALG.A.P. certification maintenance and USDA GAP audit readiness.
reference: GLOBALG.A.P.; USDA GAP/GHP Audit Program

description: Indicates whether the substitute product meets the same USDA grading standard as the primary product (True = grade-equivalent substitution). Used in quality assurance workflows and COA documentation to confirm substitution does not downgrade product quality.
reference: USDA Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) Grading Standards; ISO 22000

description: Date on which this substitution rule was most recently reviewed and confirmed by the approval authority. Used to trigger review reminders and compliance audit checks.
reference: GLOBALG.A.P.; ISO 22000; FSMA

description: Timestamp when this substitution rule record was most recently modified. Supports change management, audit trail, and data lineage tracking in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: ISO 22000; FSMA; SOX; GDPR

description: Maximum quantity of the substitute product (in the defined unit of measure) that may be applied under this rule per order or procurement event. Prevents over-substitution and supports supply chain planning constraints.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; Granular Farm Management

description: Indicates whether the substitute product meets the same Maximum Residue Limit (MRL) thresholds as the primary product for pesticide and agrochemical residues. Required for food safety compliance under FDA, EPA, and Codex Alimentarius standards.
reference: FDA; EPA; Codex Alimentarius Commission; FSMA

description: Indicates whether the substitute product maintains the same non-GMO (Genetically Modified Organism) status as the primary product. Critical for non-GMO product lines and customer labeling commitments under USDA BE (Bioengineered) disclosure rules.
reference: USDA Bioengineered (BE) Disclosure Standard; GLOBALG.A.P.; Non-GMO Project

description: Indicates whether the substitute product maintains the same organic certification status as the primary product under USDA National Organic Program (NOP). True means both products are NOP-certified organic; False means organic status differs and substitution may affect labeling.
reference: USDA National Organic Program (NOP); GLOBALG.A.P.

description: Percentage difference in standard cost between the substitute product and the primary product (positive = substitute is more expensive, negative = substitute is cheaper). Used in procurement cost impact analysis and COGS (Cost of Goods Sold) variance reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA CO; GAAP; IFRS

description: Numeric ranking (1 = highest priority) used to sequence multiple approved substitutes for the same primary product. Determines which substitute is selected first when multiple substitution rules are active simultaneously in SAP S/4HANA MM.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Substitution

description: Numeric multiplier applied to the primary product quantity to determine the equivalent substitute quantity (e.g., 1.05 means 5% more substitute is needed per unit of primary). Accounts for grade equivalency differences in weight, volume, or nutritional value.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; USDA Commodity Standards; NOP

description: Indicates whether this substitution is subject to regulatory restrictions (e.g., USDA, FDA, EPA, APHIS import/export controls, or state-level agricultural regulations) that limit when or where the substitute product may be used.
reference: USDA; FDA; EPA; APHIS; Codex Alimentarius Commission

description: Number of days between mandatory periodic reviews of this substitution rule to confirm continued validity, regulatory compliance, and business relevance. Supports governance and GLOBALG.A.P. continuous improvement requirements.
reference: GLOBALG.A.P.; ISO 22000; Internal SOP

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this substitution rule, used in SAP S/4HANA MM material substitution configuration and cross-referenced in procurement and order fulfillment workflows.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Substitution

description: Current lifecycle state of the substitution rule governing whether it may be applied in fulfillment or procurement operations. Active rules are eligible for automatic or manual substitution; suspended rules require review before use.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; Internal SOP

description: Free-text business justification describing why this substitution rule was established (e.g., 'Corn No. 2 Yellow substituted for Corn No. 1 Yellow during Q4 harvest shortfall; grade equivalency confirmed by QA'). Supports audit documentation and supply chain resilience planning.
reference: USDA; FSMA; ISO 22000; Internal SOP

description: Business process context in which this substitution rule is applicable: order_fulfillment (sales order dispatch), procurement (purchase order sourcing), feed_formulation (livestock nutrition ingredient swap), or all (unrestricted across all processes).
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; Manhattan Associates WMS; FSMA

description: Categorical classification of the substitution relationship: equivalent_grade (same quality tier, different lot/source), approved_alternative (customer or regulatory pre-approved swap), emergency (supply disruption-driven), seasonal (crop availability-driven), feed_formulation (ingredient swap in livestock nutrition plans). Drives workflow routing in SAP S/4HANA MM.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM Material Substitution; GLOBALG.A.P.; FSMA

description: Business condition that activates this substitution rule: stock_shortage (inventory below reorder point), seasonal_unavailability (crop not in season), quality_hold (primary product under quarantine), supplier_disruption (vendor supply failure), price_threshold (cost exceeds approved ceiling). Drives automated substitution logic in SAP S/4HANA MM.
reference: SAP S/4HANA MM; Manhattan Associates WMS; FSMA

description: Standard unit of measure applicable to the quantity conversion factor for this substitution rule. Uses agricultural industry standard units: BU (Bushel), MT (Metric Ton), CWT (Hundredweight), KG, LB, L (Litre), GAL (Gallon), EA (Each). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: BU|MT|CWT|KG|LB|L|GAL|EA — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: USDA Commodity Standards; SAP S/4HANA MM

reference: EPA Pesticide Label

description: Total planned cost of production for the entire budgeted area, aggregating all cost line items (seed, fertilizer NPK, crop protection, labor, equipment, irrigation, land rent, crop insurance, custom hire). Used for COGS allocation, break-even analysis, and EBITDA reporting.
reference: GAAP ASC 330; IFRS IAS 2; SAP S/4HANA CO Module; Granular Farm Management

reference: GAAP ASC 606; IFRS IFRS 15; SAP S/4HANA CO/FI Module; SOX Section 302

description: Expected crop yield per hectare (ha) used as the basis for revenue projections in this enterprise budget. Expressed in the commodity's standard unit of measure (e.g., MT/ha for grains, BU/ha for corn). Derived from historical yield records, NDVI analysis, and agronomic models.

reference: Internal - LLM Generated Cross-Domain Link

description: Current lifecycle status of the fixed asset. description: Date the asset was formally capitalized on the balance sheet and depreciation commenced. May differ from acquisition_date for assets under construction (AUC) that are transferred to productive use upon completion.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; GAAP ASC 360; IFRS IAS 16

description: Timestamp when the fixed asset record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail requirements under SOX Section 404 and GAAP/IFRS asset accounting controls.

reference: ISO 4217; IFRS IAS 21; GAAP ASC 830

description: SAP FI-AA depreciation area indicating the accounting framework for which this depreciation record applies. 'book' = GAAP book depreciation; 'tax' = US federal tax (MACRS); 'ifrs' = IFRS IAS 16 reporting; 'state_tax' = state-level tax depreciation; 'group' = consolidated group reporting.
reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA Depreciation Areas; GAAP ASC 360; IFRS IAS 16; IRS Publication 946

description: Depreciation calculation method applied to this asset. 'straight_line' = GAAP book depreciation; 'macrs' = Modified Accelerated Cost Recovery System for US federal tax; 'declining_balance' = accelerated book method; 'units_of_production' = usage-based for farm equipment; 'section_179' = immediate expensing election for qualifying farm equipment under IRS Section 179.

description: Reason code for asset disposal. Used for asset lifecycle analytics, replacement planning, and CAPEX justification. reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; GAAP ASC 360; IFRS IAS 16

description: Cumulative impairment loss recognized on this asset where the carrying amount exceeds the recoverable amount. Triggered by events such as crop failure, flood damage to irrigation infrastructure, or obsolescence of precision agriculture technology. Recorded per GAAP ASC 360 / IFRS IAS 36.
reference: GAAP ASC 360; IFRS IAS 36 Impairment of Assets; SAP S/4HANA FI-AA

reference: SAP S/4HANA FI-AA; GAAP ASC 360; SOX Section 302/404

description: Date of the most recently completed periodic depreciation run for this asset. Used to confirm depreciation is current and to identify assets that may have missed a depreciation posting cycle. Sourced from SAP FI-AA depreciation run history.

reference: GAAP ASC 360; IFRS IAS 16; IRS Publication 946
